title: Concrete bus dispatch: Williams (Joust, Robotron, Sinistar)
description:
Convert the Williams 2nd-gen board (M6809 + M6800 sound + blitter) per docs/designs/concrete-bus-dispatch.md. Blocked by the generic Cpu::reset task (the M6809 fetches its reset vector through the bus).

This is the second-bus-master case: the blitter drives the bus as BusMaster::Dma/DmaVram from inside the board, so it re-enters through &mut self and needs no split -- but DmaVram deliberately bypasses banking, so keep the two masters distinguishable through any read-path refactor. Measure joust before/after; run golden frames.
notes: Also do the scanline-outer / cycle-inner inversion here. williams.rs:465 was the third site listed in concrete-bus-dispatch-blzz.5; the Namco boards were inverted in 2b1667f and Williams was left out because it still dispatches through bus_split!, so the two changes belong together. On the Namco boards the inversion was worth a further 7-18% on top of the dispatch change.
close_reason:
Done in 9d19a4f (joust + robotron + sinistar together -- they share WilliamsBoard).

Numbers (phosphor-bench, release, 400f x 5 reps, best of 6 alternating runs, idle host):
  joust    0.634 -> 0.612 ms/f  -3.5%
  robotron 0.636 -> 0.593       -6.8%
  sinistar 0.778 -> 0.735       -5.5%
Smaller than the Namco boards' 12-27%, and expected: at 1 MHz these run a third as many cycles per frame, so more of the frame is the scanline renderer and the per-cycle audio path (DAC + CVSD + resampler), which neither change touches.

Shape: CPUs move out of the board onto each machine as separate fields (so the debug derive sees one #[debug_cpu] each, and the save-state layout is unchanged -- the board wrote its CPUs first, so no SAVE_VERSION bump). WilliamsCpus is a borrowed pair passed to a generic williams::tick. Robotron and Sinistar add nothing to the board's decoding, so WilliamsBoard implements Bus and IS their bus (no view). Joust needs a view for its LS157 mux; its per-cycle mux update became the WilliamsBus::begin_cycle hook, so the debugger's single-step gets it too.

The second-bus-master answer: the blitter lives *inside* the bus it drives, so it is lifted out of the board with mem::replace for its DMA cycle and put back after -- the safe equivalent of the aliasing this used to rely on. Nothing else observes the gap (only that cycle runs; the halt line it feeds is read by the main CPU, which is not stepping). One behavior difference: a blit whose destination walked into 0xCA00-0xCA07 would lose the write, where the aliased version corrupted the live blitter. No game does that; a debug_assert in bus_write catches it if one ever does. DmaVram still bypasses banking as before.

First real user of the generic Cpu::reset (bek7): the M6809 fetches its reset vector through the bus, so both CPUs now reset against the machine's own bus.

Also did the scanline-outer / cycle-inner inversion left here by blzz.5: rendering a line and driving the ROM PIA video timing signals now happen 260x per frame instead of on each of 16,640 cycles.

New public surface on the three machines: bus_read/bus_write (CPU-facing, side effects included -- distinct from BusDebug peek/poke) and get_cpu_state/get_sound_cpu_state, replacing what tests reached through the system's Bus impl and the board's CPU fields. Worth reusing as the convention for the remaining conversions. The board's device-index tests moved up to the machine, where they now cover the CPU/board join in the derive.

Golden frames unchanged for all 39 machines (these three are blitter-drawn), plus machine, harness and ROM-gated suites; clippy and fmt clean.

title: Prove a reference responds to its stimulus before comparing against it
description:
Every timeline-driven MAME driver in tools/sound-reference/ read the clock as `manager.machine.time.seconds`. That is the attotime's INTEGER seconds field, not elapsed time — it reads 2 for the whole of the third second. So every comparison against a fractional timeline held for a full second: the dkong jump captured as a 50 ms pulse was really a 1 s assertion and the release edge never happened at all. Fixed in this change by switching all five drivers to `manager.machine.time:as_double()`.

The captures looked entirely reasonable. Each held a plausible note of plausible length starting when it should. The jump one sat a fifth below the real note, and hours went into reconciling Phosphor against a control voltage the board never holds.

It was caught only by experimenting on the REFERENCE: capturing with two different hold lengths and finding the results byte-identical, then driving the null case and finding silence. That is the check that was missing, and it is cheap.

WHAT TO BUILD. A self-check that runs before a comparison is trusted, on both sides:
  1. Null case — run the scenario with the effect never triggered. The analysis window must be silent. Catches a capture that is really something else (power-on noise, attract music).
  2. Sensitivity — vary the one parameter under test (trigger width, or the level of one control) and confirm the capture changes. Byte-identical output across two different stimuli means the stimulus is not reaching the circuit.
  3. Both sides. sndcmp's own scenarios deserve the same treatment; nothing proves our target responds either.

Shape: `sndcmp verify <scenario>` running the null and sensitivity cases against a target, plus the same two runs on the MAME side from the driver. Fail loudly rather than reporting a diff.

The lesson is written up in docs/designs/discrete-sound-fidelity.md under 'What the first board taught'; this issue is the tooling half. The other four drivers (asteroid, galaxian, llander, dkong multi-effect) had the same bug, so any measurement taken against them before this change should be treated as unverified — that includes the numbers in …-asteroids-sound-postprocessing-hm4.
notes:
BOTH HALVES BUILT. The checks are the two that actually caught the timing bug, not a reconstruction of them.

OUR SIDE — , all scenarios by default:
  null         run with every action removed; the analysis window must be silent
  sensitivity  move every action 30 ms; the capture must CHANGE (compared byte
               for byte, because a summary statistic can hide it)

REFERENCE SIDE — tools/sound-reference/verify-reference.sh, with the drivers
honouring SND_VERIFY=null|nudge. Same two checks against a real MAME run.

THE 30 ms IS THE POINT. The bug quantised everything to whole seconds, so a
check that moved an event by a second would have passed while the defect sat
underneath it. Asteroids and Lunar Lander have whole-second timelines and were
unaffected for the same reason — a coarse probe cannot see this class of
failure. Anything measuring in tens of milliseconds needs a probe finer than the
failure it is looking for.

THE SCRIPT CAUGHT A FLAW IN ITSELF on its first run, which is worth recording:
it measured the peak over the whole WAV, so Donkey Kong's power-on noise — which
is louder than any of its effects — made the null check fail identically for
every mode. Every driver here carries a pre-roll precisely because of that
noise, so the check now measures from SND_SKIP_S (default 2.0 s) onward. A
verifier that measures the wrong span is no better than the capture it is
checking.

CURRENT STATE: all three dkong scenarios pass, and both the dkong and galaxian
drivers pass. So galaxian's DRIVER is now sound.

GALAXIAN'S VALUES ARE STILL UNVERIFIED, and this issue cannot close them. Its
sound constants were fitted against captures from the broken driver, and
re-checking them needs a sndcmp target adapter and scenarios for galaxian —
neither exists (tools/sound-compare/targets/ has only dkong). That is a separate
piece of work, and the driver passing verification is the precondition for it
rather than a substitute.
close_reason:
Both halves built, and the condition this issue named for its own closure is met.

The notes already recorded the tooling as done: `sndcmp verify` runs the null and
sensitivity checks on our side, and tools/sound-reference/verify-reference.sh
runs the same two against a real MAME run with the drivers honouring
SND_VERIFY=null|nudge.

What was left was stated as: "GALAXIAN'S VALUES ARE STILL UNVERIFIED, and this
issue cannot close them ... re-checking them needs a sndcmp target adapter and
scenarios for galaxian, neither exists". Both now exist and have been used:
tools/sound-compare/src/targets/galaxian.rs, with scenarios melody, hit, fire
and background. All four pass `sndcmp verify`, the driver passes
verify-reference.sh on all four, and all four voices measure within tolerance
against references captured from a driver proved to respond to its own timeline.

Two of Galaxian's fitted constants were deleted in the process (a 0.8 output
trim and a 1.25x hit lift), which is what the re-check was for.

A SECOND WAY A REFERENCE CAN LIE, found after this issue was written and now in
the design doc: responding to the stimulus is necessary but not sufficient. The
discrete engine simulates at the audio sample rate, so a 48 kHz capture reports
its own edge quantisation, and two of Galaxian's three reported residuals were
nothing but that. verify-reference.sh now captures at 192 kHz by default
(SND_SIM_RATE). A capture can pass both checks here and still be wrong in its
top octave.

title: Q*Bert MOB colors wrong: sprite bitplanes flipped vs MAME (LSB/MSB plane order)
description:
Q*Bert's motion-object (sprite/MOB) colors are wrong — the 4 sprite bitplanes
are flipped relative to MAME, permuting the 16 colors of every sprite by a
bit-reversal of the pen index. Same bug class as the Food Fight fix (commit
7978ad5): phosphor's decode_gfx orders plane_offsets LSB-first (entry 0 = pen
bit 0), the reverse of MAME's MSB-first planeoffset, so a machine that copies
MAME's plane list verbatim ends up with reversed planes.

Root cause — machines/src/gottlieb.rs, GottliebBoard::decode_gfx (~line 510):
    let planes: [usize; 4] = std::array::from_fn(|p| p * quarter * 8);
    // plane_offsets = [0, q*8, 2q*8, 3q*8]  (LSB-first: bit0 <- ROM quarter 0)

MAME (src/mame/gottlieb/gottlieb.cpp:2130 spr_layout):
    { RGN_FRAC(0,4), RGN_FRAC(1,4), RGN_FRAC(2,4), RGN_FRAC(3,4) }
    // MSB-first: planeoffset[0] = pen bit 3 <- ROM quarter 0

MAME maps bit3<-Q0, bit2<-Q1, bit1<-Q2, bit0<-Q3; phosphor maps bit0<-Q0 ...
bit3<-Q3 — every pen index p becomes bitrev4(p) (0<->0,1<->8,2<->4,3<->12,...),
scrambling each sprite's 16-color set.

Isolated to sprites: the tile layout in the same file (GOTTLIEB_TILE_LAYOUT,
plane_offsets [3,2,1,0]) IS correctly reversed vs MAME's gfx_8x8x4_packed_msb
(planeoffset {0,1,2,3} = STEP4(0,1), src/emu/video/generic.cpp:97), so tiles
render correctly. Sprite x_offsets/y_offsets/char_increment all match MAME
(STEP16(0,1)/STEP16(0,16)/32*8) — plane order is the only difference.

Scope: GottliebBoard::decode_gfx is used only by Q*Bert (machines/src/qbert.rs).
acceptance_criteria:
* Q*Bert MOBs (Q*Bert, Coily, balls, Slick/Sam, discs) render with MAME-matching
  colors; compare a screenshot to a MAME reference frame.
* Tile/playfield colors unchanged (already correct).
* cargo test -p phosphor-machines, clippy, and fmt pass.
close_reason: Fixed in 3ad18aa: reversed Q*Bert sprite plane order in GottliebBoard::decode_gfx to [3q,2q,q,0]*8 (LSB-first, matching MAME spr_layout's MSB-first planeoffset). Verified by user.

title: Asteroids sound fidelity: thrust rumble (MAME post-processing ruled out)
description:
Follow-up polish from the Asteroids discrete-sound migration (l7o.3). See docs/debugging-asteroids-discrete-sound.md and tools/sound-reference/.

SYMPTOM
- By ear, thrust does not rumble enough, even though its band centre (~85 Hz) matches MAME's measured ~82 Hz peak / 128 Hz centroid. So it's not a pitch error — it's missing low-end weight/body.

HYPOTHESIS: MAME output post-processing
- MAME 0.287's new audio system applies a per-game <audio_effects> chain AFTER the discrete mix. ~/mame/cfg/asteroid.cfg shows: Filters, Compressor, Reverb, Equalizer on tag ':mono'. A compressor + low-shelf EQ would lift and thicken the sub-bass rumble in the *played* sound vs the raw netlist output.
- Open question: does '-wavwrite' tap the speaker mix BEFORE or AFTER that effects chain? If after, our captured 'ground truth' already includes the effects and Phosphor should match the post-effect sound. If before, the difference vs what the user hears is the effects chain.

INVESTIGATION
1. Capture MAME thrust with the audio_effects chain enabled vs disabled (clear/zero the effects in cfg, or a fresh cfg) and compare spectra — quantify how much low-end the compressor/EQ adds.
2. Determine the wavwrite tap point (pre/post effects) from MAME 0.287 source or by toggling effects and diffing captures.
3. Decide whether Phosphor should model an output-stage low-shelf/compressor (in the discrete framework's output stage, reusable across boards) to match the played sound, vs. matching only the raw netlist.

SECONDARY (from the case-study open threads)
- Consider wiring the Phosphor-vs-MAME centroid comparison (tools/sound-reference + machines/examples/asteroid_capture.rs) as a checked-in tolerance test, gated/local-only since it needs MAME + ROMs.

NON-GOAL: bit-exact audio. Target is matching the audible character (the deep thrust rumble) within tolerance.
notes:
2026-08-21: the post-processing hypothesis is SETTLED and it is wrong. MAME
0.287's -wavwrite taps the speaker mix BEFORE the <audio_effects> chain, before
the master gain and before the mute state.

Evidence, both halves:

- Source. sound_manager::m_record_buffer has exactly one writer, in
  output_push(), taken straight from the speaker stream's input buffer and
  clamped to s16. run_effects() works on a separate copy whose output feeds only
  the OSD output streams. sound.h declares the field "pre-effects speaker
  samples for recording". Identical at the mame0287 tag and in 0.288-dev. The
  Lua sound hook reads the same pre-effects buffer, so it is not an alternative
  tap.
- Experiment. Four second Asteroids captures via drive_asteroid_sound.lua,
  differing only in cfg. Stock chain, and a chain with the compressor at 20:1
  with +24 dB in/out and the equalizer at +18 dB on all five bands: byte
  identical. -volume -20: byte identical. Control, a <device_volume gain="0.5">
  on the discrete device, which is upstream of the tap: differs, by 0.4999 in
  RMS. So the capture responds to a cfg mixer change and is blind to the effects
  chain specifically.

Also: the effects chain the cfg "carries" is MAME's fixed default, written for
every game. It records no non-default parameter. Compressor and Reverb default
to mode 0 (off), the Equalizer is on with every band at 0 dB, and the only
active stage is a 20 Hz Q=0.707 high-pass in Filters. So the played sound and
the captured sound differ by a DC blocker, and no compressor or shelf is
lifting the low end on the MAME side either.

CONSEQUENCE. Every reference WAV this branch has ever taken is raw mixed netlist
output. Nothing published needs requalifying. The thrust deficit is a real
difference between the two circuit models, so investigation item 3 (model an
output-stage shelf/compressor to match the played sound) is dropped: the played
sound does not have one. What remains is to read the thrust path in the
reference netlist against the schematic and probe per stage, per the standing
rule that a missing low end is a missing stage rather than a filter value.

comments.author: pjl
comments.text:
2026-08-21, measurement settled before touching the circuit. Two results.

1. THE ENVELOPE ALIGNER WAS WRONG, and the first thrust comparison's -0.205 s
was its bug, not a lag. It scored candidate offsets by the mean of the products
of the two RMS envelopes, so sliding the overlap off a quiet stretch raised the
average and won. Every scenario window opens 50 ms before its trigger, so every
capture has such a stretch. Against a byte-identical copy of itself the thrust
capture reported -0.070 s, and it missed a known 50 ms delay by the same amount,
reporting +0.120.

Fixed by normalizing the correlation by both segments' norms, which makes it a
cosine that Cauchy-Schwarz pins at exactly 1 at zero shift. Self-alignment is
now exactly +0.000, the known 50 ms delay reads exactly +0.050, and ours against
the board reads +0.020 rather than -0.205. Found by asking the tool to align a
file with itself, which is now a test.

Also: on a sustained voice the offset is undetermined even when correct. Thrust
against its own copy peaks only 0.028 above a typical offset, where every
transient tried (dkong stomp and jump, galaxian fire, asteroids ship-fire)
clears 0.05 and is reported bare. audiodiff now prints that caveat rather than a
confident number.

The onset column reading "-" for our side is not a defect either. onset_index
estimates the floor from the quietest tenth of the envelope, and with 50 ms of
silence in a 2.05 s window that tenth lands inside the driven signal, so the
threshold is ten times a driven level and is never crossed. Left alone
deliberately: widening the lead-in would put more silence in every window, and
changing the estimator would move numbers on two finished boards. Both windows
are the same span of the same event by construction, so nothing needs the onset.

2. WINDOW STABILITY, six windows: two start shifts each way and two length
changes. Delta is ours minus board.

  crest factor    -1.29 to -1.55    stable, never changes sign
  0-150 Hz share  +0.80 to +1.14pp  stable, but both sides are over 98% sub-150
  centroid        -0.9 to -2.7 Hz   stable, about 2% of 88 Hz
  level           +0.49 to -0.33dB  NOT stable, changes sign

So the level agreement quoted from the first comparison, 0.06 dB, was the window
being kind. The honest figure is about half a decibel, which is still agreement.
And the band share that was noise on Donkey Kong's 40 ms walk is steady here,
which is a property of the voice rather than of the metric.

THE FINDING, now trustworthy: crest factor 1.7 against the board's 3.2, at
matched RMS and matched centroid, stable across every window. Our thrust is
about half as peaky as the board's. A gain cannot do that and neither can a
filter, so this is pulse structure, which is the missing-mechanism signature.

NOT diagnosed further on purpose. Next is reading the thrust block of
asteroid_a.cpp against the schematic, before any more measuring, per the rule
that an output comparison localises nothing and accuses the last stage.

comments.author: pjl
comments.text:
2026-08-21, THRUST SOURCE FIXED. The rumble deficit was a broken noise register.

THE DEFECT. The thrust LFSR was LfsrSpec::toward_zero(16, (6,14), 0xACE1). Tap
numbers read off a schematic describe a register shifting toward its high end;
run the other way they are a different polynomial, and this one is not primitive
in that direction at all. Longest cycle from any of the 65536 starting states:
42. At 12 kHz that repeats every 3.5 ms, so the "noise" was a 286 Hz tone. The
board's register is 16 bits with XNOR feedback shifting the other way, cycle
32767.

WHY IT HID FOR SO LONG. The next stage is a band-pass with Q 7.6, and a high-Q
band-pass rings at its own centre whatever it is fed. So the voice's pitch,
centroid and fundamental all matched the board the whole time, because they were
the filter's and not the source's. Crest factor was the only metric that could
see it: filtered white noise sits above 3, a ringing filter near a sine wave's.

THE FIX. Replace the spec with the board's arrangement, TowardHigh with inverted
feedback and the output taken from the gate term. XNOR makes the all-zero state
ordinary and all-ones the lock, so the register seeds at 0, which is the state it
powers up in.

MEASURED, thrust against the board, matched windows:

                    before      after      board
  source flatness    0.046      0.409        --
  crest factor        1.79       3.00       3.25
  centroid (Hz)       86.7       87.0       88.1
  fundamental (Hz)    87.3       92.5       92.8
  0-150 Hz delta   +0.95 pp   +0.65 pp       --
  onset (s)          none      0.119      0.118
  env alignment    weak       +0.000        --
  verdict          out of tol  within tolerance

The last two are the independent confirmations. Before the fix the onset
estimator found no onset in our capture and the aligner reported its offset as
weakly determined, both because a ringing filter has no envelope structure. They
now agree with the board to 1 ms and 0 ms.

WHAT THE FIX EXPOSED. THRUST_GAIN was 0.12, fitted against a reference capture
while the source was broken, and it was supplying the make-up a ringing filter
needs. With a real source the same gain hard-clipped at full scale, caught by the
existing every_effect_is_audible test. Not re-fitted: MAME's FILTER2 bandpass is
unity at resonance (b0 = d.wc.(2/T)/den, b2 = -b0), which is why its pre-gain is
600*7.6, the mix weight times Q. Ours now mirrors that structure and lands
-3.37 dB, inside tolerance.

STILL OPEN, and recorded in the source. The band-pass component values are
themselves back-solved from the reference's fc and Q rather than read from a
schematic (R_in is 1.17k, a resistance no series makes), so nothing computed over
them is a derivation and the remaining 3.4 dB cannot be closed by arithmetic. The
output low-pass is also 2nd order at 120 Hz where the reference is 1st order at
160 Hz, left alone deliberately so the source fix stays attributable. Both want
the real schematic values.

SCOPE. toward_zero has one other production user, galaxian_sound.rs:203, checked:
cycle 131071, maximal, clean. One board affected. LfsrSpec::cycle_length is new in
core, sharing its step function with the running node so the check cannot drift
from what executes, and both Asteroids registers are now pinned by tests.

The user confirmed by ear that it now rumbles rather than hums.

comments.author: pjl
comments.text:
2026-08-22: SCHEMATIC READ, and the thrust chain now matches the board on every
metric. Sources: arcade-museum Asteroids-sp.pdf pages 7-8 (Sheet 2 Side B,
DP-143-02) and asteroids_1a.pdf pages 7-8 (Regulator/Audio PCB).

A CORRECTION TO THE PREVIOUS COMMENT. The band-pass values were never invented.
R76 47k carries the signal in, R100 1.2k ties the node to the +5V reference, and
47k parallel 1.2k = 1170.1 ohms, which is the "1_170.0" the code passed. The bug
was collapsing two real parts into one argument: op_amp_band_pass takes fc and Q
from the parallel combination but the centre gain from r_in[0], so a single
1170 entry gave an exact 89.5 Hz and Q 7.6 with a centre gain 40.2x too high.
Corrected to &[47_000.0, 1_200.0].

That also had a second-order effect nobody was looking for. The 40x overdrive
pinned the modelled op-amp against its rails: the THRUST_BP node peaked at
-0.18 dBFS, which on a 12 V rail scale is 11.75 V, and the clamping flattened
the noise peaks. Correcting the arguments moved that node's crest from 3.11 to
3.31 with no filter change.

THE OUTPUT LOW-PASS was also wrong and is now from parts. R104 6.8k in, R103 10k
feedback, C69 0.1uF across it: an inverting active low-pass, ONE pole at
1/(2*pi*R103*C69) = 159.2 Hz, DC gain R103/R104 = 1.47. It had been a 2nd-order
120 Hz Butterworth at unity gain with no part behind it.

CONFIRMED FROM THE SCHEMATIC, no change needed:
- noise: R9 + P9, two LS164s = 16 bits, clocked 12 kHz, NOISERESET on clear,
  taps R9 QG (bit 6) and P9 QG (bit 14), P5 LS86 XOR then N5 LS00 as inverter =
  XNOR, feedback shifted into bit 0 only, output taken from the gate not a
  register bit. Every property of the earlier fix.
- RC pre-filter: R75 2.2k, C62 1uF, 72.3 Hz. Exact.
- mixer: R102 4.7k for thrust into 1/4 of P11 LM324 with R86 1k feedback, +22V
  rail, +5V on the non-inverting input. Explosion uses the same 4.7k, which is
  why their true weights are equal and the reference's 600-vs-1000 split is its
  own filter-stage tweak.

MEASURED after both fixes, thrust against the board, no gain refitted:

               ours    board   delta
  AC RMS      -20.50  -20.48   -0.02 dB
  crest         3.21    3.25   -0.04
  centroid      88.1    88.1    0.0 Hz
  fundamental   92.8    92.8    0.0 Hz
  rolloff 85%  107.7   107.7    0.0 Hz
  onset        0.118   0.118    0.000 s
  0-150 Hz     98.65   98.67   -0.02 pp
  STFT distance 0.66 (was 0.83)

Stable across five windows: crest delta -0.02 to -0.11, level -0.01 to -0.05 dB.
The level is now stable too, where at the start of the day it swung 0.8 dB and
changed sign. Session arc for crest factor: 1.79 -> 3.00 (noise register) ->
3.08 (band-pass arguments) -> 3.21 (output low-pass), against 3.25.

STILL NOT DERIVED FROM PARTS: THRUST_GAIN. Its form now mirrors the reference
exactly, so the level agrees, but the weight is the reference's tweaked 600
rather than the 1000 its summing resistor implies, and Q sits in it as an energy
correction rather than a component. Retiring it means expressing every voice in
volts and letting R86/R_summing weight them, which the schematic now makes
possible for all seven. Board-wide change, not a thrust one.

ALSO NOTED, not acted on: the board gates the noise with the R11 4016B switch
BEFORE the RC; we and the reference both gate after it. Affects attack and
release shape, not steady state.

comments.author: pjl
comments.text:
2026-08-22: THUMP REBUILT FROM THE SCHEMATIC. User confirms it sounds right.

DEFECTS FOUND AND FIXED, in the order they surfaced.

1. Wrong tap on the 555. The board takes pin 3, the square, through R74/C64;
this took the capacitor. A sawtooth's harmonics fall as 1/n^2 where a square's
fall as 1/n, so the voice measured 17 Hz dull with 7 points too much energy
below 150 Hz. The capacitor tap existed because ne555_cc had no discharge
resistor, which made its square a pulse one step wide and unusable.

2. Missing discharge resistor. Added r_disch to ne555_cc; the board's is R51
18k. Passing 0 keeps the old ideal one-step discharge, so Galaxian is
untouched. The discharge relaxes toward i*r_disch and not toward ground,
because the current source keeps feeding the resistor while the pin sinks it;
MAME labels that case "Asteroids - Special Case" and I would have got it wrong
by guessing.

3. Fitted CV trim, deleted. THUMP_CV carried a 1.027 gain "to land the
reference pitch". It was compensating for the missing discharge time. With the
discharge modelled and the trim removed, the fundamental lands on 53.5 Hz
against the board's 53.5 Hz, delta 0.0.

4. Fabricated AC coupling, deleted. A 16k/1uF high-pass with no counterpart on
the board, there only to strip the capacitor tap's DC.

5. Missing coupling capacitor, added. The board's DC blocker is R14/C6 on the
Regulator/Audio PCB, 1.59 Hz, at the amplifier's input. Modelled at the mix, so
it serves all seven voices. The reference instead subtracts half the square's
swing, which its own header calls a cheat to make the waveform AC, and which
leaves a residual whenever the duty is not 50 %: that is the 0.052 DC the
reference capture carries and we now do not.

6. Fitted output gain, re-derived. THUMP_GAIN was 0.135, fitted against the
capacitor tap; with the square it ran 10 dB hot. Now the path's mix weight over
the 555's half swing, the same shape thrust uses.

7. THE ONE THE METRICS COULD NOT SEE. The gate was a multiply on the filtered
output with the 555 free-running underneath, so switching thump on connected an
oscillator at an arbitrary phase. Largest single-sample step at the onset was
3636; gating the 555's reset pin as the board does makes it 272. This changed no
steady-state number.

MEASURED against the board, matched windows, no constant fitted:
  fundamental   53.5 vs 53.5 Hz     (delta 0.0)
  rolloff 85%   172.3 vs 172.3 Hz   (delta 0.0)
  centroid      110.0 vs 117.0 Hz
  0-150 Hz      77.07 vs 75.43      (+1.64 pp)
  level         -1.67 dB
  DC            0.005 vs 0.052 (the reference's cheat)
  clipped       0 samples in 40 s of recorded play
Waveform, duty and non-harmonic energy all match within 1-2 %.

PROCESS NOTE WORTH KEEPING. Every metric agreed before defect 7 was found, and
was stable across five windows. The 3636-sample step sat inside the analysis
window and moved nothing, being one sample in ninety thousand. It was located by
one sentence of listening: "scratchiness right as it starts". A steady-state
comparison cannot see a transient defect.

STILL OPEN on this board: the saucer is built from frequency literals with no
netlist behind it (the board has a 555 LFO into a 566 VCO); the explosion
re-clocks its own register where the board samples the shared one through an
LS74; both fires gate through their envelope rather than their timer and
truncate on release; and the volts rework would retire the remaining fitted
gains across all seven voices now that every summing resistor is known.

comments.author: pjl
comments.text:
2026-08-22: THE ASTEROIDS REFERENCE CAPTURES WERE CONTAMINATED. Driver fixed,
all eight re-captured, sweep re-run.

The driver did not park the main CPU, on the reasoning recorded in its own
header: "attract mode is silent, so we don't need to halt the CPU". Silent is
not the same as not writing. The game clears the 74LS259 audio latch as
housekeeping about 0.3 ms after the driver sets it, so every latch-driven voice
was captured as one short burst per frame instead of a held note. That is five
of the eight scenarios: saucer, saucer-sel, both fires, thrust and life.

Life made it visible: chopped to a 0.3 ms burst at 61.7 Hz, which is the frame
rate. Against that reference our life measured 14.45 dB loud, crest 1.14 against
10.50, flatness 0.0001 against 0.2197, centroid off by 202 Hz, and three bands
out of tolerance. With the CPU parked and nothing changed on our side: crest
1.14 against 1.24, level -3.33 dB, centroid +57 Hz, rolloff +21.5 Hz, within
tolerance. Our life voice was correct the whole time.

NEITHER VERIFY CHECK CAN SEE THIS. The null run is still silent because nothing
is triggered; the sensitivity run still changes because a chopped capture chops
differently when the schedule moves. And the null check measures PEAK, which
chopping does not alter: the driven peaks before and after parking are identical
to seventeen significant figures. Design doc now carries this as a third check,
exclusivity, plus the cheap detector if parking is impossible: a capture
modulated at the machine's frame rate is contaminated, because no voice on these
boards is periodic at 60 Hz on its own.

Both drivers now park the 6502 at a JMP-to-self in work RAM and pet the
watchdog, as the Galaxian and Donkey Kong drivers already did. Both still pass
verify-reference.sh.

SWEEP AGAINST CORRECTED REFERENCES, all eight:
  voice          crest d   level d   centroid d   verdict
  thrust          -0.03    -0.02dB     +0.0 Hz    within
  life            -0.11    -3.33dB    +57.0 Hz    within
  saucer          +0.02    -3.33dB     +4.4 Hz    within
  saucer-large    +0.01    -3.34dB     +1.2 Hz    within
  explosion       -0.34    -3.76dB    +16.4 Hz    within
  thump           +1.20    -1.67dB     -7.0 Hz    within
  ship-fire       +5.39    +2.07dB   +1282.6 Hz   OUT
  saucer-fire     +3.15    -2.04dB    +883.0 Hz   OUT

Two corrections to earlier guesses. The SAUCER is not the worst voice: it
matches within 4.4 Hz of centroid and 0.02 of crest, because our literals are
MAME's literals and MAME's saucer is itself admittedly tweaked ("The sound can
be tweaked with the gain and adder constants in the 2 lines below"). Matching
its literals is not the same as matching the board, and settling that properly
needs the 555-into-566 circuit the schematic shows, but there is no measurable
disagreement to chase. The EXPLOSION is also within tolerance despite modelling
its own private noise register where the board samples the shared one.

A SYSTEMATIC OFFSET worth noting rather than chasing: every voice weighted by a
plain LVL_x/LVL_TOTAL sits 3.3 to 3.8 dB under the reference. MAME routes its
discrete output with add_route(ALL_OUTPUTS, "mono", 1.4), which is +2.9 dB and
accounts for most of it. That is a MAME route gain and not a board property, and
reproducing it would eat headroom our normalisation exists to keep, so it is
left alone and recorded.

NEXT: the two fires are the only voices with a real disagreement. Both are too
bright and too peaky with far too little low end (band 0 Hz is -39 pp on the
ship, -23 pp on the saucer). Our model taps the 555 capacitor and gates through
an exponential envelope that zeroes on release; the reference is a square whose
DUTY varies with frequency (4500/freq + 67 per cent) carrying a large
low-frequency component. The board has the 555s with R57 and R61 at 680 ohms on
their discharge pins, so this is the same shape of fix as thump: take pin 3,
model the discharge resistor, gate at reset.

comments.author: pjl
comments.text:
2026-08-23: both fire voices rebuilt from Sheet 2 Side B. Every timing value in
the old model is gone. Reading pages 7 and 8 of the -sp manual at 400 dpi settles
the whole chain, and the parts reproduce the reference's fitted numbers.

WHAT THE BOARD ACTUALLY IS, per voice (saucer / ship designators):

  pitch cap        C38 10uF / C47 1uF, held at +5 V by an M9 4016B section and
                   released on the enable
  pitch source     Q3 through R54 10k / Q1 through R52 33k, biased by CR3+CR4
                   into R53 1k, so 84 uA and 26 uA out of a 0.84 V drive
  VCO current      an LM324 follower puts that rising voltage on Q4/Q5's emitter,
                   whose R56/R65 3.3k to +12 V therefore delivers a FALLING
                   current, (12 - Vcv)/3.3k
  timer            M8/L9 555 on +5 V, C35/C50 1 uF, R57/R61 680, enable on pin 4
  output diode     CR6/CR8, CATHODE AT PIN 3
  amplitude        C39/C48 10 uF, held at +5 V by a second 4016B section, reaching
                   the summing node through R58 10k / R66 2.7k
  mixer            R81/R84 100k into P11's R86 1k, non-inverting input at +5 V

The old model had 0.01 uF, 110k, a 5 V rail, no discharge resistor, an envelope
multiply, a capacitor tap, a fitted linear CV ramp and two fitted output gains.
None of those is a part.

THE PARTS GIVE THE REFERENCE'S FITTED NUMBERS. Start 795 Hz against its 820/830.
Saucer ending 605 Hz against its 630. Amplitude tau, which falls out of R58/R66
and C39/C48 weighted by the duty cycle, 0.312 s and 0.112 s against its
hand-fitted 0.3 and 0.081.

TWO THINGS THE SCHEMATIC SETTLED THAT WERE NOT IN THE PLAN.

The current source feeds PIN 7, with R57/R61 between the pin and the cap. Thump,
drawn a few centimetres away, is the other way round: Q2 joins C33 and R51 goes
on to pin 7. Charging is identical either way. Discharging is not: with the
source on the cap it keeps feeding the resistor while the pin sinks, so the cap
relaxes toward i*r_disch, and with the source on the pin the pin swallows that
current and the cap empties toward ground. At the top of the saucer's sweep
i*R57 is 1.44 V against a 1.667 V trigger, so the wrong asymptote crawls the last
quarter volt and takes three times as long. ne555_cc takes a Feed555 argument
now, asserted against the closed form rather than against the other variant.

CR6/CR8's orientation, which could not be read in asteroids_1a.pdf, is
unambiguous at 400 dpi: cathode at pin 3. It is a PULL-DOWN, not a series pass
and not a clamp. That is why the amplitude decay lives in C39/C48 rather than in
an envelope, and it is also why the decay does not reach zero: the capacitor
empties through the diode during the timer's low phase and is topped back up
from the mixer's +5 V reference through R58+R81 during its high one, and the two
average out at a floor. The reference adds that floor by hand as a "+7".

THE TRIGGER DISCIPLINE IS SETTLED, and it was a real defect in the comparison.
tools/script/examples/asteroid_fire_trace.rhai watches every write to the 74LS259
through a real shot: the game rewrites the whole latch every frame and holds line
4 for FOURTEEN of them, about 230 ms, whether the button is tapped for two frames
or held for forty. It is the game's timer, not the player's finger. Both
scenarios and the driver now pulse to that length.

This mattered more than a detail. Held, the board's pitch capacitor fills to Q1's
saturation and the 555 runs on at ~175 Hz forever, because nothing in the circuit
ends it; the reference goes quiet instead, but only because its fitted duty
(4500/f + 67) crosses 100 % at 136 Hz and stops making edges. The held window was
86 % silence on one side and 2 % on the other.

MEASURED, over matched 0.35 s windows from 50 ms before the trigger:

                       ship            saucer
  centroid          +85 Hz on 1934   +202 Hz on 1495
  rolloff 85%      -108 Hz on 3101   -108 Hz on 1486
  fundamental       -12.5 Hz          -40.0 Hz
  decay tau        0.112 vs 0.114 s  0.312 vs 0.321 s
  worst band share  -7.0 pp           -8.6 pp
  crest             +1.46             +0.75
  level             -3.2 dB           -2.6 dB
  onset            0.050 vs 0.057 s  0.050 vs 0.057 s
  discontinuity     1.13 vs 1.12      1.04 vs 1.05
  verdict           within tolerance  within tolerance

Those are measured ABOVE 150 Hz, and the split is the finding rather than a
convenience. Below 150 Hz the two disagree completely, and the mechanism is not
in doubt: the board's fire path has no coupling capacitor anywhere in it. An idle
voice holds its 555 in reset, a 555 in reset has its output low, so the diode is
conducting and the summing node rests at the clamp; firing releases that node
upward for 62 % of each cycle rising to 94 %. A shot is a 230 ms DC excursion at
the mixer with a pulse train riding on it, and the mix's own coupling capacitor
(R14/C6, 1.59 Hz, tau 100 ms) barely touches something that short. The reference
has no such thing because it does not build the output network at all: it emits a
square wave primitive, which is +/-amplitude/2 about a bias it leaves at zero.
Centred by construction rather than by a circuit. Full band that is +40 and +34
points of 0-150 Hz share.

Not fitted away, because there is no part to point at: two 400 dpi crops of the
mixer and of both fire outputs show seven summing resistors going straight into
the LM324, and the only capacitors in the path are C113 after the mixer and C6 at
the amplifier's input.

RESIDUAL QUANTIFIED RATHER THAN WAVED AT. C113 (1 uF into R111's 10k, 15.9 Hz) is
a real part and does sit between the mixer and one speaker output, but only one:
the board's two outputs are anti-phase into a bridged speaker, so the
differential response is HP(1.59) * (1 + HP(15.9))/2, a 6 dB shelf between 8 and
16 Hz rather than a second high-pass. It halves the pedestal, does not remove it,
is inaudible on everything else, and modelling one channel's capacitor without
the bridge sum would over-apply it. Recorded, not added.

Costs nothing measurable in play: asteroid over its recorded movie is DC +0.0000,
0.00 % clipped, peak -5.51 dBFS.

TOOLING, both from this session's own mistakes.

disasm audiodiff has a discontinuity block now: max |x[n]-x[n-1]|, the
99.9th-percentile step beside it, the ratio, and where the largest lands relative
to each side's OWN onset. The ratio is what makes it usable here, since a square
wave's every edge is a full-swing step and reads about 1.0. It is compared side
to side rather than against a ceiling, because an impulsive effect is high on
both sides and is not defective. This is what would have caught thump's onset
scratch without an ear.

verify-reference.sh now refuses a driven window with no effect in it. Pulsing the
fires put the whole event before its 2.0 s measurement window, so the driven and
null peaks were both zero and "the null run is quieter" went on reporting ok: a
comparison between two silences that would pass for any driver at all. Fixed with
SND_SKIP_S=0.9 for these two, and the guard so the next one fails loudly.

KNOWN DIFFERENCES, both recorded in the source.

The ship's sweep ends at about 175 Hz where the reference's linear ramp reaches
110. Ours stops when Q1 saturates, which is a part; the reference's endpoint is
its own fitted number and the manual gives none. The two track within 5 % until
the last fifth of the sweep.

Mix weights are still the reference's adder constants rather than the board's
summing resistors. The schematic gives all seven (R83 47k, R77 39k, R78 47k,
R81 100k, R84 100k, R82 4.7k, R102 4.7k into R86 1k), so expressing every voice
in volts and letting the mixer weight them would retire the last fitted constant
in the file. That is a board-wide change and is the next thing worth doing here.

REMAINING ON THIS BOARD: the saucer's 555-into-566 warble and the explosion's
pitch divider still carry reference literals rather than parts. Neither shows a
measurable disagreement, so neither is urgent.

title: Atari System 1 shared board + Road Runner (2nd game)
description: Extract the shared Atari System 1 hardware out of MarbleSystem into an AtariSystem1Board (repo board-wrapper pattern, like WilliamsBoard+JoustSystem), then add Road Runner as a second game on that board. VIA register file + the handshake lines the sound CPU polls; TMS5220 returns ready/not-busy, silent drain_audio. Wired in behind AtariSystem1Sound's speech:bool flag (off for Marble). Real LPC speech is a separate follow-up (shared with Star Wars).

Wired both into AtariSystem1Sound behind the speech flag as a private Speech{via,tms} Option, mapped at sound 0x1000-0x100F per the MAME atarisy1 wiring (PA=data/status, PB D0=/WS D1=/RS D2=/READY D3=/INT). title: Road Runner analog joystick input (ADC0809 + IRQ2)
description: Reuse core/src/device/adc0809.rs for Road Runner's hall-effect analog joystick. Map 0xF40000-0xF4001F in RoadRunnerSystem's Bus (adc_r/adc_w); feed X (IN1, reversed) / Y (IN0) from input. Wire IRQ2 (the analog-joystick interrupt, gated by the adc_w A4 enable bit) into the board's interrupt_level. InputConfigurable: AnalogAxis X/Y (mouse) + keyboard fallback -> ADC channels; two hop buttons -> board f60000_buttons bits 0-1. Verify: reads move the player; IRQ2 cadence vs MAME.
close_reason: Wired Road Runner's ADC0809 analog joystick at 0xF40000 + IRQ2. adc_w selects channel/starts conversion + latches the A4 joystick-IRQ enable; adc_r returns the sample and restarts (per MAME adc_r). X=ch7 (reversed), Y=ch6. IRQ2 = enable AND end-of-conversion, EOC modeled ~512 CPU cycles after start, cleared on read (one-per-conversion cadence). Added board int2 line/interrupt_level (commit 94135e7). InputConfigurable: analog X/Y mouse + arrow-key fallback; hop/start/coin/service. This also fixes the attract demo (was frozen without IRQ2). Verified with roadrunn.zip: demo animates, player moves; Marble byte-identical; 9 tests. 2 commits (94135e7 board IRQ2, 9a9dafc wrapper ADC).
