title: Epic: Cycle-accurate I8088
description:
The I8088 is instruction-level, not cycle-accurate (core/src/cpu/i8088/README.md, 'Timing: Instruction-level (not cycle-accurate)'), while five of the seven cores are true per-cycle state machines. Same stated-goal gap as the M68000 epic.

Smaller blast radius: Q*bert is the only shipped board on it today, with Reactor and Mad Planets on the roadmap. Its existing decode/execute split (decode.rs, execute.rs, addressing.rs) and BIU-oriented structure are closer to per-cycle than the M68000's atomic model, so this should be the lighter of the two.

Sequenced after the M68000 epic so the harder core sets the pattern — revisit if the M68000 design turns out to be board-specific enough not to transfer.

First child is the design doc. Blocked by the benchmark harness.

title: Design doc: cycle-accurate I8088
description:
Write docs/designs/cycle-accurate-i8088.md before any code. It must resolve:

- BIU prefetch queue: the 8088 has a four-byte queue whose refill timing is the main source of real cycle counts and is observable through bus ordering. Decide whether to model it.
- Bus cycle model: the 8088 bus cycle is four T-states plus wait states; decide what one tick() means.
- Validation: SingleStepTests/8088 supplies cycle-by-cycle bus activity, unlike the 680x0 suite. Confirm the vectors carry what is needed and make them the per-cycle oracle — this may make the I8088 the easier core to prove, which is an argument for doing it first after all.
- Reuse: how much of the M68000 design transfers, and whether a shared per-cycle scaffolding is worth extracting.
- Migration order by instruction class, keeping the 2,577,000-vector gate green throughout.

Acceptance: as for the M68000 doc.

title: Epic: Cycle-accurate M68000
description:
The M68000 decodes and applies an instruction's full effect on cycle 0, then burns the remaining documented cycles as bus-idle waits (core/src/cpu/m68000/README.md, 'Execution model: atomic, not per-cycle'). No per-cycle bus traces, no prefetch queue. Every 8-bit core in the workspace is a true per-cycle state machine where one tick() is one bus transaction.

Design priority #1 for this project is cycle-accurate hardware matching, so this is a stated-goal gap rather than a preference. It caps what the whole 68000 branch can be: foodf, quantum, marble and roadrunner run on approximate timing today, and any future board needing DMA contention, a mid-instruction bus grant, or video timing derived from bus phase hits this wall.

Larger blast radius than the I8088 (four boards vs one) and the harder of the two, so doing this first de-risks the other.

First child is the design doc — the shape depends on decisions not yet made (prefetch queue modelling, how the existing state-only SingleStepTests gate coexists with per-cycle bus traces, and how this interacts with the concrete-bus-dispatch epic, which changes the same inner loop).

Blocked by the benchmark harness: converting an atomic core to per-cycle will cost throughput and we should know how much.

title: Design doc: cycle-accurate M68000
description:
Write docs/designs/cycle-accurate-m68000.md before any code. It must resolve:

- Bus cycle model: the 68000 bus cycle is four clock states (S0-S7 in half-clocks); decide whether tick() is one clock or one bus cycle, and how that squares with Bus<Address=u32, Data=u16> being one word transaction today.
- Prefetch: the two-word prefetch queue is the main observable difference and drives the documented cycle counts. Decide whether to model it, since without it 'cycle-accurate' is only half true.
- Validation: SingleStepTests/680x0 is state-only and already passes 1,000,058 vectors. Per-cycle work needs a bus-trace oracle it does not provide — decide what replaces or supplements it, and whether the existing gate is preserved unchanged as a regression net.
- Interaction with the byte-strobe fix (contained-fidelity epic) which touches the same bus interface.
- Interaction with the concrete-bus-dispatch epic, which changes the same inner loop.
- 68010 differences, since Atari System 1 uses the 68010 variant.
- Migration order by instruction class, and how to keep the tree green throughout.

Reference the existing docs/designs/m68000-emulator.md rather than restating it.

Acceptance: the doc answers each of the above concretely enough that the follow-on issues can be written from it.

title: MCR: CTC channel 0 zero-count is not wired to channel 1's trigger
description:
On the MCR board the Z80 CTC's channel 0 zero-count output drives channel 1's
trigger input, so the two cascade into one longer divider. MAME wires it:

  m_ctc->zc_callback<0>().set(m_ctc, FUNC(z80ctc_device::trg1));   mcr.cpp:1812

Our board never does. Mcr2Board::begin_scanline (mcr2.rs:406-418) triggers
channels 2 and 3 from the scanline counter and nothing else, and no code in
machines/ calls Z80Ctc::zc_output at all. The device already models the pulse
(core/src/device/z80ctc.rs:60, 215-217), so this is a missing wire on the board,
not a missing feature in the chip.

CONSEQUENCE. A program that puts channel 0 in timer mode and channel 1 in
counter mode gets a channel 1 that never counts. Whether any MCR II game does
that is unknown and was not checked; Satan's Hollow boots and plays, so if it
uses the cascade it is not for anything load bearing.

WHY IT IS WORTH FIXING ANYWAY. phosphor-emulator-conformance-rom-programme-hl4t.1
found that the CTC is the only thing on this board that lets a program see the
beam: prescale 256 with the MCR clock tree is exactly one scanline per count, so
a timer channel is a programmable scanline interrupt and its down counter reads
as a line number. A conformance ROM would exercise the CTC hard, and the cascade
is one of the first things such a ROM would notice.

Surfaced by the hl4t.1 board survey. See
docs/designs/conformance-rom-board-survey.md.
close_reason: Wired: channel 0's zero count now pulses channel 1's trigger in begin_cycle_inner. The schematic shows exactly one loopback from an output pin to a trigger pin on the CTC, which is the structure; the pin numbers on that scan do not match the part's pinout (CTCEN sits against a pin that is a trigger input on a Z80 CTC), so the 0-to-1 channel indices follow the reference driver and the comment says so. Measured: Satan's Hollow programs channel 1 as an auto-start timer, whose CLK/TRG input the part ignores, so the cascade is inert for it and the golden frame is byte-identical. Landed anyway because the board should model the board, and hl4t.1 found this CTC is the only window on the beam a conformance ROM here would have. Test reaches the wire directly and was made to fail (left 0, right 10).

comments.author: pjl
comments.text:
Wired, and the "whether any MCR II game does that is unknown and was not
checked" from the description is now checked. It does not.

WHAT THE SCHEMATIC SHOWS, AND WHAT IT DOES NOT. On sheet 9-6 the CTC (B3,
MK3882) has exactly one wire that leaves a pin on the left of the symbol, runs
around the bottom of the chip, and comes back to a pin on the right. It is the
only feedback path on the part; everything else goes to the buffered bus, the
CPU control lines, or named board nets (493, INT1, INT3, CTCEN). On a Z80 CTC
the only left-side outputs are ZC/TO0-2 and the only right-side inputs a
loopback could reach are CLK/TRG0-3, so what the drawing shows is a
zero-count-to-trigger cascade. That much is legible and it is the part that
matters.

What is NOT legible is which channels. The pin numbers on this scan do not match
the part's pinout: the net drawn against pin 16 is CTCEN, the chip enable, which
is pin 22 on a Z80 CTC, while pin 16 is CLK/TRG2. With the numbering that far
out I will not read channel indices off it. So 0 to 1 follows the reference
driver (mcr.cpp:1812), and the code comment says so rather than implying the
schematic settled it.

THE MEASUREMENT, WHICH CHANGES WHAT THIS ISSUE IS WORTH. I instrumented the CTC
port writes and booted Satan's Hollow from real ROMs for 600 frames. What it
programs:

  ch0 = 0x08                     interrupt vector base
  ch3 = 0xC7 then 0x01           counter, IRQ on, time constant 1
                                 -> one interrupt per 493 edge, once a frame
  ch1 = 0xA7 then 0x4E           TIMER, prescale 256, time constant 78
                                 -> 19,968 cycles, 125 Hz
  ch0 = 0x87 then 0xBB           timer, prescale 16, time constant 187
  ch2 = 0xA7 then 0xA3           timer, prescale 256, time constant 163
  ch0 = 0x03, ch2 = 0x03         software reset, stopping both

then ch0 and ch2 repeat that start/stop pattern for the rest of the run.

Channel 1 is an auto-start TIMER, not a counter: bit 6 clear, and bit 3 clear so
it starts when the time constant lands rather than waiting on CLK/TRG. In that
mode the part ignores the CLK/TRG1 input entirely. **So the cascade cannot
affect Satan's Hollow, and the golden frame is byte-identical after this
change**, which is the confirmation rather than a disappointment.

Two things worth carrying forward from that dump. Channel 3 with time constant 1
is exactly the once-per-frame interrupt the survey predicted from the `493`
decode, measured rather than inferred. And channel 2, which the reference wires
to VBLANK, is also programmed as an auto-start timer here, so that external
trigger is equally unused by this game; our board still drives it, and should,
because the wire is real.

WHY LAND IT AT ALL, GIVEN IT IS INERT. The board should model the board. It is
five lines, the structure is confirmed, MCR II has other games that are not in
the tree yet, and phosphor-emulator-conformance-rom-programme-hl4t.1 found that
this CTC is the only thing on this board that lets a program see the beam, so a
conformance ROM here would lean on it hard. Landing it inert with a test that
reaches the wire directly is better than a comment saying it was considered.

THE TEST WAS MADE TO FAIL. channel_0_zero_count_clocks_channel_1 puts channel 0
in timer mode (prescale 16, time constant 3, so a zero count every 48 cycles) and
channel 1 in counter mode fed only by that output, then runs ten periods through
the board's own per-cycle path so the cascade is exercised where it lives.
Disconnecting the wire gives left 0, right 10. Its doc comment says outright that
no game in the tree reaches this and that the test therefore builds the case
itself, so the suite does not look as though a real ROM covers it.

VERIFIED. clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -D warnings clean with
both files touched first; cargo test --workspace green; cargo fmt clean;
ROM-gated boot_check 7/7, save_state_rom 7/7, audio_sanity 13/13, and the shollow
golden frame unchanged (forced past the #[ignore] that is
phosphor-emulator-gn5w).

title: Show a running frame counter in the F10 debug overlay
description:
Keep a monotonic count of emulated frames and surface it on the F10 debug overlay, alongside the existing FPS and per-machine overlay_stats() lines. Useful for debugging: pinpointing/reproducing a glitch at a specific frame, correlating with logs, and comparing against a reference emulator's frame number.

Mechanism (frontend): the F10 overlay is gated by show_fps in frontend/src/emulator.rs (~lines 597-658). It draws fps_text plus machine.overlay_stats() through crate::overlay::draw_overlay(...) for raster machines and an egui window (present_vectors_with_overlay) for vector machines.

Proposed implementation (machine-agnostic, frontend-side):
- Add a frame counter (u64) to the main loop, incremented once per run_frame() call (per emulated frame, not per rendered frame).
- Render it on the overlay as a line like 'Frame: N' in both the raster path (crate::overlay::draw_overlay) and the vector egui path. Simplest: add it to fps_text, or add a dedicated line.
- Keep it a frontend/session counter independent of machine save state (so it works for every machine without touching MachineCore). Decide reset semantics: zero it on machine.reset(); leave it running across quick save/load (F6/F7), or restore alongside state if that's more useful for debugging (document the choice).

Acceptance: with F10 on, a frame-count line appears and increments each frame for both raster and vector machines; off when the overlay is hidden.

Consider whether it belongs next to the FPS readout permanently vs only in the overlay, and whether a per-machine current-scanline/beam readout would be a useful adjacent addition (out of scope here).
close_reason: Frame counter implemented and shown on the F10 overlay (fps line: 'fps: X  frame: N'). Unified into DebugState.frame_count so it also drives the new Step Frame control and the frame breakpoint. Increments per completed frame (debugger open or not), zeroes on F5 reset.

title: Debug observability: event tracing + rich watchpoints + memory peek semantics
description: Add a DebugTrace capability + DebugTraceBuffer ring, rich WatchpointHit metadata + phase, and DebugRead-based memory peek semantics. Consumes the canonical shared types from epic 2 (does NOT redefine them). Design: docs/designs/debug-observability.md. Blocked by epic 2.
close_reason: Epic complete across 5 subtasks: rich WatchpointHit metadata + phase semantics (d8x.1), DebugEvent/DebugTrace/DebugTraceBuffer + #[debug_events] derive + Williams pilot + UI event panel (d8x.2), DebugRead peek semantics through core/derive/memory-viewer (d8x.3), device reset/register-write debug controls (d8x.4), and instrumentation broadened to all board families incl. watchpoint support for manual-BusDebug Galaga/DigDug (d8x.5). Design doc docs/designs/debug-observability.md fully implemented for the 16-bit surface; u16->u32 widening remains with the addr32 epic (hqy) as designed.

title: debug-obs: rich WatchpointHit metadata + phase (consume canonical type)
description: Populate source/cycle/pc/region/device on the canonical WatchpointHit; implement WatchpointPhase (writes pause before side effect, reads after value). Update debug UI watchpoint display.
close_reason: Rich WatchpointHit metadata implemented: cycle/pc latched per-tick into AddressSpace16 (boards can't read CPU state mid-tick), populated alongside source/region; device attribution via watch_*_with (Williams pilot: Widget/ROM/Sound PIA, Blitter); WatchpointPhase derived from kind with all boards checking write watchpoints before side effects; debug UI shows source/value/phase/region/device/cycle/PC. 4 commits, all tests + clippy clean.

title: debug-obs: DebugEvent/DebugTrace + DebugTraceBuffer + #[debug_events] derive; Williams pilot
description: Add DebugEvent/DebugEventKind, DebugTrace trait, per-board DebugTraceBuffer ring (disabled by default, &'static str detail). #[debug_events] derive. Instrument Williams as pilot. Events excluded from save-state.
close_reason: DebugEvent/DebugEventKind/DebugTraceBuffer (4096-event ring, disabled by default, static-str detail) + DebugTrace capability added to FrontendMachine bundle with no-op defaults. #[derive(DebugTrace)] with #[debug_events] field attribute. Williams pilot records BankSwitch/Watchdog/DeviceWrite/Dma/MemoryWrite events with cycle/PC/device attribution (reusing the d8x.1 context latch); reads trace DMA+device only to avoid fetch noise. Events excluded from save states (tested). Debug UI gains a virtualized Event Trace panel. 4 commits, tests + clippy clean.

title: debug-obs: memory peek semantics (DebugRead) + BusDebug::peek + viewer
description: Add BusDebug::peek returning the canonical DebugRead (backed/io/unmapped); teach AddressSpace16/32 to return it; update memory viewer to stop showing FF for missing bytes.
close_reason: Memory peek semantics implemented: AddressSpace16::debug_peek returns canonical DebugRead (backed/io/unmapped, resolving mirrors + banking); BusDebug::peek with read()-based default; #[derive(BusDebug)] overrides peek with per-map semantics; memory viewer renders '--' for I/O and '..' for unmapped instead of fake FF. AddressSpace32 doesn't exist yet (hqy epic) — its peek lands there. 3 commits, tests + clippy clean.

title: debug-obs: device debug controls (reset / register write)
description: Expose per-device reset + register-write in the UI via existing reset_device/write_device_register. Defer semantic DebugAction list until tracing shows repeated needs.
close_reason: Device debug controls exposed in UI: per-device Reset button + hex offset/value register write, queued as DeviceAction and applied via existing BusDebug reset_device/write_device_register with immediate panel refresh. DevicePanel now carries its devices()-order index for correct dispatch past CPU filtering. Added previously-missing tests pinning the derived dispatch (indexing, write reaching device, reset isolation, CPU/out-of-range no-ops). Semantic DebugAction list deferred per design. 2 commits, tests + clippy clean.

title: debug-obs: broaden instrumentation (Namco Pac, TKG-04, Atari vector, Galaga/DigDug)
description: Instrument more boards by priority; give manual-BusDebug machines (Galaga/DigDug) reusable Watchpoints support they lack today.
close_reason: All four board families instrumented: Namco Pac (I/O latch/WSG/sprite/watchdog events + VBLANK IRQ), TKG-04 (sound latch/IRQ, NMI mask, i8257 sprite DMA with byte counts), Atari DVG+AVG (vector generator start/reset, watchdog, periodic NMI/IRQ), and Galaga/Dig Dug — which also gained the Watchpoints support they lacked: board-level Watchpoints set with per-CPU PC latching across 3 Z80s, BusDebug watchpoint overrides, and 06XX/51XX/53XX custom-chip transaction events. 9 wrappers now delegate DebugTrace. 4 commits, 20 new tests, clippy clean.

title: Debug panel unsupported on 24-bit-bus (MC68000) machines
description:
The egui debug panel (F1 / --debug) is gated on MachineDebug::debug_bus() returning Some, and the debugger's memory inspector is 16-bit-addressed. The MC68000 machines (Food Fight, Quantum) run on a 24-bit AddressSpace32 bus and return None for debug_bus, so --debug silently does nothing for them (the frontend computes has_debug = machine.debug_bus().is_some() in frontend/src/emulator.rs and disables the panel).

Cycle/instruction stepping still works internally via MachineDebug::debug_tick; only the interactive panel (register view + memory inspector) is unavailable.

To support it, the debugger's BusDebug trait and the egui memory inspector / disassembly view in frontend/src/debug_ui.rs need to handle 32-bit addresses (currently u16-addressed). The #[derive(BusDebug)] macro and AddressSpace32 wiring would also need a 32-bit debug path.

Affects: foodf.rs, quantum.rs (both note this limitation in their MachineDebug impls).
close_reason: Debug panel now works on 24-bit-bus MC68000 machines. AddressSpace32 already had the full debug surface (debug_read/peek/poke/watchpoints, all u32) and the frontend memory viewer + disassembly were already u32-aware; the gap was that foodf/quantum exposed no BusDebug. Extended #[derive(BusDebug)] to infer address width from the map field type (AddressSpace16 vs AddressSpace32 — 32-bit routes addresses untruncated) and to expand #[debug_device] on [T; N] arrays into per-element entries; added AddressSpace32::debug_write parity wrapper. Wired foodf + quantum via derive + impl_standalone_debug!. memory_map() stays 16-bit-only (its return type is &AddressSpace16 and it's unused by the frontend, which reads via peek).

title: Node-level comparison against MAME's discrete netlist
description:
Compare INTERMEDIATE nodes of a discrete circuit against MAME's, not just the
final output.

WHY THIS IS THE HIGHEST-VALUE TOOL LEFT. Every measurement we have looks at the
end of a five-stage chain. When the output is wrong there is no way to tell
which stage is wrong, so the work degenerates into editing constants and
watching one metric improve while another degrades. That is exactly how the
Donkey Kong jump rebuild stalled (…-discrete-sound-fidelity-l5r3.7, commit
7128952): the topology now matches `dkong_a.cpp` stage for stage, yet 98% of our
energy is below 150 Hz where MAME has 2.7%, and the open question — why our
square clears the envelope lid by only 16% when MAME's evidently clears it far
more — cannot be answered from the output alone.

WHAT EXISTS ALREADY:
  - Our side: `sndcmp capture --probe <name>` renders one named node instead of
    the mix (DiscreteCircuit::node_by_name).
  - MAME side: the discrete engine can log named nodes with DISCRETE_CSVLOG and
    DISCRETE_WAVLOG. Nothing in this repo uses them yet.

WHAT IS MISSING: a way to get MAME to dump the nodes we care about, and a
convention mapping their node numbers to our node names, so the two can be put
side by side with `disasm audiodiff`.

SUGGESTED SHAPE:
  1. A small Lua or a documented patch that enables WAVLOG on named nodes for a
     given machine, capturing on the same scenario timeline the gameplay
     drivers already use.
  2. A per-target node map in `sndcmp` — MAME NODE_35 = our JUMP_LID, NODE_38 =
     JUMP_MIX, and so on — so a comparison names circuit intent rather than
     integers on one side and strings on the other.
  3. `sndcmp compare --probe <name>` doing both captures and diffing them.

WORTH DOING BEFORE …-discrete-sound-fidelity-l5r3.7 (`fit`). See that issue for
why the session's evidence argues for reordering.
notes:
UPDATE after the jump rebuild.

Per-node PROBES on our side were added and were decisive: sndcmp capture
--probe over JUMP_CV / JUMP_555 / JUMP_LID / JUMP_MIX / JUMP_INT is what showed
our control voltage sitting on the released level throughout the note, and
later what showed our follower's flat top against the board's rounded one. Half
this facility now exists and paid for itself immediately.

The missing half is the MAME side, and the last open question in the jump —
where the board's rounding between the diode node and the divider comes from —
still has to be argued from the final output. See …-0fbi.

Note DISCRETE_CSVLOG/DISCRETE_WAVLOG are COMPILE-TIME; there is no runtime
option, so this needs a MAME build.

Node map for dkong jump when this is built: NODE_28 = JUMP_CV, NODE_29 =
JUMP_555, NODE_35 = JUMP_LID, NODE_38 = JUMP_MIX, NODE_39 = JUMP_INT.

PREREQUISITE: …-9e1q. A node dump from a reference that ignores its own
timeline is as misleading as an output dump from one, and that is not
hypothetical — it already happened.
close_reason:
Delivered, and it worked the first time it was pointed at a real question.

BOTH SIDES NOW EXIST:
  - Ours: sndcmp capture --probe over named stage nodes (jump-cv/-555/-lid/-mix/-int, stomp-noise/-div/-lid/-mix/-int), scaled by the supply so circuit volts do not saturate a sample.
  - MAME: a mame-nodelog package in the dotfiles repo — stock 0.287 plus one DISCRETE_CSVLOG5 on the jump chain, applied with --replace-fail so a source change breaks the build rather than silently logging nothing. It drops discrete_0.csv with a sample-rate header and one row per sample in raw volts.

Node map for dkong's jump: NODE_28 = JUMP_CV, NODE_29 = JUMP_555, NODE_35 = JUMP_LID, NODE_38 = JUMP_MIX, NODE_39 = JUMP_INT.

WHAT IT BOUGHT, immediately. The jump residual had been blamed on the emitter follower, on the strength of a waveform read off the final OUTPUT — and two independently rebuilt voices seemed to confirm it. One node comparison showed the follower matches (tau ~160 us against our 150) and the 555 matches (duty 65.9 % against 65.4 %), and that the envelope was dipping 0.21 V too shallow. That corrected a wrong diagnosis that would otherwise have sent the next session after the wrong stage, and measuring the lid's own trajectory then gave both its time constant (46.83 ms against the modelled 47.0) and the trigger width driving it (28.4 ms against a derived 26).

NOT BUILT: the sndcmp compare --probe convenience that would run both captures and diff them. Ergonomics rather than capability — the workflow is a MAME run plus disasm audiodiff — so this is closed rather than left open on it. Note DISCRETE_CSVLOG is compile-time and takes at most five nodes, so logging a different set means another MAME build; batch the nodes wanted before rebuilding. NODE_33 and NODE_34 are the ones outstanding, and would settle …-0fbi.

title: Epic: Discrete sound fidelity tooling
description:
A ladder of Rust tooling for making discrete sound demonstrably correct, and for
closing the fit loop without Python and without a rebuild.

Design: docs/designs/discrete-sound-fidelity.md

The design merges two earlier drafts (discrete-sound-fitting.md and
discrete-sound-reference-tooling.md, both deleted) and absorbs
phosphor-emulator-audiodiff-76wx, which had independently arrived at the bottom
two rungs.

WHAT IT BUYS. Today a component value can only be tried by editing
machines/src/<board>_sound.rs and rebuilding, so a three-parameter sweep is a
thousand rebuilds and in practice nobody sweeps. Analysis is Python that needs
numpy and a nix-shell, so it can never gate. The end state is: one Rust command
takes a MAME (or hardware, or other-emulator) WAV and returns fitted component
values; the fit loads straight into the emulator as a tuning.toml with no
rebuild; and landing it is an applicable diff wherever the value is a literal.

THE SIX SETTLED DECISIONS, each of which the two drafts disagreed on:

1. Tuning happens at construction, not by mutating a live circuit. Changing a
   555's timing resistor mid-run has no correct answer for cap integration,
   biquad history, or buffered audio. Construction is cheap next to simulating
   seconds of audio.
2. Parameters have explicit stable IDs, not node-name addresses. The fitting
   draft assumed node names are unique per circuit; push_node enforces nothing,
   and asteroids_sound.rs builds names with format!() so they never appear as
   source literals at all.
3. The Rust tool does not generate or run MAME Lua — the same lesson as the
   `disasm movie mame` revert. Drift is caught by validating the observable
   contract (duration, trigger/release, onset, one-shot vs sustained).
4. The differ lives in disasm (which already writes the WAVs and owns imgdiff);
   shared DSP in phosphor_core::audio::analysis; only the fitting harness is a
   new crate.
5. Volume is three separate questions — normalized shape, absolute dBFS, and
   relative board balance — reported separately so a wrong gain is not
   normalized away.
6. Every parameter is classified Schematic / Model / Calibration, and the class
   governs how a fit result is interpreted.

REFERENCE POLICY. Schematics are the authority; a fit result is a diagnostic,
not a target. Within component tolerance it is a plausible refinement; outside
tolerance it is a bug report, because applying it buries a structural defect
under a fudge factor. The tool is very good at "which of these two plausible
values is right" and structurally unable to answer "what is missing" — which is
what the probes and impulse response exist for.

CEILINGS, stated so nobody chases them: sample equality is impossible and
meaningless (independent seeds/phase; the objective is phase-blind on purpose);
structural gaps cannot be fitted away; op_amp_band_pass maps five schematic
values onto four coefficients and is degenerate by construction; and the MAME
reference is not yet known to be clean (see Phase 0).

Phases land as children below. Each stands on its own if the next is dropped —
Phases 1 and 2 are useful immediately and are not gated on the reference
question at all.

title: Phase 0: Settle whether the MAME reference is clean
description:
Determine MAME 0.287's `-wavwrite` tap point relative to the per-game
`<audio_effects>` chain, define the canonical capture procedure, and recapture
Donkey Kong with the single-trigger protocol.

Design: docs/designs/discrete-sound-fidelity.md — "Reference captures and
provenance", and Phase 0.

WHY FIRST. Asteroids' MAME cfg carries Filters, Compressor, Reverb and Equalizer
on `:mono`, and it is not established whether `-wavwrite` taps the mix before or
after that chain. If after, every reference WAV in tools/sound-reference/
already contains a compressor and an EQ, and fitting component values against it
would be fitting Phosphor to MAME's post-processing rather than to the board.
This answers half of phosphor-emulator-asteroids-sound-postprocessing-hm4.

Needs no code, and nothing in the fitting phases is trustworthy until it lands.
Phases 1-5 are NOT gated on it.

WORK:
- Settle the tap point, from MAME source or by toggling effects and diffing
  captures with the Phase 1 differ once it exists.
- If the tap is post-effects, define how to capture with a cleared chain, so a
  reference is reproducible rather than dependent on whatever is in someone's
  ~/mame/cfg.
- Write the manifest schema (see the design's "Manifest" section): producer and
  version, romset, rate, channels and channel policy, master volume,
  post-processing state, config directory, level_trust, lua_sha256, timeline,
  provenance.
- Recapture DK walk/jump/stomp as ISOLATED single-trigger events. The current
  captures repeatedly retrigger one-shots, so overlapping decays hide the
  envelope and integrated energy of a single event — they cannot answer a decay
  question at all.
- Decide where reference WAVs live (PHOSPHOR_SOUND_REFS, outside the repo by
  default).

RISK: if the tap is post-effects and the chain cannot be cleanly disabled,
references get much harder to produce and Phase 6 may not be worth building.
That is exactly why this is first and cheap.
close_reason: Settled. MAME 0.287 -wavwrite on this install is unaffected by the effects chain: capturing dkong with the default cfg directory and with a clean -cfg_directory produced BYTE-IDENTICAL WAVs (sha256 2ee4f139159948954d734070711ba6ea8d8a77bb4bbc70cffed85b252be75cf5). So the reference carries no compressor/EQ/reverb and is trustworthy as a fitting target; the risk that motivated this phase does not materialise here. Canonical capture: mame dkong -rompath <roms> -nothrottle -seconds_to_run 8 -video none -autoboot_script tools/sound-reference/drive_dkong_sound.lua -wavwrite out.wav, giving 48 kHz mono. Note the first ~1 s is pre-park boot audio at -15.5 dBFS and must be excluded from analysis — it dominated a whole-file comparison until segmented. Effects fire at 1.0/3.0/5.0 s (walk/jump/stomp), each decaying within its window, so the useful windows are 1:2, 3:4 and 5:6. Proven end to end by fitting DK's stomp in adb3e6f.

title: Phase 9: project-wide audit of unmodeled analog audio paths
description:
Sweep every machine for audio the emulator quietly does not model, and put each
finding in the coverage catalog.

Design: docs/designs/discrete-sound-fidelity.md — Phase 9.

The seed table in the design is explicitly "a seed, not a permanent hand-written
claim of completeness". This phase makes it real.

WORK:
- Search every machine and sound board for ignored analog control writes,
  deferred sound paths, and simplified chip-to-speaker routing.
- Review machines that emulate their sound CHIPS correctly but omit board-level
  mixers, coupling capacitors, selectable filters, or output stages — the class
  of gap that is invisible unless someone goes looking, because the chip tests
  all pass.
- Add every finding to tools/sound-compare/targets.toml.
- Add a catalog check to the machine-development checklist, so a new machine
  cannot land with an unmodeled analog path that nobody recorded.
- Keep the README roadmap synchronized with target status.

"All discrete sounds" is complete only when every catalog entry is `validated`
or carries an explicit documented blocker.

Backlog priority deliberately: this is the long tail, and it is worth most after
Phases 7 and 8 have proven the per-target workflow.

title: Phase 1: audio analysis module + disasm audiodiff
description:
Shared DSP in `phosphor_core::audio::analysis`, and `disasm audiodiff` as its
first consumer and the sibling of `disasm imgdiff`.

Design: docs/designs/discrete-sound-fidelity.md — Part 1.
Supersedes item 1 of phosphor-emulator-audiodiff-76wx.

WHY. tools/sound-reference/analyze_wav.py and compare_wav.py work but can never
gate: they need numpy, a nix-shell whose setup takes a README section, and a
human to run them. Everything they measure is arithmetic already done in Rust,
over audio already produced in Rust — `disasm run --audio-out` and
`disasm movie replay --audio-out` both write 16-bit mono WAVs today.

    disasm audiodiff A.wav B.wav [--png spec.png] [--json] [--tolerance ...]

Reports duration/rate, RMS and the gain ratio, DC offset, clipped-sample count,
silent fraction, centroid, flatness, and a band-energy table with deltas. Exits
non-zero past tolerance so it can gate.

BAND DELTAS ARE THE LOAD-BEARING COLUMN: they are scale-invariant, so a pure
gain error leaves them at zero and anything large is a filter, mix or source
difference. That one property separates the four ways a netlist goes wrong.

MODULE CONTENTS: signal integrity (DC, peak dBFS, clipping fraction, crest
factor, leading activity); level and time (AC RMS dBFS, integrated energy, RMS
envelope, attack, T20/T40, duration above threshold); frequency and timbre
(fundamental via spectral + autocorrelation, dominant peaks, centroid, rolloff,
flatness, band ratios, harmonic ratios); distance (multi-resolution log-magnitude
STFT, envelope L1); alignment (onset, envelope cross-correlation).

Pitch combines spectral and autocorrelation estimates — a single largest FFT bin
is unstable for swept tones and noisy resonances. Short arcade effects rarely
have the range for a reliable T60, so several decay summaries beat one number.

MECHANICS: hand-rolled radix-2 FFT (~40 lines, in keeping with a codebase that
hand-rolls a 101-tap FIR and a Bresenham resampler) so core gains no dependency.
Spectrograms need no plotting library: STFT, log magnitude, colormap, then the
existing gfxsheet::write_png — which also composes, since `disasm imgdiff` can
then diff two spectrograms.

Note this part is largely a PORT: compare_wav.py already computes band energy,
centroid, flatness, envelope and spectrogram. The design work is the alignment
and distance layers.

TESTS: synthetic signals with known properties — 1 kHz sine reads centroid ~1000
and flatness ~0, white noise reads flatness -> 1, a known decay reads the right
T20; D(x,x) == 0 and D increases monotonically as a signal is detuned. The
Python version had no tests at all.

OPEN: does the DSP belong in phosphor_core::audio::analysis (proposed — core
already owns AudioResampler, both consumers depend on it, no new dependency) or
in a leaf crate? Core does put offline analysis in the hot-path crate.
close_reason: Landed in a651087 (core::audio::analysis, 40 tests) and 120eaed (disasm audiodiff, 11 tests). Verdict splits differences-between-captures from defects-in-one, which identical-but-broken DK captures showed was necessary. Immediately reproduced …-audio-dc-offset-g7p4: DK DC offset -0.5499 with 100% of energy in the 0-150 Hz band.

title: Phase 2: registry-driven audio sanity test
description:
Boot every machine in registry::all(), capture N frames, and assert the output
is not obviously broken. No MAME, no ROMs, no reference WAV.

Design: docs/designs/discrete-sound-fidelity.md — Part 2.
Supersedes item 2 of phosphor-emulator-audiodiff-76wx.

THE CHEAPEST RUNG IN THE WHOLE EPIC, and the one with the best ratio. Assert:
- |DC| is a small fraction of full scale;
- output is not permanently saturated;
- output is not permanently silent, unless the machine declares it.

This would have caught BOTH halves of phosphor-emulator-audio-dc-offset-g7p4 —
Donkey Kong's DC offset and Joust's saturation — with no reference capture and
no human listening. It is the audio counterpart of golden_frame_test's guards.

FOLLOWS THE EXISTING REGISTRY-SUITE PATTERN: iterate registry::all() so a newly
registered machine is covered without editing the test, plus a
`the_registry_is_not_empty` guard so the file cannot pass vacuously. See
machines/tests/input_contract_test.rs and machines/tests/machine_contract_test.rs.

PROCESS-WIDE RATE: machines/tests/audio_rate_test.rs documents why a test that
touches host_sample_rate needs its own test binary and a LazyLock barrier. Follow
it or avoid touching the rate.

DECLARED SILENCE. Machines that are legitimately silent need an allowance.
`no_audio` no longer exists on the registry, so this introduces the declaration
it needs — per-machine, in the registry, reviewable in a diff, and NOT a
test-local skip list that rots invisibly.

Depends on the analysis module from Phase 1 for DC/saturation/silence
measurement, but is otherwise independent: not gated on the reference question,
not gated on any tuning work.
close_reason: Landed. Found 32 defective machines of 39: 9 with DC/saturation (7 more than …-audio-dc-offset-g7p4 knew about) and 23 emitting nothing at all (filed as …-headless-audio-silent-sweep-pql6). Exceptions are a ratchet — every_known_defect_is_still_present fails when one is fixed, so the list can only shrink.

title: Phase 3: extract discrete coefficient derivations into derive::*
description:
Pull each builder's inlined coefficient math out into free functions in
core/src/device/discrete/derive.rs, with the builders calling them.

Design: docs/designs/discrete-sound-fidelity.md — Part 5, "The derivation
refactor".

PURE REFACTOR, NO BEHAVIOUR CHANGE, and worth doing on its own merits even if
every phase after it is dropped:

- it removes the duplication between rc_low_pass and low_pass_hz, which are two
  spellings of one derivation (mod.rs:378 and mod.rs:397);
- it gives the coefficient math a place to be unit-tested DIRECTLY, rather than
  only through a built circuit's audio output;
- it is the seam Phase 5's tuning needs, since a construction-time override has
  to re-run the same derivation the builder ran.

    pub(crate) fn rc_tau(ohms: f64, farads: f64) -> f64 { ohms * farads }

    pub(crate) fn ne555_astable_coeffs(r1: f64, r2: f64, c: f64, dt: f64) -> (f64, f64) {
        (1.0 - (-dt / ((r1 + r2) * c)).exp(),
         1.0 - (-dt / (r2 * c)).exp())
    }

Derivations that depend on dt (ne555_astable, rc_disc5, op_amp_band_pass) read
sim_rate off the builder, which already stores it.

ACCEPTANCE: extracted functions reproduce the current inline math bit-for-bit;
existing discrete tests and golden frames are unchanged. This touches working
audio code, so bit-identical output is the bar, not "sounds the same".
close_reason: Landed in 2587022. All nine derivations extracted to core/src/device/discrete/derive.rs with 16 direct tests; rc_low_pass and low_pass_hz collapsed onto one derivation. Bit-identical verified rather than assumed: 600-frame dkong and galaxian audio captures byte-identical before/after, golden frames green. Surfaced phosphor-emulator-ne555-astable-ideal-rc-flat-9sjg (astable runs 3.4% flat vs the datasheet constant).

title: Phase 4: sound-compare crate, scenarios, capture, probes
description:
New workspace member tools/sound-compare (crate phosphor-sound-compare, binary
`sndcmp`): the scenario schema, the Donkey Kong adapter, capture/compare/
validate-reference, and the probe facilities.

Design: docs/designs/discrete-sound-fidelity.md — Parts 3 and 4.
Supersedes item 3 (per-voice solo) and item 4 (impulse response) of
phosphor-emulator-audiodiff-76wx.

USEFUL WITH NO PARAMETER SEARCH AT ALL. This is the phase that retires the
triplicated timeline.

SCENARIOS replace three hand-synced copies of the segment boundaries (the Lua,
the capture example's apply(), and analyze_wav.py's SEGMENTS list — nothing
checks them against each other, so a drifted window silently compares our
explosion against MAME's thump). One TOML per isolated effect, describing
hardware intent rather than emulator methods or MAME addresses. Explicit events,
not per-frame callbacks, so trigger edges are exact and independent of any
producer's frame rate.

ISOLATED EFFECTS ARE THE FITTING UNIT: sustained effects get a clear enable and
release, one-shots are triggered once and allowed to decay completely. Repeated
pulses are fine for listening and useless for fitting.

ADAPTERS: one small SoundTargetFactory/SoundTarget per target rather than a
universal "write register" trait, which would erase useful intent and still fail
to cover external DAC/PSG streams. The adapter owns board-specific timing —
Asteroids/Lunar Lander translate elapsed time to board CPU cycles, Galaxian
advances its fixed internal sim from main-CPU cycles, DK advances once per
output/DAC sample holding the DAC baseline. The scenario layer never imports
concrete machine types.

PROBES, in increasing power:
1. PER-VOICE SOLO RENDER — render one node to its own WAV instead of the mix.
   The difference between "our dkong sounds wrong" and "our dkong walk voice's
   RC decay is too fast". DiscreteCircuit::value(node) already exposes any
   node's value, so this is construction with the probe as an alternate output.
2. NAMED PROBES — a curated set per device with IDs describing circuit intent so
   they survive local topology changes. Curated, not every internal node
   promoted to stable API.
3. IMPULSE / STEP RESPONSE — the only measurement that cleanly separates a
   SOURCE error (LFSR taps, divider, envelope shape) from a FILTER error (RC
   corner, Q, order). A spectral diff of mixed output fundamentally cannot,
   because both move the same bands.

ANALYSIS RATE IS NOT THE REFERENCE'S RATE. Capture at a canonical rate and
resample the reference to meet it, reusing phosphor_core::audio::AudioResampler.
Constructing the circuit at whatever rate the reference WAV carries would change
the model under test — dkong_sound.rs builds board = sim = output = host rate by
construction, so for the first target this is not hypothetical.

ALIGNMENT: envelope cross-correlation within a bound from the declared trigger,
shifting only for analysis and reporting the offset as a metric. Waveform
cross-correlation is never used for noise-heavy effects — it would reward seed
and phase coincidence rather than circuit fidelity.

Delete machines/examples/dkong_capture.rs. Depends on Phase 1 (analysis).
close_reason: Landed in 09fcd96. tools/sound-compare (sndcmp) with the scenario schema, the DK adapter, three isolated DK scenarios, and per-voice solo render via DiscreteCircuit::node_by_name. 21 tests. Probes corrected a live reading immediately: walk's fundamental reads 376.9 Hz solo vs 551 Hz in the mix (MAME 338), so walk is 11% high, not 63%. Also showed the adb3e6f stomp fit was measured against a repeated-pulse MAME window — an isolated trigger is 2.97 dB quieter, so level/decay need a single-trigger reference. Not done here: validate-reference/manifests, impulse response, and deleting machines/examples/dkong_capture.rs (still the only thing driving the old 7s multi-effect timeline the current MAME reference matches).

title: Phase 5: TuningContext, tuning.toml overrides, sensitivity
description:
Construction-time parameter tuning, the override file that removes the rebuild
from the loop, and sensitivity ranking.

Design: docs/designs/discrete-sound-fidelity.md — Part 5 and Part 6
("Baseline and sensitivity before any optimization").

THE PROBLEM. Builder methods collapse their arguments on the way in:
rc_low_pass stores tau = ohms*farads (R and C individually lost), ne555_astable
stores two exponentials from three unknowns, op_amp_band_pass stores four biquad
coefficients that do not determine rf/c1/c2 at all. So a coefficient-space
result is unusable as a recommendation AND less constrained than reality, since
real boards are built from preferred-value parts. Tune in schematic space, in
the units written at the call site.

CONSTRUCTION, NOT LIVE MUTATION. The earlier draft proposed set_param on a built
circuit; rejected, because it has no correct answer for whether a 555 restarts,
whether biquad history stays valid, or what happens to buffered audio. Every
candidate is: resolve overrides -> construct fresh -> reset -> run -> drain ->
score -> drop. Construction is trivially cheap next to simulating seconds of
audio.

EXPLICIT IDS, NOT NODE NAMES. push_node enforces no uniqueness whatsoever, and
asteroids_sound.rs builds names with format!("{name}_AC") so they never appear
as source literals. Explicit IDs also keep parameter identity stable across
topology refactors, keep meaningless values out of the search space, and let
bounds/tolerance/class live beside the value.

ParameterSpec carries: id, label, unit, class (Schematic|Model|Calibration),
default, bounds, tolerance, scale, preferred_series, source (#[track_caller]),
and writeback (Literal|Derived, from stringify! of the value expression — see
Phase 6).

THE ROUND-TRIP KILLER, and the reason this is its own phase rather than part of
`fit`: TuningOverrides deserializes from TOML, and any consumer that builds a
machine can pass one in — sndcmp, disasm, and the frontend behind an explicit
--tuning flag. A value can then be explored by hand, on the real board against
the real music, with NO REBUILD, before any optimizer exists.

GUARDS, because a stray tuning file silently altering emulation would be worse
than the problem it solves: opt-in only (no implicit lookup, no env var that can
linger in a shell), a loud banner at startup and in the debug overlay, and
provenance in the file so a stale fit applied to a changed scenario is visible.

SENSITIVITY BEFORE OPTIMIZATION. Perturb each parameter around its default and
report which metric families move and in which direction. The ranking is itself
a recommendation — it says which part of the model can plausibly explain the
error, before anyone spends evaluations.

NO HOT-LOOP COST: TuningContext exists only during construction; resolved
scalars land in the same node fields the emulator already uses. Verify with
`cargo run --release -p phosphor-bench` before and after.

Depends on Phase 3 (derive) and Phase 4 (crate/adapters).
close_reason:
NOT BUILDING THIS. It exists to serve the fitting loop, and the branch concluded
that fitting is the wrong tool for this problem. See the close reason on
phosphor-emulator-discrete-sound-fidelity-l5r3.7 for the evidence; in short,
every value ever fitted on this branch was later deleted, and each turned out to
be standing in for a mechanism that was missing from the model.

Taking the three pieces separately, because they are not equally obsolete:

TUNING.TOML OVERRIDES, to take the rebuild out of the loop. Obsolete. The loop
it was speeding up was value iteration, and the loop we actually run is
"understand the topology, express it, rebuild". A cargo build of the affected
crates is about a minute, which is nothing against reading a netlist. Worse, an
override file makes it easy to keep a value alive without a part behind it,
which is the exact failure this branch spent two sessions learning to avoid.

TUNINGCONTEXT AND EXPLICIT PARAMETER IDS. Obsolete as specified, but the
reasoning behind it was right and was absorbed rather than lost. The problem it
named, that builder methods collapse their arguments so a coefficient-space
result cannot be turned back into a component, is real. The answer that stuck is
simpler than a parameter registry: keep the schematic values at the call site as
literals with the part designator in a comment, so the code reads as the board.
galaxian_sound.rs and dkong_sound.rs both do this now, and it is what made the
melody's mixer weights checkable against the netlist by eye.

SENSITIVITY RANKING. This is the piece with independent worth, and it is the one
to bring back first if any of this is revisited. "No exposed parameter materially
improves the score" is a structural signal, not a fitting step, and it is in the
Structural diagnosis table on its own merits. It was not needed here only because
the cheaper test kept working: can I point at the part on the schematic? The
design text stays in the doc.

Nothing about the reference policy, the probes or the scenarios is affected;
those are Phases 0 to 4 and they are what did the work.

title: Phase 6: sndcmp fit and writeback; correct Donkey Kong
description:
The optimizer, the write-back path that closes the loop, and the first real use:
diagnosing Donkey Kong's walk/jump/stomp from reference evidence.

Design: docs/designs/discrete-sound-fidelity.md — Part 6, "What is automatic,
end to end", and Decision 7.

GATED ON PHASE 0 having concluded the reference is clean.

OBJECTIVE — three reported components, never one unexplained score:
  shape_score     phase-insensitive spectral/timbre difference
  envelope_score  aligned attack/decay difference
  level_score     raw level/energy difference, when provenance is trusted
The aggregate is a documented weighted sum used for RANKING, not the only
evidence shown. shape_score is multi-resolution log-magnitude STFT distance over
w in {256, 1024, 4096}: phase-blind, because two independent emulators are never
sample-aligned and their noise never correlates sample-for-sample — any
time-domain distance measures alignment, not timbre.

SEARCH LADDER: 1 param bounded grid + refinement; 2 coarse grid + pattern
search; 3-4 multi-start derivative-free in normalized coords; more than 4,
refuse and ask for a smaller hypothesis. Log space for ohms/farads/Hz/seconds.

PREFERRED VALUES: a continuous optimum of 8.2431e-3 ohm-farad is not a
recommendation. Re-score at E6/E12/E24 and report all four of continuous
optimum, nearest realizable, score at realizable, and schematic compatibility.
A snapped score much worse than the continuous one means a narrow minimum, which
is itself a finding.

IDENTIFIABILITY, all reported: condition number of the local Hessian estimate;
pairwise sensitivity correlation; warnings when many combinations score nearly
equally or the optimum sits on a bound; and hold-out across effects sharing a
node (Asteroids thrust/explosion share NOISE; a DK shared output or DAC
parameter fitted on jump must be re-scored on walk and stomp).

WRITE-BACK — Decision 7, and the half that removes the retyping:
- Every fit writes a tuning.toml (--out-tuning) the emulator loads directly, so
  the result is audible on the real board with no rebuild and no source edit.
- `sndcmp writeback FIT.toml [--apply]` lands the values whose registration site
  is a float LITERAL — either a module-scope const or a literal argument. In
  dkong_sound.rs nearly every tunable is already `const WALK_C: f64 = 33e-9;`,
  so the common case is the automatic one.
- A DERIVED value (LVL_EXPLOSION / LVL_TOTAL, 18_432_000.0 / 6.0 / 2.0, v1 - v0)
  is refused with the expression named and a suggestion of which term to edit.
  Pasting a fitted float over a ratio silently decouples it from its
  denominator.
- Values the reference policy rejects — out of tolerance, ill-conditioned,
  degrading a hold-out — are never written, with or without --apply. --apply
  lands what the report already recommended; it is not a policy override.

DONKEY KONG. Diagnose each effect from evidence; PREFER TOPOLOGY FIXES TO
IMPLAUSIBLE SCALAR FITS. The current jump and stomp custom components are model
hypotheses, not protected implementations — if their probe shapes disagree with
the reference, the right result is a new topology, not new constants. Validate
the three effects together for relative level, and add a mixed full-machine
scenario for effect-to-DAC balance (DAC_GAIN = 0.55 and STOMP_GAIN = 7.0 are
calibration values, fittable only once absolute level is trusted).

THE CI TEST THAT NEEDS NO MAME: capture the default model, construct another
with one deliberately wrong exposed parameter, fit against the default capture,
assert recovery within tolerance. Separate tests use deliberately wrong waveform
or envelope STRUCTURE and assert the fitter refuses to claim a trustworthy
schematic recommendation.

EXPECT op_amp_band_pass TO BE ILL-CONDITIONED: five schematic parameters onto
four coefficients is degenerate by construction. Fitting rf alone with c1/c2
pinned is the realistic use. The tool must say so rather than return confident
numbers.
close_reason:
NOT BUILDING THIS. The branch answered the question this phase existed to answer,
and the answer was that the optimizer is the wrong tool.

Its stated first real use was "diagnosing Donkey Kong's walk/jump/stomp from
reference evidence". All three were diagnosed and corrected, and so were the
music voice and all three Galaxian voices, without any of it. What did the work
every time: read the reference topology, model what is there, probe per stage,
compare against a reference proved to respond to its own timeline.

The evidence against fitting is not a preference, it is the branch's record:

  - Every value ever fitted on this branch was later deleted. Donkey Kong
    carried four fitted filter corners; not one had a part on the schematic, and
    each was standing in for a missing mechanism (a divide-by-eight counter, an
    oscillator that chops rather than multiplies, an absolute-volts lid, an
    undriven decay circuit). Galaxian carried a 0.8 output trim and a 1.25x hit
    lift; both came out when the melody's mixer weights were corrected.
  - Fitting made the output measure better while the model got further from the
    board. A stomp gain fitted against overlapping decays, a walk pitch fitted
    against a hold the game never produces, a wobble oscillator deleted because
    its variation looked like noise. Each had to be undone.
  - The test that actually worked is free: "can I point at the part?" The design
    doc records that it never gave a false answer here, and it is faster than
    any spectral comparison.

An optimizer would have found excellent values for every one of those wrong
models. That is the failure mode, and building a tool whose output is a fitted
scalar would institutionalise it.

WHAT REPLACES IT, all already built and used: sndcmp probes for per-stage
comparison, disasm audiodiff for scoring, verify-reference.sh for proving a
reference is an experiment, and DISCRETE_CSVLOG node dumps for localising a
residual to a stage. The objective function described here (shape, envelope and
level reported separately, never one aggregate) was worth specifying and is what
audiodiff reports.

IF THIS IS EVER REVISITED, the preferred-value snapping and the identifiability
analysis are the parts with independent worth, and the design text stays in the
doc for that. The optimizer itself should not be built until there is a residual
that has survived a node dump and a schematic reading, which has not happened
yet on either board.

title: Phase 7: migrate remaining implemented discrete devices
description:
Bring the already-implemented discrete devices onto the same workflow, and
retire the Python rig entirely.

Design: docs/designs/discrete-sound-fidelity.md — Phase 7 and "Coverage catalog".

Mechanical once Donkey Kong sets the pattern. In order:
1. Congo Bongo percussion — including comparison against MAME's sample playback
   and any available original sample recordings, which is a different reference
   kind than the others and exercises the design's claim that the tool does not
   care where a WAV came from.
2. Galaxian and the shared Galaxian-family sound board.
3. Asteroids.
4. Lunar Lander.
5. Donkey Kong Jr. — shares the TKG-04 board/device seam but has a different
   sound program and control usage, so it gets its own scenarios once the DK
   device model is corrected.
6. Moon Cresta-family scenarios that differ from Galaxian.

PER TARGET: catalog entry and isolated scenarios; an adapter; registered
parameters and probes; established references with provenance; diagnose and fix;
Rust-only regression coverage; marked `validated` only after schematic review.

COVERAGE CATALOG (tools/sound-compare/targets.toml) lands here as the reviewed
inventory, so a newly discovered or newly added discrete path cannot quietly
drop out of the plan. Statuses: missing, partial, implemented-unvalidated,
implemented-needs-validation, validated, blocked (reason required). Tests assert
unique IDs, that referenced scenarios exist, that implemented adapters have
entries, that cataloged scenarios name valid controls, and that a target cannot
regress from validated without a visible data change. `sndcmp targets` prints
it, making the project-wide plan visible from the CLI.

DELETIONS when the last board migrates: tools/sound-reference/analyze_wav.py,
and the remaining machines/examples/*_capture.rs binaries (asteroid, llander,
galaxian, xevious — xevious has a capture example and no Lua counterpart at all
today). compare_wav.py stops being the documented path but may stay for
exploratory one-offs, where iterating is faster.

REGRESSION CONTRACT: AC rather than raw RMS for audibility, pitch/envelope/
energy ranges, absence of clipping or unexpected DC, deterministic output for a
fixed scenario, reset and save/load continuation, relative effect levels. Exact
PCM hashes may be useful diagnostics but must NOT be the only contract — a
shared resampler improvement can legitimately change every sample while
improving the sound.

title: Phase 8: build the missing discrete paths with the tooling in hand
description:
Implement the discrete audio that does not exist yet, using the comparison
tooling DURING construction rather than retrofitting it afterwards.

Design: docs/designs/discrete-sound-fidelity.md — Phase 8.

These targets benefit most from the tooling existing first: construction can
proceed against isolated measurements and schematic stages, instead of producing
a plausible sound and tuning it later. This is the first use of the tooling for
construction rather than debugging.

1. Asteroids Deluxe explosion/latch paths mixed with its POKEYs. Register writes
   are currently stubbed; the POKEYs work.
2. Mario Bros. Mario/Luigi walk and skid paths mixed with its DAC. Explicitly
   deferred today.
3. Namco 54XX (MB8844) digital output plus the analog DAC/filter/mixer for
   Galaga and the Xevious family — see phosphor-emulator-uxi9 and
   phosphor-emulator-pd5e. Commands sent via 06XX chip-select 3 are discarded
   today and explosions are silent. The DAC ladder and op-amp filter values can
   be fitted AS THEY ARE WRITTEN.
4. Konami Scramble/Frogger discrete output-filter controls. Filter control is
   latched but not modeled.

Each follows the Phase 7 per-target checklist: catalog entry, isolated
scenarios, adapter, registered parameters and probes, references with
provenance, Rust-only regression coverage, and `validated` only after schematic
review.

title: Discrete sound device framework (v1: Asteroids, Lunar Lander, Donkey Kong)
description:
Reusable framework for discrete / board-level analog sound paths, per docs/designs/discrete-sound-framework.md.

Replaces ad-hoc per-board discrete sound (currently: DkongDiscrete synthesizes finished 44.1kHz PCM and is mixed AFTER resampling, bypassing the board analog path; Asteroids and Lunar Lander discrete writes are stubbed under no_audio) with a typed Rust circuit graph: contiguous Vec<Node> enum + Node::Custom escape hatch, topo-sorted evaluation with one-step-delay back-edges for feedback, per-component clock domains, AudioResampler output, Saveable/Debuggable integration.

v1 scope = framework + three migrations. Order (Asteroids first to de-risk the framework on simpler latch/data-driven Atari boards before DK's harder shared-analog mixer):
  1. Framework skeleton + evaluation model
  2. Mixer and filter primitives
  3. Asteroids migration (first real consumer)
  4. Lunar Lander migration
  5. Donkey Kong migration

Follow-ons (DK Jr., Mario Bros., Asteroids Deluxe, Namco 54XX) are out of v1 scope and tracked separately.
close_reason: v1 complete. Built a reusable discrete-sound framework (core/src/device/discrete/: typed-handle builder -> DiscreteCircuit, Vec<Node> enum + Custom escape hatch, topo-sorted eval with one-step back-edges, per-component clock domains, mixer/filter primitives) and migrated all three v1 boards onto it, each verified against MAME 0.287 with a capture-and-compare rig (tools/sound-reference): Asteroids (l7o.3), Lunar Lander (l7o.4), Donkey Kong (l7o.5). The rig + case study (docs/debugging-asteroids-discrete-sound.md) caught multiple bugs ears missed (write_d7 latch, XNOR DC-lock, level/balance/headroom). Follow-ups tracked separately: hm4 (MAME output post-processing / thrust rumble); DK fidelity + DK Jr. reuse noted in l7o.5.

title: Discrete sound: framework skeleton + evaluation model
description:
Phase 1. Add core/src/device/discrete/.

- DiscreteCircuitBuilder + typed handles (LogicInputId/DataInputId/PulseInputId/ExternalSourceId/NodeId).
- DiscreteCircuit runtime: contiguous Vec<Node> enum over the v1 primitive set + a single Node::Custom(Box<dyn CustomComponent>) escape-hatch variant. Static dispatch for common primitives; box fat per-variant state.
- Evaluation model: topological sort at build(); per-node output-slot value array (Vec<f64>); cycle detection (DFS) cutting back-edges read with one-step delay; same held-slot mechanism provides cross-clock-domain sample-and-hold.
- DiscreteScheduler with per-component clock domains (BoardCycle / FixedFrequency / OutputSample / EventOnly); dt-based analog state.
- Basic input/source/math primitives (logic/data/pulse inputs, edge detector, fixed/variable square, LFSR noise, gain/add/multiply/clamp).
- AudioResampler integration to mono i16.
- Saveable: include node output slots (held + back-edge state); versioned.
- Unit tests for deterministic primitives (LFSR, square phase/freq, save/load round-trip).

No board migration in this phase.
close_reason: Implemented in core/src/device/discrete/ (mod.rs, node.rs, tests.rs): typed-handle builder -> DiscreteCircuit, Vec<Node> enum + Node::Custom escape hatch, topo-sorted evaluation with one-step-delay back-edges, per-component clock domains, input/source/math primitives + LFSR noise, AudioResampler<i16> output, versioned Saveable with node output slots. 14 unit tests pass; clippy + fmt clean.

title: Discrete sound: mixer and filter primitives
description:
Phase 2. Analog approximation primitives on top of the skeleton.

- RC charge/discharge (envelope), RC low-pass, RC high-pass / coupling cap.
- First-order and second-order filters (band-pass, Sallen-Key-style approximation).
- Resistor mixer (with optional pull-up/down/load), diode mixer (configurable forward drop/threshold), DAC / resistor ladder.
- External source input node (accept samples from existing chip/DAC devices).
- Per-primitive unit tests: RC approaches target within tolerance, filter step-response sanity, mixer scaling, diode threshold, DAC monotonicity/endpoints, external-source sample handling, save/load.
close_reason: Implemented analog primitives in core/src/device/discrete/: RC low-pass, RC high-pass/coupling, asymmetric RC envelope (charge/discharge), Chamberlin state-variable 2nd-order filter (low/band/high-pass), passive resistor mixer (weighted-average + optional load), diode-OR mixer (max minus forward drop), and R-2R/weighted DAC ladder. External-source node already present from skeleton; added builder methods, eval/reset/save-load, and FilterMode. 10 new unit tests (24 total in module); clippy + fmt clean.

title: Asteroids: migrate discrete sound to the framework (first consumer)
description:
Phase 3. First real migration — validates latch-driven + data-driven inputs and de-risks the framework before DK.

Add AsteroidsDiscreteSound (circuit + AsteroidsDiscreteInputs) and wire the currently-stubbed bus writes:
- 0x3600 explosion: bits 2-5 volume/data; bits 6-7 pitch divider (MAME-observed 00->12, 01->6, 10->3, 11->5 — verify against schematic).
- 0x3A00 thump: bit 4 enable; low nibble DAC data.
- 0x3C00..=0x3C07 addressable audio latch: saucer enable/fire/select, thrust, ship fire, life.
- 0x3E00 noise reset pulse.

Signal paths: thump DAC ladder->555/filter; saucer VCO/warble/filter; fire decay-square/filter; thrust LFSR->band/low-pass; explosion sampled-noise->RC; life 3kHz square -> output mix -> gain.

Remove no_audio from AsteroidsSystem; route AudioSource through the device. Saveable + Debuggable (SAUCER/THRUST/THUMP_DATA/EXPLODE_PITCH/NOISE_LFSR ...). Tests: mapping of each write, noise reset pulse, audio drains after a frame, save/load.

Added a triangle-wave primitive to the framework for the saucer. Documented in docs/debugging-asteroids-discrete-sound.md. Remaining low-end-rumble polish tracked in phosphor-emulator-asteroids-sound-postprocessing-hm4. Tests/clippy/fmt green.

title: Lunar Lander: migrate discrete sound to the framework
description:
Phase 4. Compact register-driven circuit; reuses Atari noise/latch primitives established by the Asteroids migration.

Add LunarLanderDiscreteSound and wire stubs:
- 0x3C00 sound register: bits 0-2 thrust volume; bit 3 explosion enable; bit 4 3kHz tone enable; bit 5 6kHz tone enable.
- 0x3E00 noise reset pulse.

Circuit: 12kHz LFSR noise -> RC filter -> thrust gain (3-bit) -> band/low-pass; explosion gate; 3kHz and 6kHz fixed tones; final mix + output filter/gain.

Remove no_audio from LunarLanderSystem. Saveable + Debuggable. Tests: register mapping, noise reset, tone-only deterministic non-silent output, thrust/explosion non-silent, save/load.

New machines/src/llander_sound.rs (LunarLanderDiscreteSound) models MAME's llander_discrete netlist: a shared resettable 12kHz XNOR LFSR (Custom LanderNoise) -> RC LP -> band-passed thrust + unfiltered explosion (which reuses the 3-bit thrust value as its volume) -> 560Hz LP, plus fixed 3kHz/6kHz alert tones. Wired 0x3C00 sound register + 0x3E00 noise reset in llander.rs; replaced no_audio with a hand AudioSource; tick per frame; reset; Saveable+Debuggable; 5 tests.
