title: The golden-frame comparison is #[ignore]d; the reason it names is closed
description:
golden_frame_test::every_pinned_machine_still_draws_its_frame, the only test in
the tree that compares what a machine draws against a committed pin, is
#[ignore]d. The reason it names has been resolved for two days.

Its ignore message:

  disabled while the vector renderer is being reworked (phosphor-emulator-ukgy);
  re-enable or retire it once its utility has been reviewed

phosphor-emulator-ukgy closed on 2026-08-25: "All five filed stages closed."

CONSEQUENCE, AND IT IS THE SHAPE THIS REPOSITORY KEEPS TRIPPING OVER. A plain

  PHOSPHOR_ROMS=... cargo test -p phosphor-harness --test golden_frame_test

reports "11 passed; 0 failed; 1 ignored" in about 1.4 seconds without comparing a
single frame. Everything it does run is metadata: that frames.toml covers the
registry, that the reference PNGs match their hashes, that a movie entry round
trips. The eleven green results look exactly like a golden-frame suite passing.
Anyone following CLAUDE.md's instruction to "run it after any rendering,
palette, video-timing or CPU change" gets a green tick and no comparison.

The machinery still works. Forcing it with `-- --ignored` and scoping with
PHOSPHOR_GOLDEN_ONLY compares normally; I did that for marble and roadrunner
while verifying phosphor-emulator-xvz6 and both matched their pins in about five
seconds each.

WHAT TO DO, AND THE DECISION IS NOT MINE. The ignore message defers to a review
of the test's utility, which is phosphor-emulator-gr27, still open. So there are
two honest outcomes and one dishonest one:

- Re-enable it. The vector rework that motivated the disable is done, and if
  some vector pins are stale they should be recaptured and reviewed by eye,
  which is the documented procedure.
- Retire it deliberately under gr27, delete the pins, and say in CLAUDE.md that
  nothing checks what a machine draws.
- Leave it as it is, which is the dishonest one: the suite keeps reporting green
  and CLAUDE.md keeps telling people it is the check that would notice a machine
  drawing the wrong picture.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND ITSELF. The conformance-ROM epic
(phosphor-emulator-conformance-rom-programme-hl4t) is built on the premise that
golden frames carry two jobs and do one of them well. Right now they carry
neither, so the epic's argument for what conformance ROMs replace should be read
against that. gr27 is the issue that owns the question and predates all of it.

Found while verifying phosphor-emulator-xvz6.

title: Review whether the golden frame comparison earns its keep
description:
every_pinned_machine_still_draws_its_frame is #[ignore]d while the vector renderer is reworked (phosphor-emulator-ukgy). The other five tests in the file stay live: they guard the data file, the coverage of the registry, and that a hand-edited hash fails without ROMs.

The question to answer before re-enabling: what has it actually caught, versus what it has cost in recaptures. Two data points from the session that disabled it. It caught nothing about the i32 flip overflow, because the beam only leaves the screen in situations the pinned frame does not reach. It then demanded a recapture of all three vector machines for the incremental-generator change, where two of the three differences were an animation phase and the third was a different attract level from a moved RNG seed, none of which is a rendering regression.

Worth considering whether the vectors hash alone is the better pin for the vector machines, since it is renderer-independent and is what the frontend actually draws, and whether the frame hash belongs only to the raster machines.

Re-enable, narrow, or retire.

comments.author: pjl
comments.text: Related: phosphor-emulator-conformance-rom-programme-hl4t proposes conformance ROMs as the timing oracle, which bears directly on the 're-enable, narrow, or retire' decision here. The argument made there: golden frames carry two jobs and only do one well. They pin artwork (tile and sprite decode, palette derivation from PROMs, orientation, ROM loading), which nothing else in the tree does. They also stand in as the only guard against timing regressions, which they do badly, because a timing change and an attract-loop phase change are indistinguishable in a hash. That is exactly the failure mode recorded above: three vector recaptures where two were an animation phase and one a moved RNG seed. A conformance ROM can take the second job because its expected output is derived rather than captured. It cannot take the first. So the answer to this issue is probably 'narrow' rather than 'retire', but the narrowing is only safe once the replacement exists for a given board.

title: Epic: Graphics consolidation — remaining cleanups
description:
Design: docs/designs/graphics-consolidation.md (rev 2)

Four independent, well-scoped cleanups left over from the graphics consolidation
work. No shared design, no ordering between them, each one commit, each
frameshot-validated. Grouped only so they do not get lost — the same reason the
contained-fidelity epic exists.

CONTEXT. Rev 1 audited the render path across ~40 machines and proposed four
consolidations; Features 1, 2a and 2c are done, Feature 3 is done and correctly
stopped at two machines, Feature 4 is done bar one housing detail. Seven machines
migrated onto the shared helpers.

What rev 1 got wrong was the SIZE OF THE ADDRESSABLE SET. It assumed the
remaining hand-rollers were blocked by missing helper features. Having built
those features, the honest answer for most of them is that their renderers are
STRUCTURALLY DIFFERENT, not feature-poor — per-column independent vertical scroll
(galaxian_video), per-pixel whole-frame loops into a u16 pen buffer (mrdo),
dirty-gated per-tile rendering at 2x upscale (mcr2), a u16 index buffer plus
per-tile GfxCache selection (atari_system1). Rev 2 makes an explicit per-machine
call on each so the migration stops at the right place instead of drifting into
contorting helpers.

Net remaining work is these four items. Everything else is closed by decision,
not left open.

ACCEPTANCE BAR FOR ALL FOUR: pixel-identical. These are pure refactors, so a
changed golden hash is a bug and MUST NOT be recaptured to make a migration pass.

title: Migrate congo_bongo fg tilemap to render_tilemap_scanline
description:
Migrate congo_bongo's foreground tilemap (congo_bongo.rs:970) to
core::gfx::render_tilemap_scanline.

THE ONE CLEAN REMAINING FIT among the hand-rolled tilemap renderers. It is
already per-scanline, 32 columns of 8x8, doing tiles.pixel(code, px, py) plus a
palette lookup with pixel-0 transparency — which is exactly the shape the
enriched RGB helper takes after Feature 2a (TileInfo with flip_x/flip_y,
resolve_color_fn returning Option<(u8,u8,u8)> for transparency). fg_bank and
pal_offset capture into the closures.

Its sprites already go through draw_sprite_row, so this finishes the board.

Acceptance: golden frame byte-identical (frameshot-compare before/after);
cargo test -p phosphor-machines green.

title: Decide foodf: migrate onto the scrolled helper, or delete it
description:
Decide foodf: either migrate foodf.rs:740 onto
core::gfx::render_scrolled_tilemap_scanline, or DELETE that helper. Do these two
together or not at all — do not leave it unused.

render_scrolled_tilemap_scanline (the non-indexed variant) has ZERO production
callers. Only its _indexed sibling is used, by xevious. It was built on spec as
the RGB sibling of a helper that turned out to only be needed in indexed form.

foodf is the one plausible adopter: its column-scan tile order (col * rows + row)
expresses fine in tile_info_fn, and its -8 scroll is what the scrolled helper
exists for. If the migration is clean, it retires the dead helper by giving it a
caller. If it is not, delete the helper — an unused helper is worse than no
helper, because the next person assumes it is exercised.

RELATED CLOSED DECISION worth honouring here: new gfx helpers land with their
first caller in the same commit. Both unused helpers in the codebase came from
building a sibling on spec, and this issue is the cleanup for one of them.

Acceptance: either foodf's golden frame is byte-identical and the helper has a
caller, or the helper is gone. Not neither.

title: Decide compute_resistor_net: delete or document as a reference model
description:
Decide core::gfx::compute_resistor_net (resistor.rs:63): DELETE it, or state in
the module docs that it is deliberately kept as a reference model.

Zero production callers; exercised only by its own unit tests. Rev 1 proposed
expressing the DK-family Darlington DAC through it; that did not happen, because
compute_tkg04_channel models the TTL output stage itself rather than a generic
resistor network.

Either outcome is fine. What is not fine is leaving a tested-but-uncalled helper
with no note, because it reads as production code that simply has not been
adopted yet — which is what caused it to be built in the first place.

Acceptance: `sak fs grep compute_resistor_net core machines` shows either nothing
outside its own tests plus a module-doc note explaining why, or nothing at all.

title: Move compute_tkg04_channel into gfx::resistor, dropping the cross-machine import
description:
Move compute_tkg04_channel from machines/src/tkg04.rs:103 into
core/src/gfx/resistor.rs, dropping the machine-to-machine dependency.

mario_bros.rs:46 currently imports it ACROSS MACHINES — mario_bros depends on
tkg04 for a palette DAC model, even though rev 2 established that Mario Bros does
not share the TKG-04 board at all (it has its own board and Z80 DMA, and shares
only the palette model). That import is the last trace of the wrong assumption.

The deduplication was the important half and it already happened; this is the
housing. One commit, low priority, but it removes a dependency edge that will
confuse the next person to read either file.

Acceptance: no machines/src file imports from another machines/src file for this;
golden frames byte-identical for dkong, dkongjr and mariobros.

title: Epic: Graphics rendering consolidation
description:
Raise adoption of the sound-but-under-used shared gfx helpers (core/src/gfx/) and delete near-identical hand-rolled renderers. Design: ~/graphics-consolidation.md. Acceptance bar: pixel-identical output, validated per-machine with disasm frameshot --compare.

Verified against code: shared helpers exist as described; render_tilemap_scanline is opaque/no-flip/(u16,u8) with exactly 3 callers (so 2a enrichment is low-blast-radius); tilemap_offset is byte-identical across galaga/digdug/namco_pac. Corrections found during verification — apply when scoping: (a) compute_tkg04_channel is ALREADY shared (mario_bros imports it, not a copy) so Feature 4 is smaller than the doc claims; (b) galaxian resnet_raw_weights is closer to compute_resistor_net than compute_resistor_weights; (c) draw_sprite_row has 4 core callers not 5-6; (d) render_tilemap is galaga-only (digdug/xevious name it render_background).

Phases: (1) palette resistor-DAC dedup [lowest risk]; (2a) enrich RGB tilemap helper (TileInfo+flip+Option transparency, 3 callers); (1-unify) Namco galaga/digdug/xevious renderers; (3) bitmap-scanline helper; (2b) indexed+priority variants [largest lift]; (2c) fix galaxian draw_sprite_row shadowing. Phases individually shippable; 1-2a are pure wins with tiny blast radius.
close_reason: Delivered the shared gfx scanline substrate and migrated every machine that fits pixel-identically. SHIPPED: palette DAC (pal_nbit, compute_resnet_weights); RGB + indexed + scroll-aware tilemap scanline helpers (TileInfo+flip+Option transparency); bitmap-scanline helper; sprite helpers (RGB + indexed); namco_tilemap_offset dedup. MIGRATED (all frameshot 0.0%): burgertime/shollow/galaxian palette, pacman/dkong/mariobros tilemap, galaxian shadow+sprite, gridlee+williams bitmap, galaga+digdug+gottlieb indexed, xevious scroll bg/fg. OUT OF SCOPE (documented .11/.12/.13/.15): priority compositing is inherently machine-specific — atari(u16 translucent-blend), foodf(claimed+pf_pen+cocktail), ccastles(priority PROM), mcr2(dirty+2x+OR-merge) share no model. Per-column-scroll (galaxian tilemap) and bespoke bitmap layers (missile_command planar 3rd bit, ccastles) also machine-specific.

title: graphics: consolidate palette resistor-DAC math (Feature 4)
description: Feature 4 — lowest risk, do first. Add pal_nbit(value,bits) to resistor.rs and dedupe btime/mcr2 hand-rolled pal2bit/pal3bit. Migrate galaxian_video resnet_raw_weights (galaxian_video.rs:357) to a shared helper — NOTE: it is closer to compute_resistor_net (per-bit voltage divider) than to compute_resistor_weights, so pick/extend the right model, not a blind swap. Leave mrdo_palette_rgb (diode-coupled ladder) bespoke, documented as intentionally standalone. CORRECTION vs doc: compute_tkg04_channel is already shared (mario_bros imports it from tkg04), so there is NO tkg04/mario duplication to extract — skip that bullet. All palette output byte-identical; port existing per-machine expected constants into resistor.rs tests.
close_reason: pal_nbit + compute_resnet_weights in resistor.rs; deduped btime/mcr2/galaxian. frameshot 0.0% (burgertime/shollow/galaxian).

title: graphics: migrate galaxian_video to indexed+priority helpers
description: Follow-up to .6/.3. Migrate galaxian_video's tilemap + the private draw_object_sprite_row (renamed in .3) onto render_tilemap_scanline_indexed / draw_sprite_row_indexed with the priority buffer, replacing the hand-rolled loops. Preserve the starfield/bullet layers and the sprites_clip. Acceptance: frameshot --compare 0.0% across the family (galaxian, and a spot-check of scramble/frogger).
close_reason: Migrated galaxian_video sprite blit to core gfx::draw_sprite_row (completes the .3 rename). Tilemap is per-column vertical scroll (no helper fits; galaxian-specific) - stays hand-rolled. galaxian is RGB/painter's (no priority buffer), so uses the RGB helper. frameshot 0.0% @ galaxian/frogger/scramble 300/700.

title: graphics: migrate foodf to indexed+priority helpers
description: DEFERRED: foodf is a bespoke per-pixel priority compositor, not a near-identical hand-roll. BLOCKERS (verified by reading render() at foodf.rs:692): (a) PLAYFIELD is a 256x224 column-scan tilemap (index=col*32+row) rendered per-pixel with a -8 scroll (rem_euclid 256) and cocktail flip via source-coord mirror -> needs the scroll-aware tilemap helper .14 EXTENDED to column-scan + cocktail (or handle cocktail via central-orientation); (b) SPRITES draw front-to-back with a claimed first-opaque-wins mask, 8-bit horizontal wrap (dx=(xpos+col)&0xFF, visible at w=256), cocktail dest-mirror (dx=255-dx), and a pf_pen priority test -> needs the priority-compositing sprite helper .15. Depends on .14 + .15. Cocktail should ideally move to the central-orientation epic (like mario_bros) rather than stay a source/dest mirror here.
close_reason: foodf is a bespoke priority compositor (claimed first-wins + pf_pen + 8-bit wrap + cocktail dest-mirror, RGB). No shared helper fits it (see .15 finding). Out of consolidation scope; cocktail belongs in central-orientation, mid-frame in the raster epic.

title: graphics: migrate atari_system1 playfield/MO to indexed+priority helpers
description: Follow-up to .6. Migrate the Atari System 1 playfield + motion-object renderers (marble, roadrunner) onto render_tilemap_scanline_indexed / draw_sprite_row_indexed writing index+priority buffers, then composite. Acceptance: frameshot --compare 0.0% vs pre-change (marble, roadrunner).
close_reason: atari_system1 uses u16 (10-bit) palette indices and a bespoke MO merge (translucent-bank blend + colour-0 priority-pen mask) that the u8 indexed/priority helpers can't represent. Uniform-scroll playfield could adopt a future u16 scroll-aware variant, but the priority merge stays machine-specific. Out of consolidation scope.

title: graphics: migrate mcr2 to indexed+priority helpers (upscale stays caller-side)
description: Follow-up to .6. Migrate MCR2 (satans_hollow) tilemap + sprites onto render_tilemap_scanline_indexed / draw_sprite_row_indexed. Per the design, the 2x upscale (render 1x, upscale in the existing rotate/palette pass) and the sprite-erase dirty marking (sprite_tile_dirty) stay caller-side — do NOT contort the helper. Optional if the upscale entangles the loop too much. Acceptance: frameshot --compare 0.0% vs pre-change (shollow).
close_reason: mcr2 render is dirty-tracked persistent buffers + 2x upscale + OR-based priority merge (prio|pen) + sprite-erase dirty marking — all machine-specific (design already put upscale/dirty caller-side). Doesn't fit the shared helpers. Out of consolidation scope.

title: graphics: scroll-aware tilemap scanline helpers (RGB + indexed)
description: Add render_scrolled_tilemap_scanline{,_indexed}: generalize the fixed-grid tilemap helpers to a scrolled map. Signature: (map_cols, map_rows, tile_w, tile_h, scroll_x, scroll_y, viewport_w, scanline, tile_info_fn:(map_col,map_row)->TileInfo, resolve_fn, buffers..., x_offset). Internally ty=(scanline+scroll_y).rem_euclid(map_rows*tile_h); tx=(screen_x+scroll_x).rem_euclid(map_cols*tile_w); per-tile flip + fine sub-tile offset. Caller computes scroll_x/scroll_y. The fixed-grid helper is the scroll=0 special case. COVERS: xevious bg+fg (both scrolled 64x32 maps, .8 migrated only sprites), atari_system1 playfields. LIMIT: uniform-per-scanline scroll only (per-line row-scroll ok); NOT per-column vertical scroll (galaxian). Core tests for scroll/wrap/flip; migrate xevious bg/fg + atari_system1, frameshot 0.0%.
close_reason: Added render_scrolled_tilemap_scanline{,_indexed}; migrated xevious bg+fg (resolves .8 deferral). frameshot --compare 0.0% @ 180/600/900/1200 (scrolling). atari_system1 playfields can adopt next.

title: graphics: priority-compositing sprite helper (first-wins + reference-priority compare)
description: FINDING (examined all four priority machines): no shared compositing model exists, so a single priority-compositing sprite helper cannot serve them pixel-identically. atari_system1: u16 (10-bit) indices (u8 helpers can't hold), translucent-bank blend + colour-0 priority-pen-mask MO merge. foodf: RGB, claimed first-wins + pf_pen visibility + 8-bit wrap + cocktail dest-mirror. ccastles: priority-PROM lookup keyed by (sprite pen, bitmap pen) selecting source + palette bit. mcr2: u8 indices, dirty-tracked persistent buffers + 2x upscale + OR-merge (prio|pen) + sprite-erase dirty. All bespoke and mutually different; the design itself hedged each (2x upscale caller-side, dirty-tracking out of scope, 'optional per machine', 'consider mcr2'). Conclusion: priority compositing is inherently machine-specific, out of consolidation scope.
close_reason: Priority compositing is inherently machine-specific: atari (u16 translucent-blend), foodf (claimed+pf_pen+cocktail RGB), ccastles (priority PROM), mcr2 (dirty-track+2x upscale+OR-merge) share no model and can't fit one pixel-identical helper. Out of consolidation scope.

title: graphics: enrich render_tilemap_scanline (TileInfo + per-tile flip + Option transparency)
description: Feature 2a. Evolve render_tilemap_scanline (tilemap.rs:26): tile_info_fn -> TileInfo{code,attr,flip_x,flip_y}; resolve_color_fn -> Option<(u8,u8,u8)> (None = transparent, covers raw-pixel==0 AND galaga LUT-based lut&0x0F==0x0F since the closure sees attr+pixel); helper applies per-tile flip before the cache lookup. Only 3 existing callers to update (namco_pac/tkg04/mario_bros — opaque + flip=false). Add core tests for flip and transparency. Unblocks galaga/digdug/xevious fg, gottlieb, galaxian, congo_bongo fg, foodf.
close_reason: render_tilemap_scanline enriched (TileInfo+flip+Option transparency); 3 callers updated. frameshot 0.0% (pacman/dkong/mariobros).

title: graphics: fix galaxian_video private draw_sprite_row shadowing (Feature 2c)
description: Feature 2c — small. galaxian_video.rs:624 defines an inherent method literally named draw_sprite_row (different signature), shadowing the core gfx::sprite::draw_sprite_row and called via self. at :563. Rename it (or migrate to the core helper as part of 2b). Confirmed present during verification.
close_reason: Renamed galaxian private draw_sprite_row -> draw_object_sprite_row. frameshot 0.0%.

title: graphics: unify Namco galaga/digdug/xevious renderers (Feature 1)
description: Feature 1 — depends on 2a (fg tilemap needs transparency). Hoist namco_tilemap_offset(col,row) into namco_galaga (or a namco_video module) and delete the byte-identical copies in galaga.rs:550/digdug.rs:673/namco_pac.rs:708. Migrate galaga+digdug tilemaps to the enriched render_tilemap_scanline and sprites to core draw_sprite_row (namco_pac.rs:822 shows the LUT trans_mask + SpriteClip tunnel-wrap pattern). Multi-tile 2x2 sprite iteration stays in the board; each 16x16 sub-tile calls draw_sprite_row per row. Xevious: route its fg blit through the enriched helper; keep the scrolling-bg address logic, its migration can trail. NOTE: render_tilemap is galaga-only (digdug/xevious call it render_background). Frameshot-compare each migrated machine.
close_reason: Hoisted namco_tilemap_offset to shared namco_video module (3 copies deduped); frameshot 0.0% (galaga/digdug/pacman). Per-machine tilemap/sprite renderer unification folded into .6 (all 3 are index-space, not RGB).

title: graphics: add render_bitmap_scanline helper + migrate packed-framebuffer machines (Feature 3)
description: Feature 3. core/src/gfx/ has no bitmap helper today. Add render_bitmap_scanline(src, pixels_per_byte, high_first, resolve: Fn(u8)->(u8,u8,u8), buffer, x_offset). Migrate the hand-rolled unpackers: williams.rs:441 (4bpp 2px/byte high-first), missile_command.rs (bit-planar 2bpp), ccastles.rs:852 bitmap layer (4bpp packed), gridlee.rs:632 (2px/byte, per-line palette latch captured in the closure). Frameshot-compare each. Indexed variant can follow if a bitmap machine ever needs priority (none do today).
close_reason: Added gfx::render_bitmap_scanline; migrated gridlee + williams. frameshot 0.0% (gridlee/joust). missile_command (planar 3rd bit) + ccastles (priority-entangled) left hand-rolled.

title: graphics: indexed+priority scanline helpers + migrate priority machines (Feature 2b)
description: Feature 2b — largest lift, sequenced last. Add render_tilemap_scanline_indexed and draw_sprite_row_indexed writing palette index + priority into persistent buffers (resolve_index_fn -> Option<(u8 index,u8 priority)>). Migrate gottlieb, galaxian_video, foodf, atari_system1 playfield; consider mcr2. Caller responsibilities (do NOT contort the helper): mcr2 2x upscale (render 1x, upscale in the existing rotate/palette pass) and mcr2 sprite-erase dirty marking stay caller-side. Optional per machine (no priority layers => never needed). Frameshot-compare each. This 2b substrate is also the prerequisite for mid-frame-raster Tier A priority machines.
close_reason: Added render_tilemap_scanline_indexed + draw_sprite_row_indexed with tests; migrated galaga tilemap+sprites (both helpers, 0.0% diff). Remaining priority-machine migrations (digdug/xevious/gottlieb/galaxian/foodf/atari/mcr2) are follow-up enabled by these helpers.

title: graphics: migrate digdug renderers to indexed scanline helpers
description: Follow-up to .6. Migrate Dig Dug (index-space, same NamcoGalagaBoard as galaga) onto render_tilemap_scanline_indexed + draw_sprite_row_indexed. galaga (.6) is the template: per-scanline tilemap over the native indexed buffer, LUT-based transparency via resolve->Option, sprites via draw_sprite_row_indexed. Dig Dug has two tilemap layers (render_background bg tiles + render_foreground 1bpp text, pen 0 transparent) plus sprites. namco_tilemap_offset already shared. title: 23 machines emit no audio at all from a headless boot
description:
The new registry audio sanity test (harness/tests/audio_sanity_test.rs) found
that 23 of 39 registered machines produce a capture whose peak is -200 dBFS —
digital zero for a full ten seconds, including the boot window.

MEASURED with `disasm frameshot --machine <m> --frames 600 --audio-out x.wav`
followed by `disasm audiodiff x.wav`, on 2026-08-19.

Namco WSG:      pacman, mspacman, galaga, digdug, xevious
Galaxian board: galaxian, mooncrst, pisces, uniwars
Konami/Scramble: scramble, scobra, frogger
Atari vector:   astdelux, tempest, starwars, esb, irobot, marble
Other:          mrdo, docastle, dowild, gridlee, shollow

WHY THIS IS FILED AS A BUG rather than recorded as correct behaviour: several of
these boards demonstrably make sound at power-on. Pac-Man plays its startup
jingle before any coin is inserted. Calling them "silent by design" to make a
test pass would be inventing a hardware claim.

Note galaxian is subtly different from the rest — it emits a power-on transient
in roughly the first second and nothing after, which is why it shows 99.6%
silent over a raw capture but 100% once the test's settle window is applied.

WHAT IS NOT YET KNOWN, and is the actual work here:
  1. Is the sound path simply not driven from `Harness::run_frame`? The same
     harness DOES produce audio for dkong, joust, robotron and the rest, so it
     is not a blanket harness problem — but it could still be per-family.
  2. Do these boards need a coin or start before their sound CPU runs? The
     rhai `open()` note in memory says galaga needs ~3000 frames to clear its
     power-on self-test, so 600 frames may simply be too few for some.
  3. Is the sound genuinely unimplemented for some of these? Asteroids Deluxe's
     discrete effect registers are known-stubbed, and the 54XX explosion path
     for galaga/xevious is known-missing (…-uxi9, …-pd5e).

SUGGESTED FIRST STEP: re-run the sweep with a much larger frame count (5000+)
and with a coin pulse, and see how many of the 23 remain. That separates "needs
more time or input" from "not wired up" without touching any board code.

Each machine is recorded in harness/tests/audio/expectations.toml as a
[[known_defect]] with `silence = true`. That file is a RATCHET, not a skip
list: `every_known_defect_is_still_present` asserts these machines are still
silent, so fixing one fails the suite until its entry is deleted. Delete
entries as they are fixed.
close_reason: INVALID — the finding was a fixture artifact, not a bug. The sweep booted each machine input-free, which reaches attract mode, and most arcade boards are silent until coined up. Replaying recorded input movies (~/.config/phosphor/movies) on the same builds gives healthy audio for all 23: pacman -4.6 dBFS peak with DC -0.018, frogger -14.4 dBFS, tempest -12.1 dBFS. The sanity test now replays a movie when one exists and only judges silence on a movie fixture; all 23 entries deleted from expectations.toml. Fixed in c0e168d.

title: Headless emulation benchmark harness
description:
There are no benchmarks anywhere in the workspace: no benches/ directory, no criterion dependency, no #[bench]. The in-app profiler (frontend/src/profile.rs) is good — per-phase timings and Chrome Trace export — but it measures one interactive session and produces nothing comparable across commits.

This blocks every performance item: none of them can be justified or refuted today.

Shape: 'run N frames of machine X headless, report frames/sec and ms/frame'. phosphor-harness is SDL-free, so the bench target needs no system dependencies and can live in harness/ or machines/.

Representative boards to cover:
- pacman   — single Z80, one address space (cleanest signal)
- galaga   — 3x Z80 sharing one board (multi-CPU dispatch cost)
- tempest  — M6502 + AVG + Mathbox (vector path)
- marble   — MC68010 + M6502 sound (68000 path)
- joust    — M6809 + M6800 + blitter (two address spaces, second bus master)

ROM-gated: skip cleanly when PHOSPHOR_ROMS is unset, same convention as tools/script/tests/frameshot_parity.rs.

Acceptance: a single command that prints a stable frames/sec figure per board, repeatable within a few percent run to run.
close_reason:
Implemented in 9f0198f as the tools/bench crate (phosphor-bench). Boots via the shared Harness, runs N frames headless with no throttle, reports per-frame emulation/render/audio cost plus fps and a realtime multiple. Defaults to pacman, galaga, tempest, marble, joust. ROM-gated through roms_dir(); exits 0 with a hint when ROMs are absent.

Acceptance ('a stable frames/sec figure per board, repeatable within a few percent') met and measured, not assumed: three consecutive full runs agreed within 1.7% (pacman 0.17%, marble 1.0%, joust 1.0%, tempest 1.1%, galaga 1.7%). Getting there required changing the estimator — reporting the median repeated only within 4.3%. The workload is deterministic (no RNG, no wall clock in the tick path), so all variation is host noise and noise only adds time; the minimum is therefore both the more accurate and the more stable estimator. The trailing +/- now reports how far the slowest rep lagged, so noise is visible rather than hidden.

Baseline (release, 600 frames, 120 warmup, 5 reps):
  pacman  emul 0.823 ms/f  total 0.829  1206.6 fps  19.91x realtime
  galaga  emul 1.011 ms/f  total 1.085   921.6 fps  15.21x
  tempest emul 1.135 ms/f  total 1.183   845.2 fps  14.09x
  marble  emul 2.455 ms/f  total 3.151   317.4 fps   5.30x
  joust   emul 0.751 ms/f  total 0.757  1320.6 fps  21.97x

Notable for the epics that depend on this: emulation is ~99% of frame cost on the raster boards (render 0.006 ms/f on pacman and joust), so concrete-bus-dispatch is aimed at the right place. Marble is the outlier at 0.697 ms/f render — the playfield/motion-object priority compositor — and is the slowest board overall at 5.3x realtime.

Caveat recorded in the tool's --help: the 120-frame default warmup is far short of most machines' power-on self-test, so the default numbers measure self-test code rather than gameplay. Fine for A/B (both sides measure the same thing); raise --warmup for in-game figures.

Unblocks ci-build-foundation-xnk5.3 (release profile) and concrete-bus-dispatch-blzz.

title: Epic: Headless CPU/bus debugging & trace tooling
description:
Surface the mature interactive-debugger machinery (MachineDebug/DebugCpu/BusDebug/DebugTrace/Watchpoints) to headless workflows, plus the two small core features recurring bug hunts keep needing. Design: docs/designs/headless-debugging.md.

Verified against code: all trait surfaces, run_frameshot harness, parse_u32_auto, and the #[debug_map] derive exist as the doc describes; check_read/check_write already carry value+width so conditional watchpoints are a localized change. Instruction trace + hang detection are pure harness code (zero per-board work). Lowest-risk / highest-leverage of the three design docs; unblocks the mid-frame raster audit and directly serves the open ESB reset bug (j63p).

Phases: (1) trace harness + event/watchpoint logging [frame loop]; (2) instruction trace + break-pc [cycle loop]; (3) conditional/value-match watchpoints [only core-type change]; (4) hang/idle-loop detection; (5) interactive debugger UX + CLI polish. Phases 1-4 and 5 are independently shippable.

The design doc moved from ~/headless-debugging.md into docs/designs/headless-debugging.md and is marked implemented.

title: audiodiff's decay T20/T40 is wrong on a noise-gated envelope
description:
audiodiff reported Galaxian's hit decaying 36 % too fast (T20 0.524 s ours
against 0.818 s for the board). Both numbers are wrong, and the error was large
enough to be written up as the board's last outstanding residual.

Measured directly, by least-squares fitting the log of a 20 ms-windowed upper
envelope:

                       ours      board
  gated node peak    3.3000 V   3.3000 V
  noise enable duty    52.3 %     51.5 %
  fitted cap tau     0.7527 s   0.7652 s
  output envelope    0.7523 s   0.8002 s

For tau of 0.76 s a true T20 is tau*ln(10) = 1.75 s. audiodiff reported 0.524 and
0.818, neither close to 1.75 nor to each other.

WHY IT FAILS HERE. The hit is a capacitor voltage GATED by a 7920 Hz noise line,
so about half of all samples are exactly zero regardless of how much charge is
left. Any envelope follower with a window shorter than the LFSR's run lengths
sees the envelope collapse to zero repeatedly and reports whichever dropout it
hit first. This is not exotic: every gated-noise voice on these boards has it,
which is most explosion and shoot effects.

I hit the same bug in my own analysis first, using a window of four noise
periods. Widening it to 20 ms (about 160 noise periods) fixed it. So the shape of
the fix is known.

SUGGESTED: measure decay by fitting an exponential to the log-envelope over the
span where it is above some floor, rather than by first-crossing of a threshold,
and choose the envelope window from the signal rather than fixing it. Report the
fitted tau alongside T20 so a bad fit is visible. A first-crossing metric on a
signal with legitimate zeros cannot be made reliable by tuning the threshold.

UNTIL THEN: do not trust T20/T40 on any voice gated by noise. The scratchpad
script that measures it correctly is small and could move into the analysis
module more or less as is.

Found while node-dumping Galaxian's hit chain; see phosphor-emulator-t8iu.
close_reason:
Fixed. Two changes to core/src/audio/analysis/level.rs.

T20/T40 ARE NOW MEASURED ON THE ENVELOPE'S UPPER HULL. decay_time took the first
crossing of the target below the peak, on a raw block-RMS envelope. A voice
carried by noise has an envelope that fluctuates hard around its trend, so the
first crossing finds a statistical dip rather than the decay, and the bias is
one-sided because the peak it measures down from is itself the maximum of the
same fluctuation. Taking the non-increasing upper hull answers "has it fallen
this far and STAYED there", which is what a decay time means.

DECAY_TAU_S IS NEW: a least-squares fit of the time constant across the whole
decay, with the fit's r2 alongside it. This is the number to read on a noisy
voice, and the r2 is what makes it safe to quote: a clean exponential fits above
0.99, and anything that is not one reports a low value instead of a confident
wrong tau. audiodiff prints both.

RESULT on the signal that exposed it, Galaxian's explosion against a converged
reference:

                    before      after     board
  decay T20        0.524 s    1.711 s    1.866 s
  decay tau             -     0.781 s    0.788 s
  decay fit r2          -       0.797     0.832

The fitted taus agree to 0.9 %, which matches an independent measurement made
off the board's NODE_155 node dump (0.7527 s ours against 0.7652 s). T20 of
1.711 s against a theoretical tau*ln(10) of 1.80 s is the hull crossing landing
slightly early, which is expected and harmless.

IT MOVES ONLY WHAT WAS BROKEN. Galaxian's fire is unchanged to three decimals
(T20 0.359 vs 0.374, T40 0.733 vs 0.738) and its fit is r2 0.999, because its
envelope is a clean exponential with no dips deep enough to trigger the defect.
The melody correctly reports no decay at all. That is the behaviour to want from
a fix like this: it is a repair, not a redefinition.

TESTS: a noise-gated decay built from a real LFSR at 7920 Hz, which fails hard on
the old code; a fitted tau recovering a known exponential; and a two-stage decay
that must report a poor fit rather than a confident number. The last one caught
my own first attempt, whose slow stage sat below the fit's floor so only the
clean fast stage was being fitted.

CONSEQUENCE FOR NUMBERS ALREADY QUOTED: hull crossing can only be later than or
equal to first crossing, so every T20/T40 measured before this is a LOWER BOUND.
Smooth envelopes (galaxian fire, dkong jump) are unaffected; noise-gated ones
(galaxian hit, dkong stomp and walk) may not be. Noted on the dkong walk issue,
whose decay evidence predates this.

title: Concrete bus dispatch: Atari DVG/AVG family
description: Convert the M6502 vector boards -- Asteroids, Asteroids Deluxe, Lunar Lander, Quantum, Star Wars (seven bus_split! sites) -- per docs/designs/concrete-bus-dispatch.md. Blocked by the generic Cpu::reset task (the M6502 fetches its reset vector through the bus). Measure tempest/asteroids before/after; golden frames here also pin the vector display list, so a reordered tick shows up.
close_reason:
Partially done, remainder split out.

Converted in 6cfbd9b: Asteroids, Asteroids Deluxe and Lunar Lander -- the three machines that actually share AtariDvgBoard.

Numbers (phosphor-bench, release, 400f x 5 reps, best of 6 alternating runs, idle host):
  llander  0.361 -> 0.336 ms/f  -6.9%
  astdelux 0.624 -> 0.591       -5.3%
  asteroid 0.430 -> 0.422       -1.9%
Small for the usual reason: 1.512 MHz, 25,200 cycles/frame, and a large share of each frame is vector rendering and discrete-sound simulation that this change doesn't touch. Asteroids gains least -- its emulation cost is already the smallest in the bench set, and its discrete sound advances once per frame rather than per cycle.

First real 6502 users of the generic Cpu::reset (bek7): the 6502 fetches its reset vector through the bus, so these could not have been converted before it.

Shape: board + per-game view, since each game puts real I/O in front of the board (input muxes, DIPs, discrete sound, POKEY, EAROM, analog thrust pedal). Added a begin_cycle hook to AtariDvgBus for per-cycle game work -- Asteroids Deluxe clocks its POKEY there, which also let its debug_tick_pre go: the debugger's single-step now clocks the POKEY exactly as run_frame does, because both go through the same tick. No frame-loop inversion: this board has no scanline structure, only a per-cycle NMI counter.

NOT done, split out to v5gm: Quantum and Star Wars. Neither uses AtariDvgBoard -- Quantum is a standalone M68000 + AVG machine (~1200 lines, 'u32 word' bus_split arm) and Star Wars is a standalone two-6502 board (~2700 lines, seven bus_split! sites). Both need a different shape (nesting the bus state rather than a board-plus-view), and each is a conversion in its own right rather than a variation on this one. The issue's premise that this family was five M6502 machines on one board was wrong in the same way the TKG-04 issue's was.

Golden frames unchanged for all pinned machines; machine, harness and ROM-gated suites pass; clippy and fmt clean.

title: Concrete bus dispatch: Galaxian (Moon Cresta, Pisces) and MCR II (Satan's Hollow)
description: Convert the two single-Z80 shared boards per docs/designs/concrete-bus-dispatch.md. Mechanical: the Pac-Man shape applies directly. Watch for game-specific decoding that is really board behaviour (move it to the board so the board can be the bus, avoiding a view struct). Measure and run golden frames.
close_reason:
Done in beb4ef8 (galaxian + mooncresta + pisces/uniwars + satans_hollow).

Numbers (phosphor-bench, release, 400f x 5 reps, best of 6 alternating runs, idle host):
  galaxian 1.517 -> 1.317 ms/f  -13.2%
  pisces   1.541 -> 1.378       -10.6%
  mooncrst 1.528 -> 1.376        -9.9%
  shollow  3.408 -> 3.266        -4.2%

Satan's Hollow gains least for the usual reason: 2.496 MHz, a heavy compositor, and an SSIO sound board whose Z80 runs *inside the device* rather than through this bus -- so comparatively little of its frame is main-bus dispatch.

Shapes: both boards became the bus outright. GalaxianBoard serves Galaxian, Moon Cresta and UniWar S unchanged (they differ only in the map-layout flag and GFX-bank mode the board already carries); Mcr2Board serves Satan's Hollow, its only machine. Three system-level 'impl Bus' blocks deleted outright.

Pisces was the one exception: it re-wires 0x6002 (GFX bank instead of coin lockout), so it keeps a newtype view. Deliberately not folded into bus_write_common -- that would charge every other Galaxian game a comparison on every write.

Useful measurement fell out of that pairing: pisces (newtype view) and mooncrst (board direct) land within 0.002 ms/f of each other on identical hardware. So a single-pointer view hoisted out of the loop costs nothing; the Galaga regression was specifically about multi-pointer views rebuilt per cycle. Recorded in the design doc.

Also inverted both frame loops (Galaxian: starfield advance + line render + VBLANK NMI; MCR II: the CTC's two scanline-triggered channels), renamed GalaxianBoard::check_interrupts to interrupt_state, and preserved save-state layout (both boards wrote their CPU first).

Golden frames unchanged for all pinned machines (galaxian, mooncrst, pisces, uniwars, shollow); machine, harness and ROM-gated suites pass; clippy and fmt clean.

26 files still reference bus_split!.

title: Inlinable fast path for backed-memory bus reads
description:
Now that converted boards dispatch to a concrete bus, the remaining per-access cost is the work inside bus_read_common/bus_write_common: a page lookup, a watchpoint check and a trace-enabled check on every access. Those functions are too large to inline, so each access is still a direct call with the register pressure that implies -- the Pac-Man codegen shows 29 call sites to bus_read_common in one Z80 cycle instantiation.

Idea: an #[inline] fast path for the common case (address lands in a backed ReadWrite/ReadOnly region, no watchpoints armed, tracing off) that reads the backing store directly, falling out to the existing function for I/O, unmapped addresses, and any debug observability. A trait object could never inline this; a concrete bus can.

Measure with phosphor-bench on pacman and galaga (both converted). Verify golden frames -- a fast path that skips a watchpoint check when one IS armed would be a silent debugger regression, so the fallback condition needs a test.

Depends on concrete bus dispatch reaching the boards being measured.

title: Debugger shows a stale image for machines that render in run_frame
description:
Machines that render once at the end of run_frame into a cached framebuffer (rather than per-scanline during tick()) show a frozen image while running under the debugger. The debugger advances the machine via MachineDebug::debug_tick() (frontend/src/debug_ui.rs execute_frame), which calls the board's tick() but never run_frame(), so the cached framebuffer is not refreshed. The frontend still copies that stale framebuffer via render_frame().

Affects Continue-in-debug, the new Step Frame, and frame breakpoints. Known-affected machines: Burgertime (machines/src/burgertime.rs run_frame calls board.render() after the tick loop), Dig Dug, and likely other render-in-run_frame machines. Per-scanline renderers (Williams/Joust, Missile Command, Gridlee, ...) update correctly because their scanline buffer is written during tick().

Note: CPU register / memory / device inspection and all breakpoints work correctly; only the displayed picture is stale.

Fix options: (a) have affected boards render at frame boundaries inside tick() (e.g. when clock crosses cycles_per_frame) so both run_frame and debug_tick refresh the framebuffer, removing the redundant explicit render() in run_frame; or (b) add a way for the debug path to request a render once per completed frame. Option (a) is localized per machine and keeps a single render site.

Audit all machines for the render-in-run_frame pattern when fixing.
close_reason: Fixed by Phase 1 (commit e9380a3) and confirmed by pjl in the real frontend debugger. Machines that cached a render in run_frame now render at a frame-boundary hook shared by run_frame and debug_tick, so the picture stays live under Continue-in-debug, Step Frame, and frame breakpoints. Audited all machines for the render-in-run_frame pattern as the issue asked: exactly six were affected (galaga, xevious, digdug, burgertime, qbert, shollow); mrdo, foodf, marble and roadrunner render on demand from live state and were never stale. Took fix option (a) — render at frame boundaries inside the tick path, single render site, redundant run_frame render removed. Output byte-identical (frameshot 12/12) and guarded by the ROM-gated acceptance test debug_tick_advances_picture_like_run_frame.

title: Tempest's headless render_frame double-applies ROT270
description:
Captured while pinning golden frames (phosphor-emulator-frame-regression-w1pi.2). harness/tests/golden/tempest.png shows every string running bottom-to-top: the picture is 90 degrees off upright.

AtariAvgBoard::render_frame calls rasterize_vectors(.., flip_y = false), and that branch is documented as 'ROT270: Y already maps to screen-Y directly' — i.e. the rasterised buffer is already in screen space. Every caller of render_frame then applies the machine's declared orientation centrally (Orientation::ROT270 for TempestSystem), which rotates it a second time.

The frontend does not hit this: for vector machines it feeds vector_display_list to GL, and the shader's 'rotation == 270' branch only negates Y (frontend/src/vector_gl.rs) rather than rotating, so the live game looks right. The two paths therefore disagree, and the disagreement is invisible to frameshot_parity.rs because both of its sides go through render_frame.

Affects: disasm frameshot, phosphor-script screenshot, the debug UI's texture fallback, and the golden frame pinned for tempest.

Fix needs a decision on where the AVG's screen mapping belongs — in rasterize_vectors, in the declared orientation, or in the GL shader — and the three should then agree. The golden hash for tempest must be recaptured with the fix.
close_reason: orientation() was answering two questions: a framebuffer rotation for the frontend and a Y-negate hint for the GL shader. Tempest needed only the second. The cabinet's mapping now lives in the coordinates the AVG emits, the board rasterizes with flip_y, and no orientation is declared. Test asserts the mapping rather than the enum.

title: Epic: Input movies — record and replay gameplay
description:
Design: docs/designs/input-movie.md

A deterministic input-movie format (*.phmi) that records a cabinet's exact input
trace and replays it headlessly with a byte-identical framebuffer, plus the
frames.toml integration that makes the golden suite pin GAMEPLAY rather than
attract mode.

WHY. golden_frame_test pins an exact frame hash for all 40 registered machines,
but every entry is input-free: 40 [[frame]] entries, 3 with an nvram fixture,
ZERO scripting any input (`press` exists only as a header comment). So the suite
guards attract loops, title screens and demo playback, never a frame produced
under player control — collision, scoring, input-driven sound and every code path
behind a coin are unguarded. Separately, PressSpec/MotionSpec cannot express a
trackball or spinner trace at all, which is what the ten analog machines need
(ccastles, foodf, gridlee, irobot, marble, missile_command, quantum, roadrunner,
starwars, tempest).

This is NOT about fixing determinism — that is already enforced by
golden_frame_test and save_state_rom_test. It is about coverage.

Separate epic from checkpoint rewind: no shared types, traits or crates. The sole
interaction is that rewind is disabled while a recording is armed; whichever epic
lands second adds the guard.

title: Movie format, recorder/player, and Harness::build_with_movie
description:
harness/src/movie.rs: the *.phmi format, MovieRecorder, MoviePlayer, and
Harness::build_with_movie. No frontend, no ROMs needed to test.

FORMAT (LE throughout, matching StateWriter):
  magic b"PHMI" | version:u16 | header_len:u32 | header
  records_len:u32 | deflate(records)
  trailer: sha256(all preceding bytes), 32 bytes

MovieHeader { machine: String, rom_digest: [u8;32], controls: Vec<String>,
              dip: Vec<u8>, nvram: Option<Vec<u8>>, host_sample_rate: u32,
              frames: u32 }

MovieRecord = Button{frame,ctl,pressed} | Absolute{frame,ctl,bits}
            | Relative{frame,ctl,bits} | ReleaseAll{frame}
            | Dip{frame,bank,value} | Marker{frame,label}

FOUR LOAD-BEARING DECISIONS:

1. Records are per EVENT, never aggregated per frame. RelativeCounter::add_delta
   (core/src/core/input.rs:78) is `pending += delta as i32` — truncation on every
   call. Two 0.6-deltas contribute 0; one summed 1.2-delta contributes 1. On
   Tempest and Quantum, DrainPolicy::ClampDrop discards the remainder so the
   error never averages out. Store floats as f32::to_bits so replay truncates
   identically.

2. rom_digest is sha256 over the loaded ROMs in rom_names order. A movie replayed
   against a different dump must fail loudly, not desync into a
   plausible-but-wrong frame hash.

3. `controls` is an interned index table of stable_names; records carry a u16
   index into it. Survives InputId renumbering, and a 36k-event trackball movie
   does not carry 36k copies of "track_x".

4. host_sample_rate is SET on replay via set_host_sample_rate before the machine
   is built — not compared and rejected. Rejecting would make a committed movie
   fail on any host whose card opens at a different rate. Ordering rule is
   audio-output-path.md section 3.

NOT in the header: SAVE_VERSION. A movie holds no save state, so it must not
couple to the save format — that decoupling is what lets a committed movie
survive tlv-save-state.md.

REPLAY. build_with_movie verifies machine + rom_digest, sets the host rate,
builds and resets, loads inline NVRAM, applies dip, and resolves controls to
InputIds through the machine's own control table. run_frame() drains records
while records[cursor].frame == self.frame, in order, then steps the machine. The
existing PressSpec/MotionSpec path is untouched.

Frame index = completed frames at delivery time. Exact, not approximate: the SDL
pump and run_frame are sequential, and resync only runs after reset, state load
or focus change, so nothing calls handle_input mid-frame. No sub-frame cycle
field is needed.

Acceptance: a movie round-trips through write/read with identical records;
build_with_movie rejects a machine mismatch and a rom_digest mismatch.
close_reason: Format, recorder, player and Harness replay landed in 68d5ce2 and 91e0c61. 27 unit tests cover the round trip per record kind, bit-exact float payloads, and rejection of bad magic/version, body corruption, every truncation prefix, an out-of-range control index, a record past the declared span, and non-monotonic frames. Deviation from the design doc: sha2 and flate2 became real harness dependencies rather than being avoided — the Cargo.toml note claiming sha2 had to stay dev-only did not survive checking, since zip already pulls flate2 into this crate's runtime tree and digest/block-buffer/crypto-common are vendored for zip's sha1 and hmac. build_with_movie's ROM-digest and machine-mismatch rejection paths need a booted machine, so they are covered by the determinism gate in .3 rather than here.

title: disasm replay / movie info / movie check subcommands
description:
Thin CLI wrappers over Harness::build_with_movie, following the existing
frameshot/trace conventions (--machine, positional roms path, parse_u32_auto).

  disasm replay --movie <m.phmi> [--frames N] <roms>  replay; optional frameshot
  disasm movie info  <m.phmi>                         header + per-frame counts + markers
  disasm movie check <m.phmi> <roms>                  replay + hash, CI without a PNG

`movie info` must work WITHOUT a ROM set or a machine — the header is
self-describing. It is the human-readable view that justifies the format being
binary rather than TOML.

Deliberately NO `disasm record`: headless recording has no human to record, and
PressSpec/MotionSpec already covers what a headless author would express.

Acceptance: `movie info` prints a readable summary of a movie produced by the
format issue with no roms argument; `movie check` replays and prints the frame
hash.
close_reason: replay / movie info / movie check landed. movie info needs neither ROMs nor a machine, as specified. movie check prints the same sha256 frames.toml pins — guaranteed by construction rather than by coincidence, because the extraction in 7036460 moved hash_frame/hash_vectors/render_oriented into phosphor-harness so the golden suite, frameshot and the movie CLI share one encoding; vector machines print the display-list hash too. 6 integration tests drive the compiled binary, three of them ROM-free so they run in CI. No disasm record subcommand, as designed: headless recording has no human to record.

title: Determinism gate: movie_test.rs, incl. the audio-drain check
description:
harness/tests/movie_test.rs — registry-driven over create_bare, plus ROM-gated
cases via roms_dir(), mirroring save_state_rom_test.rs gating.

CASES:
- record a synthetic event stream, replay twice, assert identical save_state()
  AND render_frame();
- record-then-replay equivalence against a live run;
- negatives: rom_digest mismatch, machine mismatch, unknown control name, a
  record past header.frames.

MUST ALSO RESOLVE, do not defer: headless Harness never calls fill_audio, so
SampleRing accumulates and eventually drops-oldest with an overruns() counter. If
any of that reaches a machine's Saveable, the replay-twice test passes in-process
but a movie replayed under different drain conditions will not match on the
save-state half of the fingerprint. The frame hash is unaffected either way.
Determine whether audio transport state is inside Saveable; if it is, either
exclude it from the fingerprint and say so in the test, or drain
deterministically. Discovering this during the golden-pin work instead is
expensive.

Acceptance: deliberately perturbing a replayed record fails the test; the
audio-drain question is answered in a comment, not left open.
close_reason: Determinism gate landed. 11 tests: ROM-less registry-driven record/replay over all 40 machines, ROM-gated on booted machines, encode/decode round trip, and the three negatives. The audio-drain question is answered and asserted rather than deferred — draining does not change saved state, because AudioResampler::save_state writes its filter state but not its output SampleRing, so a movie fingerprints the same headless or live. Two anti-vacuity guards added: 38 of 40 machines observably react to the generated input, and the two-0.6-deltas-vs-one-1.2-delta distinction is provably witnessable. Golden frames unchanged.

title: Frontend capture: Recording tee wrapper + HostAction::MovieRecord
close_reason: Frontend capture landed. Recording is a tee over InputConfigurable; input::dispatch and input::resync are unmodified, and resync is teed too since it emits real events with no SDL event behind them. F2 = HostAction::MovieRecord, rebindable. Arming resets and mirrors Harness::from_movie's boot order (capture NVRAM, reset, restore NVRAM, snapshot DIP) so replay reconstructs the same start. Only whole frames advance the counter, which is the debugger partial-frame case the issue flagged. Mid-session DIP edits are recorded; quitting mid-take still writes the file; writes are atomic. The fast-forward prerequisite was already met — F9 toggles the throttle. Not verified in a live SDL window by me: the tee is unit-tested and the wiring compiles clean, but the F2-in-a-running-game flow needs a human at the keyboard.

title: Golden gameplay pins: movie field in frames.toml
description:
The payoff. frames.toml gains one optional field; an entry carrying it replays
the movie instead of running input-free.

    [[frame]]
    machine = "marble"
    movie   = "movies/marble-level1.phmi"
    frames  = 4200
    shows   = "Level 1, ball mid-way up the second ramp, enemy marble closing"
    size    = [512, 384]
    frame   = "sha256:..."

Movies live in harness/tests/golden/movies/, beside the existing nvram/ fixtures,
and round-trip through PHOSPHOR_GOLDEN_UPDATE with the other human-authored
fields. Every existing guard applies unchanged: registry coverage, the
no-uniform-frame check, the ROM-less PNG/hash cross-check.

TWO HONEST NOTES:
- A gameplay pin is no MORE fragile than an attract pin — both are exact
  functions of the ROM set and frame count — but it will FAIL more often, because
  it covers more machine state. That is the point, and it raises the value of
  `shows` and the committed reference PNG, which carry the human judgement that
  the frame was right when pinned.
- Not every machine needs one. Prefer where attract mode guards least: the ten
  analog machines first (marble, tempest, missile_command, ccastles), then
  machines whose attract loop is a static title screen. Keep clips short — the
  boot phase records zero records, so a 3000-frame seek costs nothing in file
  size.

Acceptance: at least four analog machines carry a gameplay pin whose `shows`
describes something an attract loop cannot reach; each pin reviewed as a PNG diff
before commit.

title: Emit a MAME-playable form of a movie's digital input (not .inp)
description:
Emit a MAME-playable form of a movie's input, so a gameplay frame can be
compared against MAME behind a coin rather than only in attract mode.

DO NOT TARGET MAME'S .inp FORMAT. It is port-bit-level, keyed by a driver's
ioport tag and bitmask, and three problems compound:

- It is tied to a MAME build. .inp playback is only reliable against the exact
  version and ROM set that recorded it, so a committed conversion rots on every
  MAME upgrade.
- It needs a per-machine port map (our stable_name -> MAME's port tag + mask),
  hand-built across 40 machines, verifiable only by running both and diffing.
- Analog would not survive. MAME's analog_field model (sensitivity, delta,
  centering) is not our RelativeCounter model, and our per-event truncation —
  the property the record shape exists to preserve — has no counterpart. A
  trackball trace converted to .inp is a different session that happens to start
  the same way.

TARGET INSTEAD: a neutral scenario emitted two ways. Author a scenario once
(frame 600 coin, frame 640 start, frames 700-760 hold left) and produce both our
.phmi and a MAME Lua script driving ioport fields at the same frames. Tractable
because the per-machine mapping is needed only for the handful of controls a
scenario uses, not the whole table, and there is no binary-format or
MAME-version coupling. Precedent exists in this repo: the Xevious runaway
(phosphor-emulator-xevious-8u2a.1.5) was cracked with an out-of-tree MAME Lua
bus-diff.

SCOPE: digital controls only. Analog is explicitly out — see above — which means
this covers the case frames.toml's existing `press` mechanism could nearly
express anyway. The genuine new capability is comparing frames BEHIND A COIN.

CHECK FIRST, BEFORE BUILDING ANYTHING: whether input transfer is the binding
constraint at all. MAME runs attract mode deterministically with -str plus
-snapshot, and disasm frameshot/imgdiff already cover our side — that is how the
existing 40 golden frames were validated. If the comparisons that actually get
made are attract-mode ones, this buys little. Establish a concrete comparison
that is blocked today before paying for a per-machine mapping table.

ALSO VERIFY: the exact Lua ioport API surface against the MAME build in use
(manager.machine.ioport.ports[...].fields[...]:set_value() or its current
equivalent). Known to exist, but the shape should be confirmed rather than
assumed.

Acceptance: one machine, one digital scenario, the same frame reached in both
emulators, compared with imgdiff — plus a recorded finding on whether the
approach generalises enough to be worth extending.
notes:
REMOVED. `disasm movie mame` and tools/disasm/src/mame.rs are deleted. The tool
worked; its useful envelope turned out to be too narrow to justify keeping, and
a narrow tool that looks general is a trap.

WHY. Two independent emulators never share state, and the measured divergence
curve is unforgiving: at frame 200 our replay and MAME's differed by 0.22% of
pixels (and the diff was only the player sprite's animation phase); by frame
2500 the sessions had diverged outright, 2450 points against 2950. Even at its
best it was never EXACT, so it could not serve as a gate — only as something to
eyeball. Its one real advantage was scale across 40 machines, and scale only
pays if the comparison is run routinely, which divergence rules out. A
hand-written ten-line Lua covers the occasional one-off just as well.

What it was not needed for, in the end:
- attract-mode video comparison needs no input transfer at all; MAME's -str plus
  -snapshot already does it, and that is how the 40 golden frames were validated
- per-effect audio has a better tool already: tools/sound-reference's
  drive_*_sound.lua plus the machines/examples/*_capture.rs siblings feed BOTH
  emulators the same register writes on the same timeline, so game state never
  enters into it
- gross audio properties (DC offset, clipping, band balance, silence) are
  session-independent and want no MAME reference at all — see the audiodiff
  issue's registry-driven sanity test

FINDINGS WORTH KEEPING, since they cost real measurement and outlive the code:

1. MAME's Lua ioport API in 0.287: manager.machine.ioport.ports[tag]
   .fields[name]:set_value(v); fields carry .mask and .is_analog.
   emu.add_machine_frame_notifier exists alongside the older
   register_frame_done / register_frame.

2. A FRAME NOTIFIER WHOSE SUBSCRIPTION IS NOT RETAINED IS SILENTLY COLLECTED.
   `emu.add_machine_frame_notifier(function ... end)` with the result discarded
   does nothing at all — the script loads, prints nothing, and the run looks
   like ordinary attract mode. Bind it to a variable. This cost an entire
   debugging cycle.

3. PORT TAGS VARY WILDLY BETWEEN DRIVERS (:IN0, :P1, :SYSTEM, :DSW1, :1820,
   :F60000) BUT FIELD NAMES ARE CONVENTIONAL: "P1 Up", "P1 Button 1", "Coin 1",
   "1 Player Start", "Tilt". Search every port by name and ignore the tag.

4. Coin slots and start buttons are numbered by SLOT, not player — our own
   tables declare both coin1 and coin2 with player: None, because a coin slot
   does not belong to a player.

5. MAME's -wavwrite TAPS BEFORE the per-game audio_effects chain. Capturing
   dkong with its normal cfg (Filters/Compressor/Reverb/Equalizer on :mono) and
   with an empty cfg directory produced byte-identical WAVs. So a wavwrite
   comparison is raw synthesis against raw synthesis, and the difference from
   what a MAME user hears is that chain. This answers the open question in
   phosphor-emulator-asteroids-sound-postprocessing-hm4.

6. Analog cannot transfer regardless: marble's MAME trackball fields are
   is_analog with mask 255, an absolute port value, against our stream of
   relative deltas. Different models, not different encodings.
close_reason: Built and verified end to end against MAME 0.287. `disasm movie mame <movie> [--snap-at N] -o out.lua` emits a frame-notifier script, ROM-free. The InputKind+player rule replaced the per-machine port table the issue assumed: field names are conventional across drivers even though tags are not, so lookup is by name across all ports. Two bugs the verification caught that reading could not: coin slots are numbered by slot not player (burgertime declares both coin1 and coin2 with player:None, so both mapped to 'Coin 1'), and MAME unsubscribes a frame notifier whose subscription object is not retained — an unbound one silently does nothing and the run looks like plain attract mode. RESULT: at frame 200 our replay and MAME's differ by 0.22% (126/57600 px), and the diff is only the chef sprite's animation phase; by frame 2500 the sessions have diverged (score 2450 vs 2950). So a transferred scenario is frame-faithful early and drifts over thousands of frames of player-controlled physics. Practical guidance recorded: comparison scenarios should be SHORT — reach the state, snapshot, compare — not 'replay four minutes'. Analog remains out, confirmed by marble's is_analog absolute-value ports.

title: Frontend movie playback (--movie), including into the debugger
description:
Let the SDL frontend replay a movie, not just record one. `--movie <file.phmi>`
binds it and plays it back in the live window.

CHEAPER THAN IT LOOKS. The frontend ALREADY holds a Harness — DebugSession wraps
one (tools/script/src/session.rs:29) and the frontend drives it as
Rc<RefCell<DebugSession>>. Harness::bind_movie already exists, and
apply_scheduled_input/advance_frame are already public for exactly this case:
their doc comment says they are "for callers that drive the machine cycle-by-cycle
rather than frame-by-frame", which is the frontend's debug loop. Estimate 60-80
lines: a --movie flag, a harness accessor on DebugSession, calling
apply_scheduled_input() before execute_frame and advance_frame() after when
frame_executed, plus an overlay.

WHY, IN ORDER OF STRENGTH:

1. REPLAYING INTO THE DEBUGGER IS A WORKFLOW THAT DOES NOT EXIST TODAY. Every war
   story in headless-debugging.md was attract-mode reachable. A bug that needs a
   coin and three minutes of play has no debugging path at all right now — you
   cannot get there. With playback you replay to the frame the bug shows and have
   breakpoints, watchpoints, the event ring and the memory viewer already sitting
   on it. This is a new capability, not a convenience.

2. PICKING A PIN FRAME IS CURRENTLY GUESS-RENDER-LOOK. The golden-movie workflow
   is `disasm replay --frames N -o f.png`, look, adjust N, repeat. Watching at
   60 Hz with a frame counter and pause/step collapses that to "watch until it
   looks right, read the number off the overlay".

3. AUDIO. disasm replay is silent. The audio-output-path epic was explicit that
   "by ear" was a gate no measurement could stand in for, and a movie is a whole
   session.

SCOPE LINES TO HOLD:

- LIVE INPUT IS IGNORED during playback. Letting a keypress take over and end the
  replay is a reasonable affordance but muddies what is being watched. Start with
  pure playback; add takeover later if it is missed.
- THE FRONTEND MUST NOT BECOME AUTHORITATIVE FOR GOLDEN CAPTURE. The pinned hash
  keeps coming from the headless path, or CI cannot produce it without a display.
  Frontend playback is for looking; `disasm movie check` stays the source of truth.
- The frame counter must advance only on frames that actually ran — the same
  frame_executed gate the recorder uses, since the debugger can step cycles.

NON-ISSUE, recorded so it is not re-litigated: the frontend paces frames against
the audio ring and can drop or repeat under load. That does not affect replay
determinism, because input is delivered by frame index, not wall clock. A
stuttering window still replays the identical session.

Acceptance: `--movie` plays a recorded session back in the window with sound; the
overlay shows frame N of M; pausing and single-stepping keep the movie aligned;
and the frame reached at N matches what `disasm replay --frames N` renders.
close_reason: Frontend playback landed. --movie binds and replays in the live window with sound and the debugger available. MoviePlayer::deliver was extracted so the harness and the frontend share one delivery body rather than duplicating the ordering rules — the frontend's machine reference is borrowed out of the session and cannot reach back into it mid-frame, which is why playback state sits beside the session rather than in its Harness. Live game input is suppressed during playback (host hotkeys still work, so pause/step/debug panels remain); the frame counter advances only on frames that actually ran, matching the recorder's frame_executed gate; a MOVIE n/total overlay shows for the whole replay rather than behind the FPS toggle, since reading that number off the screen is the point. A movie for another machine or another ROM dump is refused before anything is reset. Not verified in a live window by me.

title: disasm replay --audio-out, and fix the frameshot audio tail bug
description:
`disasm replay` should write the replayed session's audio to a WAV, so a movie
can be compared by ear and by spectrum against a reference capture — the same
role `disasm frameshot --audio_out` plays for attract mode, but for gameplay.

Add `--audio-out <FILE>` to `replay`, reusing the existing write_wav helper.

MUST DRAIN PER FRAME, NOT ONCE AT THE END. SampleRing grows by doubling to
SampleRing::MAX_CAPACITY and then drops its OLDEST samples
(core/src/audio/ring.rs:10-14,41). The ceiling is about three seconds at 44.1 kHz.
So a run that only drains after the loop keeps roughly the last three seconds and
silently discards everything before it.

THE SAME LATENT BUG IS ALREADY IN `frameshot --audio_out`
(tools/disasm/src/main.rs, run_frameshot): it runs the whole frame loop and only
then loops fill_audio until empty. For the 1800-3100 frame captures that command
is normally used for, that is 30-50 seconds of emulated audio arriving as ~3
seconds of tail. Nobody has compared the printed sample count against the
expected rate x duration, so it has gone unnoticed. Fix both — drain inside the
frame loop — and verify by asserting the captured sample count is within a few
percent of frames / frame_rate x sample_rate rather than trusting the file looks
plausible.

Acceptance: a WAV from a several-thousand-frame replay contains the whole run,
not its tail; the sample count matches the run duration; and the same check
passes for frameshot.
close_reason: Fixed and verified empirically. frameshot --audio-out reported exactly 131072 samples (the SampleRing ceiling) for a 600-frame dkong run that should produce ~441000; after draining per frame it reports 436590. replay gained --audio-out on the corrected shared path; a 4152-frame dkong movie yields 3021202 samples matching its duration. Two ROM-gated regression tests assert a 600-frame capture exceeds twice the ring ceiling for both subcommands.

title: Rhai load_movie(): replay a recorded session from a script
description:
Add `m.load_movie(path)` to the Rhai surface, so a script can replay a recorded
session headlessly.

NEARLY FREE, and that is the point. DebugSession::run_frames already calls
self.harness.run_frame(), which already calls apply_scheduled_input ->
apply_movie_input. Movie delivery through Rhai therefore already worked; the only
missing piece was the binding.

THE WIN IS SAMPLING A RUN CHEAPLY. `disasm replay --frames N` re-runs from frame
0 for every sample, so hunting for a golden-pin frame costs a whole replay per
guess — 44 s a shot on a four-minute Marble Madness movie. A bound movie boots
once and walks forward: four samples of a 4324-frame Burger Time recording take
about 7 s, against ~11,600 frames replayed if each were its own `disasm replay`.
That matters directly for the golden-pin batch in .5.

Second use: scripted analysis at a gameplay moment. Watchpoints, the event ring,
hang detection, regs, disasm and poke are already in the Rhai surface, so
`load_movie(); run_frames(5000); watch(...); run_frames(100); events()` becomes
the headless, repeatable twin of the debugger workflow .7 enabled.

Checks, matching the frontend: refuse a movie recorded for another machine, and
one recorded against a different ROM dump, BEFORE resetting — a mistyped path
must not quietly destroy the session it was aimed at. The digest check is skipped
only when the session wraps a machine someone else booted (the in-frontend
console), which has no ROM path to re-derive it from.

Note the existing "rhai open() cold-boots, run_frames past the self-test" caveat
does not apply here: a movie starts at power-on and its boot period is part of
the recording.
close_reason: Landed. DebugSession::load_movie plus the Rhai binding; delivery already worked through run_frames -> harness.run_frame, so this was the binding and the guards only. Verified against a real 4324-frame burgertime capture: four samples in one boot in 7.1s. Documented in tools/script/README.md with examples/sample_movie.rhai. Two ROM-less tests: a bound movie is delivered by run_frames, and another machine's recording is refused without resetting the session.
