title: ESB: mid-game watchdog reset (~19s) from RAM buffer overrun into the stack
description:
Empire Strikes Back (esb) boots and plays, but ~19s into an actual game (start a game, e.g. Free Play + fire) the main CPU derails and the watchdog resets the board.

Reproduced headless at ~frame 934 (deterministic, input-independent). The boot-check does not catch it because a reboot still yields a stable non-empty vector list.

Failure mechanism (traced instruction-by-instruction):
- Bank-2 ROM code (~0xea00-0xed00) runs a RAM write loop with X in the MathRamLo region ($4800-$4FFF), around 0x4829.
- The write overruns into the CPU stack (S ~ 0x4fed, same $4800 region) and clobbers a stacked return address with 0x4e5f.
- A later RTS at 0x91c1 pops 0x4e5f and jumps into RAM -> garbage -> watchdog reset. (RTS/6809 are correct; they faithfully return the corrupted value.)

Ruled out:
- Not the 6809 / shared board logic (base Star Wars is unaffected).
- Not the slapstic alt/bitwise sequences (direct-banking-only reproduces identically).
- Not a bank-switch-mid-loop (slapstic bank stable at 1, bit4/bank2 at entry 0 throughout).
- Not input-driven (occurs with zero yoke input).
- Bank/ROM layout is byte-correct (CRC-validated load; interleaving matches MAME esb image).

Leading suspect: the overrun length/pointer derives from a value that is wrong only on ESB. Since ROM content and banking check out and the CPU is fine, the most ESB-specific compute path is the Matrix Processor running ESB's distinct mathbox PROMs (136031-107..110); a value it produces (read from $5000) may be feeding the bad write count/pointer.

Repro (headless): create the esb machine, set dsw1=0x00 (Free Play), press fire ~frame 100, run ~1000 frames; watch board.clock restart (watchdog) or cpu.pc return to the ~0xEExx boot entry.

Next step: disassemble the 0xea00-0xed00 write loop and trace the count/pointer back to its source (matrix output vs. a banked table).
notes:
2026-08-08 (see j63p.1 for the full trace): the "RAM buffer overrun into the
stack" framing in this issue's title/description is WRONG and should be retired.

There is no overrun. The failure is a cross-bank return landing in the wrong
slapstic bank: bank2:$9171 JSR $8295 -> bank1:$8298 -> bank1:$829B `JMP $8090`
(stay in bank 1) instead of bank2:$829B `JMP $80A0` (return to bank 2), so
execution resumes mid-routine at bank1:$9174 holding bank 2's X. The $4E5F that
the RTS at $91C1 pops is a stale-but-legitimate object pointer, not a clobbered
return address.

Also retire the leading suspect recorded here: it is not the mathbox. The
Matrix Processor output is not involved in the diverging path, and the ESB
mathbox PROMs were already confirmed to load in MAME order.

Our slapstic device model is byte-for-byte equivalent to MAME's for chip 101,
so the remaining suspect is the ADDRESS STREAM the M6809 presents to it -
specifically don't-care/VMA cycles. Next steps in j63p.1.
close_reason: Fixed in c08770a: M6809 don't-care cycles now drive the bus, so the ESB slapstic alt-banking sequence completes. Verified no derail over 4000 frames and zero watchdog expiries over 6000 frames of gameplay.

title: j63p: interrupt recognised one instruction late (frame 55, cycle 2045954)
description:
Investigation notes for j63p. Superseded the earlier "corrupting write" reading:
the derail is a WRONG-SLAPSTIC-BANK RETURN, not stack corruption.

REPRODUCTION (no source patch needed; DIPs are now exposed):
  disasm trace --machine esb --dip 'Coinage=Free Play' --press fire1@300:16 \
    --break-pc 0:0x4E5F --frames 3000 <roms>
  -> stops on --break-pc at frame 1129, cycle 41649243. Deterministic.
  Works from any --from-frame now that the cycle loop applies scheduled presses.
  Rhai equivalent: set_dip("Coinage","Free Play"); run_frames; step() + pc(0).

MECHANISM (traced instruction-by-instruction, frame 1129):
1. bank2:$9171 `JSR $8295` is a cross-bank trampoline. bank2:$8295 = `JSR $8090`;
   the opcode fetch at $8090 is a slapstic DIRECT bank select to bank 1, so the
   RTS at $8093 returns to $8298 read from bank 1.
2. Each bank carries its own copy of the return trampoline, and they differ:
     bank 1 $829B = `JMP $8090`  (stay in bank 1)
     bank 2 $829B = `JMP $80A0`  (return to bank 2)
   We execute bank 1's copy, so we never come back to bank 2.
3. Execution resumes at bank1:$9174 (`STA 6,X`) - the MIDDLE of bank 1's
   $9168 routine - carrying bank 2's X = $91C5, a ROM byte-table pointer that
   bank2:$91B1 `LDX #$91C3` / `ABX` had legitimately loaded.
4. That runs bank 1's $9156/$915E rotate chain, whose `RTS` at $91C1 (S=$4FED)
   pops a stale word - $4E5F - and jumps into RAM. Watchdog resets the board.

CORRECTIONS to the earlier notes:
- X = $4E5F is NOT garbage. It is a legitimate live object pointer in CPU RAM
  ($4800-$4FFF is plain RAM in MAME's map too), pushed and popped correctly
  many times per frame (10+ times over frames 1117-1129 with no derail). The
  PSHS at $9125/$B4CA are innocent.
- There is no RAM write-loop overrun into the stack. Conditional watchpoints
  on $4FED/$4FEE (=4E/=5F) show only ordinary PSHS traffic.
- "Slapstic bank stable at 1" was an artifact of looking at too small a window.
  The bank moves constantly: 1<->3 alternation early, with bank 2 appearing
  from frame 1025 on. First bank-2 entry is frame 1025 cyc 37801889.

RULED OUT (this pass):
- The slapstic DEVICE MODEL. Every chip-101 constant (bankstart 3; bank selects
  0080/0090/00A0/00B0; alt 1f00/1e00, 1fff/1fff, 1ffc/1b5c, 1fcf/0080, shift 0;
  bitwise 1ff0/1540 ... 1ff8/1550), the geometry (0x8000-0x9FFF, 8-bit bus,
  13 decoded lines -> shift 0), and all five state handlers are equivalent to
  MAME's atari_slapstic_device (src/mame/atari/slapstic.cpp). Idle, active_101_102
  and alt_valid_101_102 were compared line-by-line; test_in/test_any/test_bank/
  test_reset/test_inside build identical masks.
- Feeding the chip every CPU address (not just window accesses) is correct -
  MAME installs its tap over the whole address space too.
- The alt sequence being unreachable. It IS reachable: alt_valid needs
  (addr & 0x1FFF) == 0x1FFF outside the window, and $BFFF is executed from
  7 times in the run, most recently frame 1129 cyc 41647541 - 1700 cycles
  before the derail.

NEXT STEP: the divergence is in the ADDRESS STREAM fed to the chip, not the
chip. Two concrete leads, in order:
1. Instrument slapstic STATE transitions (not just committed bank changes) and
   check whether an alt/bitwise sequence is being started or broken at a
   different point than on hardware - especially around the $BFFF access at
   cyc 41647541 and the $9E00-$9EFF fetches (which match alt_start,
   test_in 0x1F00/0x1E00) at cyc 41648848-41648855.
2. Audit our M6809's bus cycles against MAME's for don't-care/VMA behaviour.
   Ours drives no address on don't-care cycles (the only $FFFF read left is the
   reset vector, mod.rs:618) after the TST fix in 9706bbc. Chip 101's alt step 2
   is documented as landing outside the window "in practice a 6809 dummy VMA
   access", so a missing or extra dummy access shifts the state machine by one.

TOOLING SHIPPED THIS PASS (all were blocking or actively misleading):
- StarWars/ESB DIP banks exposed (DSW0 is variant-specific, DSW1 shared), so
  Free Play no longer needs a source patch. `--dip` on `disasm trace`.
- `disasm trace` stop conditions now report where and why the run ended. They
  used to stop silently while the summary still advertised the full frame
  range, which reads exactly like "never fired" - this cost hours.
- The cycle loop now applies scheduled `--press`/`--move` edges (Harness gained
  apply_scheduled_input/advance_frame). Previously any press aimed past
  --from-frame was silently dropped in --cpu/--break-pc mode.
- starwars now emits debug events at all: slapstic BankSwitch (with the address
  that tipped it), LS259 bit-4 bank line, and watchdog pet/expire.
- StarWarsSystem::debug_pre_tick services the pending sound-CPU reset, which
  run_frame did and debug_tick did not - the machine behaved differently under
  the debugger than at full speed.
notes: ROOT CAUSE FOUND — see phosphor-emulator-vy6l. The M6809 does not drive $FFFF on don't-care/VMA cycles, so ESB's slapstic alt-banking sequence can never complete its 'valid' step, the game never reaches bank 2 by that path, and the cross-bank return lands in bank 1 where $9174 is 'STA 6,X' instead of bank 2's 'RTS'. Established by tracing MAME 0.287 in actual gameplay (Lua harness; the notifier subscription must be stored in a global or it is garbage-collected) and finding it executes bank 1's $829B then bank 2's $9174 — a 1->2 bank change with no access to $80A0, which only the alt sequence can produce. j63p is now blocked on vy6l.
close_reason: Investigation complete; j63p fixed in c08770a. Notes retain the full path, including three wrong root-cause claims and the two tooling bugs that caused them.

title: Donkey Kong music: peaks 5.5 dB above the board's while the sustained level sits 4.9 dB below
description:
Found while checking that the new shared mixer/amplifier stages had not muffled the music. They had not — the spectrum now matches closely (centroid 143.0 Hz against 146.8, fundamental 188.5 against 186.8, band split 45/54 against 52/47, no band out of tolerance). The LEVEL is the problem, and in two directions at once.

Measured over a gameplay capture on the same schedule (tools/script/examples/dkong_walk_gameplay.rhai against tools/sound-reference/drive_dkong_gameplay.lua), standing still so it is music only:

                    ours      board
  AC RMS         -22.51 dB  -17.65 dB
  peak            -0.79 dB   -6.29 dB
  crest factor       12.19       3.70
  silent %            22.1        4.2

So the sustained music is 4.9 dB quiet while isolated peaks run 5.5 dB hot, and our crest factor is 3.3x the board's. Something in the DAC path emits transients the board does not, and they are what is consuming the headroom.

This blocks a straightforward fix to the balance. Now that all three effects are calibrated against the board's absolute levels, DAC_GAIN should come up ~4.9 dB to put the music on the same scale — but the peak is already at -0.79 dBFS, so raising it clips. The transient has to be understood first.

Note 22.1 % of our capture measures silent against the board's 4.2 %, which points the same way: our DAC output is gappy where the board's is continuous. Suspect the I8035 DAC feed (box-filtered sample path into feed_dac) or the discharge line, which the TKG-04 model wires but does not drive (dkong_sound.rs, DkongInputs::discharge) — on the board that line bleeds the DAC between samples through Q7/R20/C32, and not driving it could plausibly leave steps where the board has a decay.
close_reason:
Fixed. The cause was a missing stage, exactly as this issue suspected: the DAC's signal-decay circuit (Q7 across 10 kOhm and 10 uF) was allocated as a logic input and never driven, because the TKG-04 board never called set_discharge.

The sound CPU drops its port 2 bit 7 when a sample finishes and the board fades the DAC over tau = 100 ms. Ending a sample on a step instead is a click, and those clicks were consuming the headroom the music was being attenuated to leave.

                    before      now      board
  AC RMS         -22.51 dB  -18.00 dB  -17.65 dB
  peak            -0.79 dB   -7.02 dB   -6.29 dB
  crest factor       12.19       3.54       3.70

With the peaks 6.6 dB lower there was room for the music to simply be the board's level, so DAC_GAIN stops being a compromise (0.55 -> 1.213) and every voice on the machine is now calibrated against the board rather than against what sounds balanced.

REMAINING, and separate from this issue's claims: our capture still measures silent 18.7 % of the time against the board's 4.2 %, and the band split is 39/61 against 52/47 below and above 150 Hz. Both say something is still absent in quiet passages rather than mis-levelled. Worth its own issue if anyone pursues the DAC path further; the level, peak and crest questions this issue was opened for are closed.

title: phosphor-disasm tests do not compile: run_trace() call sites are one argument short
description:
Pre-existing on main (confirmed by stashing unrelated work and rebuilding), not
caused by any current change — noticed while running `cargo test --workspace`
for phosphor-emulator-vy6l.

`cargo test -p phosphor-disasm` fails to build with 8 x E0061: `run_trace` takes
19 arguments, the test call sites in tools/disasm/src/trace.rs (~line 1585
onwards) supply 18. Argument #13, `Option<&str>`, is missing — a parameter was
added to `run_trace` without updating its own test module.

`cargo build` is unaffected, which is why it went unnoticed: only the test
target breaks. Consequence is that the whole phosphor-disasm test suite has
been silently not running.
close_reason: Fixed in two commits. (1) The 8 run_trace call sites in trace::tests were missing the entropy_file argument added by e4d39d9; passing None at each restores the build and all 42 disasm tests pass, with no pre-existing failures hiding behind the break. (2) Removed the root cause: run_trace now takes a named TraceOptions struct (Default + new(machine, path)) instead of 19 positional args, so a future parameter cannot silently shift or omit an argument at a call site. Verified cargo test --workspace --no-run builds every target; clippy and fmt clean.

title: M6809: CWAI and the interrupt vector sequence are short of cycles
close_reason: CWAI gains the two don't-care cycles between its operand read and its pushes (16 to the wait state, was 14), and the vector-only wake path gains the /VMA cycle on each side of the vector fetch (5 to resume, was 3). Both sequences confirmed against MAME's base6x09.lst first. Covered by a test that asserts the whole bus trace rather than the totals, since a cycle count can balance out two errors, and this is the only coverage these paths can have: a single-step vector cannot express an interrupt arriving, so CWAI and SYNC are outside cross-validation.

comments.author: pjl
comments.text:
2026-08-23: FIXED. Both sequences confirmed against MAME's base6x09.lst before
touching anything, and they are exactly as this issue transcribed them.

  CWAI:                        INTERRUPT_VECTOR:
    @m_cc &= read_opcode_arg();  @dummy_vma(1);
    @dummy_read_opcode_arg(0);   @m_pc.b.h = read_vector(0);
    @dummy_vma(1);               @m_pc.b.l = read_vector(1);
    %PUSH_REGISTERS;             @dummy_vma(1);

CWAI (op_cwai) gains the two don't-care cycles between the operand read and the
pushes: one re-driving PC, one at $FFFF. 1 fetch + 15 execute = 16 cycles to
reach the wait state, where it was 14.

The vector-only path (execute_interrupt cycles 20-23, reached only from CWAI's
wake) gains the /VMA cycle on each side of the vector fetch, which the full
NMI/IRQ/FIRQ entries already had at their cycles 14/17 and 5/8. Resuming from
CWAI is 5 cycles where it was 3: one to notice the request, then the bracketed
fetch.

Checked while in there and NOT changed: the wait state itself drives no address.
MAME's eat_remaining() only burns m_icount, so ours matches.

THE TEST IS A SEQUENCE, not a count, and that is the part worth keeping. Five
existing CWAI tests hard-coded 14 and 3, so they failed and were updated, but a
total can be right for the wrong reason: drop two don't-care cycles and add two
elsewhere and it balances exactly. InterruptBus now records every access in
order, and cwai_and_its_wake_drive_the_addresses_the_hardware_drives asserts the
whole trace:

  entry  0x0000 r (opcode), 0x0001 r (operand), 0x0002 r (PC re-drive),
         0xFFFF r (/VMA), then 12 writes 0x00FF..0x00F4
  wait   nothing at all, asserted explicitly
  wake   0xFFFF r, 0xFFF8 r, 0xFFF9 r, 0xFFFF r

That is the only coverage these two paths can have. A single-step vector cannot
express "and then an interrupt arrives", so CWAI and SYNC are excluded from
cross-validation entirely, which is why the gap survived this long.

Green: phosphor-core 80 test targets, m6809 cross-validation 266,000 vectors
across 266 opcode files, clippy, fmt. The M6809 README now records CWAI's cycle
shape and why it has a hand-written timing test rather than a validator.

title: CMOS inverter relaxation oscillator primitive (both Donkey Kong wobbles are measured, not derived)
description:
Donkey Kong has two CMOS inverter relaxation oscillators wobbling its 555 control voltages, and after the jump and walk rebuilds BOTH carry a rate that was measured off the board rather than derived from their parts. That is the only such number left in either chain and it is the same gap twice.

  voice  inverters  R_timing  R_bias  C       tau     measured period  ratio
  jump   3          18 k      3.3 M   3.3 uF  59.4 ms  110 ms          1.85 tau
  walk   2          4.3 k     43 k    10 uF   43 ms     87 ms          2.02 tau

The period is a fixed multiple of R_timing*C, but the multiple depends on where
the inverter chain's effective switching thresholds land, and that depends on
the device's transfer characteristic and on how many inverters are in cascade.
Taking the datasheet thresholds (a third and two thirds of supply) gives 3.54
tau for jump — half the real rate.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS. Both were wrong before, in the same direction
and for the same reason: someone read the RC corner (1/(2*pi*R*C)) as the
oscillator rate. Jump was 8.4 Hz against 9.09; walk was 1.16 Hz against 11.5,
a factor of ten, which does not read as a slow wobble but as no wobble at all.
A primitive that takes component values and gets the period right removes the
whole class.

SHAPE. A NodeKind modelling the standard three-or-two inverter RC oscillator:
timing resistor, bias resistor, capacitor, supply, and an inverter description
(output low/high, input rise/fall thresholds, input protection clamp). Output is
the last inverter's level, so a square. Two details the current stand-ins miss:
  - DUTY. The board's is not symmetric. Walk measures ~40/60 because its bias
    resistor is only 10x its timing resistor; jump's is 183x and measures even.
    fixed_square cannot express this, and it is why walk's duty is recorded as a
    known simplification in dkong_sound.rs.
  - The capacitor node swings well outside the rails, so the input protection
    clamp is part of the timing, not a detail.

OTHER USERS: radarscp has the same two oscillators, and Mario Bros' sound board
uses the same part. So this is shared, not dkong-specific.

Closing this lets WALK_LFO_HZ and JUMP_LFO_HZ stop being measured constants and
become consequences of the parts, which is the standard the rest of both chains
now meets.
close_reason:
Done for the rate, NOT for the duty — read on before assuming it is fully solved.

Added inverter_osc: a CMOS relaxation oscillator built from the timing network and the gate's datasheet transfer characteristic. Both Donkey Kong wobbles now derive their rate from component values; WALK_LFO_HZ and JUMP_LFO_HZ are gone.

Three models were checked against both circuits BEFORE writing it, which is what makes this a prediction rather than a fit:

                                    jump (110 ms)      walk (87 ms)
  ideal mid-supply threshold        130.5 (+19 %)      94.0 (+8 %)
  datasheet thresholds as hysteresis 209.9 (+91 %)     51.5 (-41 %)
  gate transfer curve               110.5 (+0.5 %)     84.4 (-3.0 %)

Only the transfer curve reproduces the difference between the three-gate and two-gate versions — 1.85 tau against 1.96. An ideal threshold gives 2.20 tau for both and cannot tell them apart, which is the evidence that the gate's gain does the work.

WHAT THIS ISSUE CLAIMED AND DID NOT DELIVER: the duty. The board holds walk's low pitch for about 60 % of each cycle; the model produces 53/47 from the same bias-resistor mechanism that ought to explain it. So the period falls out of the components and the duty does not. Recorded in dkong_sound.rs beside the oscillator rather than left implicit. Whatever skews those half cycles is not in this model, and a new issue should be opened if it ever matters audibly — it does not today.

title: audio_sanity_test takes 7 minutes and is the cost of every local test run
description:
harness/tests/audio_sanity_test.rs runs 5 tests in 431 seconds. It is ROM-gated, so CI never pays that and every local `cargo test --workspace` does. It is currently about three quarters of the wall time of a full run, and it dominates work that cannot possibly affect audio: a change to the vector display list pays seven minutes to prove the POKEYs still make noise.

The failure mode is not that the test is wrong, it is that a test this slow stops being run. Anyone iterating will start scoping their runs by hand, which is fine until the day they scope out the thing they broke.

Worth working out where the time goes before deciding what to do. Likely candidates: it boots several machines from ROM and runs each for a long stretch to accumulate enough audio to judge, and the run length may be set by what a spectrum needs rather than by what the assertion needs. If most of it is boot-to-attract, an NVRAM fixture would cut it the way frameshot --nvram does elsewhere.

Options, roughly in order of preference:
1. Make it faster. If the assertions only need a second or two of audio each, the frame counts are the thing to look at.
2. Split it: a quick check that each machine produces audio at all in the normal run, and the expensive spectral work behind its own opt-in, run when the sound path changes.
3. Leave it and document that a full local run costs eight minutes, so nobody is surprised into skipping tests entirely.

Noticed while doing vector rendering work, where every iteration was costing ten minutes for tests that could not be affected by any of it.
close_reason: 431s to 27.1s, and measuring more than before: the suite was sweeping the roster twice (OnceLock), now runs one machine per core, and the movie collection was re-recorded shorter. No assertion was weakened and nothing was truncated. Remaining floor is docastle being the slowest board per frame, not a long recording.

comments.author: pjl
comments.text:
Resolved. The suite ran 5 tests in 431s when this was filed; it now runs 11 in
27.1s, and it measures strictly more than it did.

  wall           431s -> 27.1s
  CPU                 -> 339.0s
  parallelism         -> 12.5x (of 16 cores)
  coverage    23 movie fixtures -> 40

Three things did it, and the first was not what this issue predicted.

1. THE SUITE WAS EMULATING THE WHOLE ROSTER TWICE. sweep() is a plain function
   and both ratchet tests call it, and libtest runs those two on separate
   threads. Its doc comment already said "Measure every machine once, then
   judge", so the intent was there and the implementation did not match it. A
   OnceLock was half the saving before any other change (880429f).
2. The sweep now runs one machine per core (880429f), and a wasted second
   decompression of every ROM zip is gone (0fc0f35).
3. The movie collection was re-recorded shorter and deliberately played:
   90,641 frames over 40 machines against 170,322 over 23. Galaga alone had been
   26,386 frames, 7m20s of recorded play, and was the entire wall time.

This issue's own preferred option was "make it faster, the assertions may only
need a second or two of audio". That turned out not to need deciding: nothing
was truncated and no assertion changed, so the suite still judges whole recorded
sessions. See phosphor-emulator-audio-movie-span-wa38, closed alongside.

WHAT IS LEFT IS NOT SPEED. The floor is now docastle at 23.3s, which is the
slowest board per frame in the tree (153 frames/sec against dkong's 393), not a
long recording, and the sweep finishes within 4s of that floor.

The remaining problem is that the movies are not committed, so both this timing
and that coverage are properties of one developer's machine. A contributor with
no collection falls back to input-free boot on every machine, where the silence
check does not apply, and sees the same green run. That is not hypothetical:
mrdo passed clean for the entire life of this suite because its fixture measured
a silent attract mode, and it turned out to have a missing coupling capacitor
worth +0.183 of DC (059ec78).

title: The CPU-observable assertions: VBLANK, IRQ4, and the placeable IRQ3
description:
The assertions whose verdict is a word in RAM, so they need no framebuffer and
can pass on landing.

Depends on the skeleton (.1). Each of these is a phase in the ROM and a separate
#[test] in the harness, the way the Williams suite is arranged: ten separate test
functions rather than one collecting assertions, so the runner reports "these two
signals moved and these four did not" for free.

T1 - THE VBLANK LEVEL. Poll 0xF60000 bit 4 (active low, atari_system1.rs:736-749)
across a frame and record the transition count and the dwell either side. The
board raises VBLANK at scanline 240 of 262, so the expectation is one falling and
one rising edge per frame with the blanked span about 22/262 of it. This is the
frame-synchronisation primitive everything else keys off, so it is measured
first.

T2 - THE VBLANK INTERRUPT. IRQ4 fires once per frame at scanline 240
(atari_system1.rs:1103-1105) and is held until acked at 8A0001. Count handler
entries per frame and confirm the ack clears it; an unacked IRQ4 should re-enter
immediately, which is a second thing worth asserting because it is the shape of
bug that hides behind a working game.

T3 - THE PROGRAMMABLE SCANLINE INTERRUPT, and this is the load-bearing one.
Write a motion-object timer entry (0xFFFF in word 1) whose band computes to a
chosen line, then confirm IRQ3 fires there. The band formula is
`(256 - (word0 >> 5) - vsize * 8 - 1) & 0x1FF`, so pick word0 to land on a known
line and assert against that line, not against whatever the code computes.

Assert it at more than one line. A single placement can be satisfied by an
interrupt that fires at a fixed scanline and ignores the list entirely, which is
exactly the wrong thing to pin, so use at least two well-separated lines and
require the interrupt to move with them.

T4 - THE ONE-SCANLINE WIDTH. 0x2E0000 bit 7 reads the IRQ3 state
(atari_system1.rs:781-783), and the board asserts it for exactly the line the
entry targets. Poll it across a frame and confirm it reads set on one line and
clear on the others. This is the assertion that distinguishes a real one-line
pulse from a level that latches until acked.

T5 - THE READ-TWICE ASYMMETRY. The timer interrupt reads live sprite RAM while
the compositor renders from mo_shadow, copied at the start of vblank
(atari_system1.rs:1135-1145). So a timer entry written mid-frame changes the
interrupt in the frame it is written and the picture only in the next. Assert
both halves: the interrupt moves this frame, and the rendered result does not.

The second half of T5 needs the framebuffer, so it can be split into .3 if it
turns out to depend on per-scanline rendering. Check that before assuming: it may
not, since it is about which copy of a list is read rather than about when a line
is drawn.

ACCEPTANCE. Each expectation carries its derivation in the test's doc comment,
and each figure is marked as derived from our source rather than from a
schematic, because that is what it is until someone checks it. The Williams doc's
risk 1 applies here word for word: this makes the suite a regression guard
immediately and a correctness guard only after that check.

Every one of these should be made to fail on purpose before being trusted. The
cheapest mutations: move VBLANK_SCANLINE, make timer_irq_at_scanline return true
unconditionally, and hold scanline_int set for a whole frame instead of one line.

title: M6809 TST memory ops: dummy VMA cycle disagrees with test vectors, aborting the validation suite
description:
`cargo test -p phosphor-cpu-validation` fails on the very first M6809 mismatch and, because `test_all_opcodes` panics on first failure, every opcode after 0x0D goes unchecked. Pre-existing on main; found while verifying the DRY 1 macro refactor (phosphor-emulator-dry-refactors-0lhx.1), which is not the cause.

SYMPTOM
  m6809_single_step_test: `0d 4b: cycle 5 (bus 3) addr  left: 65535  right: 59211`
  (0xFFFF vs 0xE74B, the DP:addr effective address)

SCOPE — all 3000 cases of the three TST memory forms fail, and only these:
  test_data/m6809/0d.json  1000/1000  TST direct    (bus3 addr/data/op)
  test_data/m6809/6d.json  1000/1000  TST indexed   (bus3 addr/data/op)
  test_data/m6809/7d.json  1000/1000  TST extended  (bus4 addr/data/op)
  The other 263 opcode files pass 1000/1000.

CAUSE
TST shares RMW timing but must not write back, so `rmw_direct`/`rmw_indexed`/`rmw_extended` in core/src/cpu/m6809/alu.rs special-case it into a dummy read at 0xFFFF (see rmw_direct cycle 4, core/src/cpu/m6809/alu.rs:650-659). The checked-in vectors still encode the older behaviour — a read of the effective address on that cycle. Vectors are self-generated (cpu-validation/src/bin/gen_m6809_tests.rs drives our own M6809), so they went stale when the dummy-cycle address changed and were never regenerated.

WHICH SIDE IS RIGHT
The stale vectors PASS cross-validation against the reference emulator (0d 1000/1000, 7d 1000/1000, 6d 998/1000), i.e. the reference also re-reads the EA on that cycle. On real hardware a /VMA cycle drives 0xFFFF on the address bus, so the current emulator matches the datasheet and the reference does not. Per CLAUDE.md (\"if cross-validation differs from datasheet for timings, use the datasheet values\") the emulator behaviour looks correct and the vectors should be regenerated — but confirm against the 6809 datasheet cycle-by-cycle table before regenerating, since this permanently forks these three opcodes from the reference.

SUGGESTED FIX
1. Confirm the datasheet lists the final TST cycle as VMA/0xFFFF.
2. Regenerate: cargo run -p phosphor-cpu-validation --bin gen_m6809_tests -- all (or just 0d/6d/7d).
3. Re-run cross-validation and record the expected 0d/6d/7d divergence so it is not mistaken for a regression later.
4. Consider whether the dummy cycle should be emitted as BusOp::Internal rather than a real read, so the vector format distinguishes VMA cycles from genuine bus reads.

ALSO WORTH FIXING
`test_all_opcodes` aborting on the first bad case hides all later coverage. Collecting failures and reporting a per-opcode summary would have caught this being masked.
notes:
CORRECTION to the original report: the M6809 vectors are NOT checked in.
.gitignore line 3 ignores cpu-validation/test_data/, so test_data/m6809/*.json
are locally-generated artifacts (the test panics with a 'run gen_m6809_tests'
message if the directory is absent). The stale vectors were therefore a stale
LOCAL working copy predating the TST dummy-cycle change, not committed data --
a fresh checkout regenerating from scratch would have passed on main.

That does not change the fix, which stands on its own merits:
  - the three TST /VMA cycles were the only don't-care cycles in the M6809 that
    drove a real bus transaction, and that inconsistency is now gone;
  - the datasheet confirmation above is unaffected;
  - the test-harness summary and the README corrections are unaffected.

It does mean nothing needs committing under cpu-validation/test_data/.
close_reason:
Confirmed against the MC6809E datasheet and fixed.

DATASHEET CONFIRMATION (step 1)
Figure 17, Cycle-by-Cycle Performance, sheet 5 of 5 lists the two groups side
by side:
  ASL/ASR/CLR/COM/DEC/INC/LSL/LSR/NEG/ROL/ROR (all except immediate):
    Data(EA) / Don't Care(FFFF) / Data Write(EA)
  TST (all except immediate):
    Data(EA) / Don't Care(FFFF) / Don't Care(FFFF)
So TST's final cycle is a don't-care /VMA cycle, not a store and not an EA
re-read. The emulator was right; the vectors were stale.
Table 9 also confirms the counts: 0D=6, 6D=6+, 7D=7 -- unchanged.

FIX
- core/src/cpu/m6809/alu.rs: the three TST special cases in rmw_direct /
  rmw_indexed / rmw_extended now emit a true internal cycle instead of
  'bus.read(master, 0xFFFF)'. This resolves step 4 of the issue: they were the
  only three /VMA cycles in the whole M6809 that drove a real bus transaction,
  so a dummy read could disturb memory-mapped I/O at 0xFFFF while every other
  don't-care cycle stayed silent. The vector format now distinguishes them as
  "internal". Cycle counts are unchanged.
- Regenerated 0d/6d/7d vectors (step 2). cargo test -p phosphor-cpu-validation
  passes; full workspace test, clippy and fmt are clean.

CROSS-VALIDATION (step 3) -- no fork, contrary to the issue's expectation
The concern about permanently forking these three opcodes from the reference
does not apply: the cross-validator does not compare bus traces at all (it
checks registers, final memory at accessed addresses, and total cycle count),
and the cycle count is identical either way. Post-fix numbers are exactly the
pre-existing baseline: 0d 1000/1000, 7d 1000/1000, 6d 998/1000.

The residual 6d 2/1000 is NOT TST-related. A full sweep gives 264,090/266,000
with 53 indexed opcodes failing, all one cause: postbyte 0x9F ([n] extended
indirect), where the datasheet's Table 2 says +5 cycles and the reference core
charges +8. Datasheet wins, so phosphor is correct. Filed as
phosphor-emulator-oyxg and documented in cpu-validation/README_m6809.md.

ALSO FIXED
- cpu-validation/tests/m6809_single_step_test.rs now collects failures and
  panics with a per-opcode summary (counts + up to 3 example cases) instead of
  aborting on the first bad assertion. This immediately showed the failure was
  confined to 0d/6d/7d with the other 263 opcodes passing.
- cpu-validation/README_m6809.md: recorded the known [n] divergence and the TST
  bus-trace note, and corrected two stale claims -- it advertised
  '266,000/266,000 (100%)' and credited elmerucr/MC6809, but the validator
  actually compiles mame0148/src/emu/cpu/m6809/m6809.c.

title: Mirror MAME function keys, add shift chords, fix text-field capture
description:
Two problems, one file cluster.

1. Our hotkeys drifted from MAME by one slot across the throttle/FPS/profiler
   group, and F5 means the opposite of what it means in MAME: reset here, pause
   there. Muscle memory from MAME actively hurts here.
2. Host hotkeys never consult video.wants_keyboard(), so a host hotkey on a
   printable key fires while an egui text field has focus. Typing a watch
   address into the debug panel steps the CPU on 7, toggles run/pause on 0, and
   the same defect hits / (legend), ` (DIP panel), P (pause) and Tab (settings).
   Function keys are immune only because egui types no text from them.

DECIDED WITH THE REQUESTER. Do not relitigate any of these without asking.

- Full MAME layout, not a partial fix.
- Our extra actions move onto MAME homes where one exists.
- Shift only. No ctrl or alt chords, so MAME RCtrl+RAlt and Shift+Ctrl+F12 are
  deliberately not expressible.
- Mouse grab goes on Scroll Lock. MAME has no equivalent (its RCtrl+RAlt needs
  modifiers we are not modelling); Scroll Lock is MAME Toggle UI Controls, the
  nearest surviving idea of who owns the input device, and no game wants it.
- Hard reset is implemented for real, not aliased to the soft reset.
- Frame advance is a NEW global action on Shift+F5, stepping the frontend pause,
  distinct from the debugger run-mode StepFrame.
- Debugger run/pause moves to bare F8, its step keys to Shift+F8/9/10.
- Shift+F4 stays UNBOUND and reserved for rewind. See sequencing below.

PRIMARY SOURCE. READ IT FIRST.

MAME defaults live in ~/ws/mame/src/emu/inpttype.ipp: the UI block at lines 893
to 946, plus line 625 where SERVICE is KEYCODE_F2 and is a MACHINE input, not a
UI key. Read that block before touching DEFAULTS.

MAME guards its plain keys with not_code KEYCODE_LSHIFT, so bare F5 fires only
when shift is up. Chord matching must therefore be EXACT on the modifier state,
not "at least these modifiers". Two MAME entries are inconsistent about this:
UI_SHOW_FPS guards only LSHIFT and not RSHIFT, and UI_FRAMESKIP_INC guards
neither. We match exactly everywhere. Do not reproduce those two.

TARGET LAYOUT

  Esc         Quit                     MAME UI_CANCEL
  F1          Debug panel              ours; MAME F1 is help/audit, dead in game
  Shift+F1    unbound
  F2          UNBOUND, freed so a machine can bind a service switch (MAME F2)
  F3          Reset (soft)             MAME UI_SOFT_RESET
  Shift+F3    Hard reset (NEW)         MAME UI_RESET_MACHINE
  F4          UNBOUND, reserved for an in-session gfx viewer (MAME UI_SHOW_GFX)
  Shift+F4    UNBOUND, reserved for rewind (MAME UI_REWIND_SINGLE)
  F5          Pause                    MAME UI_PAUSE
  Shift+F5    Frame advance (NEW)      MAME UI_PAUSE_SINGLE
  F6          Quick save               MAME UI_SAVE_STATE
  F7          Quick load               MAME UI_LOAD_STATE
  F8          Debugger run/pause       ours; MAME F8 is frameskip dec, we have none
  Shift+F8    Debugger step cycle      ours
  F9          UNBOUND                  MAME frameskip inc, we have none
  Shift+F9    Debugger step instruction  ours
  F10         Frame throttle           MAME UI_THROTTLE
  Shift+F10   Debugger step frame      ours
  F11         FPS overlay              MAME UI_SHOW_FPS
  Shift+F11   Profiler                 MAME UI_SHOW_PROFILER
  F12         Screenshot               MAME UI_SNAPSHOT
  Shift+F12   Record input movie       MAME UI_RECORD_MNG
  ScrollLock  Grab mouse               approximates MAME UI_TOGGLE_UI
  Tab         Settings panel           MAME UI_MENU
  `           DIP panel                ours; MAME ~ is OSD sliders / debug break
  /           Key legend               ours
  P 7 8 9 0   FREED. These reach the machine now.

Deviations to state in the source, not to quietly absorb:
- MAME F6/F7 prompt for a save slot and Shift+F6/F7 are the quick variants. We
  have one slot, so our single quick save/load takes the BARE key. Semantically
  ours is MAME Shift+F6. Shift+F6 and Shift+F7 stay unbound.
- F8/F9 carry debugger actions where MAME carries frameskip, which we do not
  implement. The parity claim has a footnote there and the footnote belongs in
  host_keys.rs.

STAGE 1. Chord model.

frontend/src/host_keys.rs today is one bare Scancode per action:
HostBindings.overrides is HashMap<String, i32> (line 143), action_for takes a
Scancode (line 167), key_for returns Option<Scancode> (line 158).

Introduce HostChord { scancode, shift: bool } with exact-match semantics.
Touches, all of which must move together:
- host_keys.rs: DEFAULTS, key_for, action_for, rebind, conflicts, key_label
  (needs a "Shift+F5" rendering).
- state.rs:77, which persists HostBindings into state.toml.
- emulator.rs:619-930, the 19 dispatch arms, which must read keymod.
- emulator.rs:520-539, hotkey capture. TODAY THIS WOULD BIND SHIFT ITSELF: it
  takes the first KeyDown, and pressing shift produces one. Capture must ignore
  bare modifier presses and record the modifier state of the first non-modifier
  key.
- settings_ui.rs:187 and :237, the settings grid and the key legend.

MIGRATION. state.toml holds existing user rebinds as bare integers. Deserialize
must accept a bare i32 as { scancode, shift: false }. A bug here silently eats
somebody rebinds, which is the exact hazard called out in
phosphor-emulator-contained-fidelity-np9x.6. Coordinate with that issue: it wants
migration round-trip tests and frontend/tests/ is still empty.

STAGE 2. The wants_keyboard guard. This is the bug fix and it is independent of
the layout, so it can land first and be verified on its own.

DispatchCtx.egui_wants_keyboard (input.rs:551, checked at input.rs:588) guards
GAME input only, and is built in the last match arm (emulator.rs:987). Every
host arm above it is unguarded. The only keyboard guard on the host arms is
console_state.visible (emulator.rs:568).

Rule to implement: while video.wants_keyboard() is true, suppress every host
hotkey EXCEPT those whose scancode egui never consumes, which is F1 through F12
plus ScrollLock. That is what keeps the moved debugger keys live during text
entry while killing the 7/0//`/P/Tab misfires.

Escape needs a decision and a sentence in the source: today Escape quits even
with a field focused. Under this rule it would be suppressed, so Escape defocuses
the field first and quits on the second press, which is conventional. Say so out
loud rather than letting it be discovered.

STAGE 3. Layout. Rewrite DEFAULTS to the table above. Update the tests in
host_keys.rs that pin the old keys: defaults_resolve_both_ways (line 225),
every_default_key_is_unique (becomes chord uniqueness),
rebinding_frees_the_old_key_for_the_machine,
step_keys_run_in_order_of_increasing_granularity (the 7/8/9 rationale comment at
lines 85-93 is now wrong and its replacement must explain Shift+F8/9/10),
key_labels_print_the_key_cap_not_the_scancode_name, reset_restores_factory_keys.

conflicts() changes meaning: a shifted chord can no longer shadow a machine key,
so only bare chords are reportable. That is a real improvement (Shift+F6 stops
stealing F6 from a machine) and the test must assert it, not just the old case.

STAGE 4. Hard reset on Shift+F3. A rebuild from ROM, not machine.reset(). The
movie arm path already does a deferred rebuild while the machine is borrowed for
the frame (emulator.rs:737-747, arm_requested); reuse that shape. Must set
needs_resync, for the reason spelled out at emulator.rs:721-728.

STAGE 5. Frame advance on Shift+F5. Steps the FRONTEND pause (emulator.rs:913),
not debug_state.run_mode. New HostAction::FrameAdvance, not debugger-modal.

WHAT WOULD MAKE EACH CHECK FAIL. Add none of these without watching it fail once.

- Exact modifier match: a test that Shift+F5 does NOT resolve to Pause and that
  bare F5 does NOT resolve to FrameAdvance. Break it by matching with contains()
  instead of equality and confirm both assertions go red.
- Migration: a state.toml fixture holding the OLD bare-integer form, asserted to
  load as shift:false and to still resolve. Break it by removing the untagged
  fallback and confirm the parse fails rather than silently returning defaults.
  A migration test that constructs its input from the new serializer cannot fail
  and is worthless; the fixture must be a literal string.
- Guard: assert the predicate directly, that a bare printable chord is
  suppressed under wants_keyboard and an F-key chord is not. A test that only
  checks the F-key case passes with the guard deleted.
- Chord uniqueness across DEFAULTS, which is the existing test widened to the
  (scancode, shift) pair.

SEQUENCING

- phosphor-emulator-rewind-jgqx.3 specifies HostAction::Rewind as a HOLD binding
  on R. MAME puts rewind-single-step on Shift+F4. This issue reserves Shift+F4
  and binds nothing. jgqx.3 has to decide between a hold-to-scrub on R and MAME
  parity, and it now has a chord model available either way. A comment goes on
  jgqx.3 saying so.
- phosphor-emulator-contained-fidelity-np9x.6 owns state.toml migration testing.
  Whoever lands second inherits the other tests. Do not write two migration
  frameworks.
- phosphor-emulator-input-movie-no93 owns the movie record action that moves
  from F2 to Shift+F12. No behaviour change, binding only.

NOT IN SCOPE

- Frameskip (MAME F8/F9), fast forward (MAME Insert), cheats (MAME Shift+F8),
  save-state slot selection (MAME F6/F7 prompt), AVI recording. We do not have
  these features; the keys stay unbound rather than being faked.
- An in-session graphics viewer on F4. gfxview exists but only as a CLI mode
  (main.rs:161-175). F4 is reserved, not implemented.
- A machine-side service switch on F2. This issue only frees the key; binding it
  is a machines-crate control-table change.
- Ctrl and Alt chords.

VERIFICATION. Frontend only, so no board, core device or CPU is touched and the
ROM-gated suites are not required for correctness here. Run the workspace clippy
and test lines. The end state is judged by hand: open the debug panel, focus the
watch-address field, type 7 and 0 and confirm the CPU does not step, then press
Shift+F8 and confirm it does.

A NOTE ON THE HOUSE RULE. Repo convention is not to cite MAME in source comments
and to describe the hardware directly. That rule exists to stop MAME being used
as a hardware authority. This is a UI convention, not hardware, and the whole
point of the change is to match what users already know, so naming MAME in
host_keys.rs is correct here. Make that call consciously rather than by accident.

comments.author: pjl
comments.text:
Implemented across four commits on branch mame-function-keys. All five stages
landed; nothing from the plan was dropped.

WHAT THE SOURCE SAID

MAME UI defaults are ~/ws/mame/src/emu/inpttype.ipp lines 893 to 946, plus 625
where SERVICE is KEYCODE_F2 as a machine input. Two things only visible by
reading it:

- Plain keys carry not_code KEYCODE_LSHIFT, so bare F5 fires only with shift up.
  Chord matching therefore has to be exact equality, not a subset test.
- Two entries are inconsistent about that guard. UI_SHOW_FPS (line 926) guards
  LSHIFT but not RSHIFT, so Right-Shift+F11 shows the FPS counter rather than the
  profiler. UI_FRAMESKIP_INC (923) guards neither. Matched exactly everywhere
  here and did not reproduce those.

WHAT THE BUG ACTUALLY WAS

Wider than reported. DispatchCtx::egui_wants_keyboard existed and was correct,
but it is consumed inside input::dispatch, which is the LAST arm of the event
match (emulator.rs:987 before the change). All nineteen hotkey arms matched
ahead of it. So it was not only 7/8/9/0: /, `, P and Tab misfired the same way
while any egui text field had focus. Function keys were immune only because egui
types nothing from them.

Fixed at the root by dropping a guarded KeyDown above the whole match, exempting
the keys egui makes no use of (F1-F12, ScrollLock). Deliberately KeyDown only:
input.rs:593-597 already documents that a guarded release strands a held key on.

FOUND WHILE WORKING, NOT IN THE ORIGINAL PLAN

1. rebind() displacement was broken. Rebinding onto a taken key wrote
   Scancode::Escape into the displaced action instead of unbinding it, so the
   settings panel showed that action sitting on Escape and pressing Escape quit
   (Quit resolves first in DEFAULTS). Could not be carried into the new format
   without encoding a wrong value, so it is now a real unbound list. TOML has no
   null and state::save discards a serialization error silently, which is why it
   is a separate Vec rather than an Option in the map.
2. Hard reset would have eaten NVRAM. rebuild_machine() builds from ROM and does
   NOT load NVRAM; that happens once in main before run(). Since main writes
   machine.save_nvram() back on exit, a naive hard reset would have blanked
   battery RAM in memory and then overwritten the players nvram file. Now carries
   NVRAM and DIP across, reusing the movie path reset/NVRAM/DIP ordering, which
   has to stay identical to Harness::from_movie.
3. Capture would have bound Shift. emulator.rs:520-539 took the first KeyDown,
   and shift presses first and raises its own. Now waits for a non-modifier and
   swallows the modifier press so it does not reach the game either.

CHECKS I MADE FAIL ON PURPOSE BEFORE KEEPING

- survives_text_entry: forced true, watched Num7 fail; forced false, watched F1
  fail. Both halves, so a constant cannot pass it.
- Pre-chord state.toml migration: changed StoredChord::Bare off i32 and watched
  the parse fail with "data did not match any variant". The fixture is a literal
  old-format string, not something built by our own serializer, which would have
  passed with the compatibility arm deleted.
- global_step consumption: reverted to clearing it only on the path that uses it,
  and watched a_step_request_cannot_outlive_the_frame_it_asked_for fail.

WHAT I DID NOT DO

- No service switch on F2. This only frees the key; binding it is a machines
  control-table change.
- No in-session gfx viewer on F4. Reserved only.
- No rewind on Shift+F4. Reserved only; see the note on rewind-jgqx.3.
- No frameskip, fast forward, cheats, save-state slots or AVI. The keys stay
  unbound rather than faked, pinned by
  the_keys_reserved_for_missing_features_stay_unbound.
- No Ctrl or Alt chords, so the console toggle (Ctrl+`) is still hardcoded and
  unrebindable.
- Did not write the state.toml migration test framework that
  contained-fidelity-np9x.6 owns. The chord migration test is inline in
  host_keys.rs; frontend/tests/ is still empty.

VERIFICATION

nix develop -c cargo clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets --locked
-- -D warnings: clean. Full workspace test: 125 groups, 0 failures, exit 0.
Frontend suite went from 62 to 85 tests.

ROM-gated suites NOT run, deliberately: nothing outside frontend/ was touched, no
board, core device or CPU, and nothing on the render path. debug_ui::execute_frame
changed but the harness has its own frame stepping and does not depend on the
frontend crate.

STILL OPEN: the layout is judged by hand and I cannot press keys. Needs a human
to confirm, in a running session: typing 7 and 0 into the debug panel watch
field does not step; Shift+F8 still does while that field is focused; Escape
leaves the field on the first press and quits on the second; Shift+F3 on a
machine with NVRAM (Williams, or any with a CMOS fixture) power-cycles without
losing the saved contents; and Shift+F5 held walks forward a frame at a time.

title: Marble Madness (Atari System 1)
description:
Add Marble Madness (1984), the project's first 16-bit multi-CPU arcade machine, on the Atari System 1 board (MC68010 main @ 7.15909 MHz + M6502 sound @ 1.789772 MHz).

Builds on the new M68000 core (first exercised by machines/src/foodf.rs, the closest end-to-end template). System 1 is the gateway to four more titles (Peter Packrat, Indiana Jones, Road Runner, RoadBlasters) that share this board.

User-chosen scope for this first cut:
- Audio: boot-first - POKEY only (reuse core/src/device/pokey.rs); YM2151 STUBBED (silent, but registers/IRQ wired so the sound CPU runs). Full FM synthesis is a tracked follow-up.
- Video: correct-but-staged - build the full alpha + playfield + motion-object compositor and palette first, then iterate the trickier PROM 4/5/6-bpp banking and SLIP scanline IRQs against MAME.

New components: Slapstic 137412-103 device, EEPROM 2804 (via Nvram), YM2151 stub, System 1 video (banked tilemaps + atarimo linked-list MO engine), machines/src/marble.rs.

Hardware verified against MAME atari/atarisy1.cpp, atarisy1_v.cpp, slapstic.cpp, atarimo.*.

Full plan: ~/.claude/plans/plan-for-marble-madness-goofy-rainbow.md
close_reason: done

title: P0: 68010 fidelity check (exception frame / VBR)
description:
Confirm the existing M68000 core with M68kVariant::M68010 is sufficient for Marble Madness before building on it. Risks: 68010 pushes an extra format/vector word on exception frames and has a VBR; MOVE from SR is privileged. Marble runs supervisor-mode with vectors at 0, so it almost certainly runs as-is.

Verify by reading core/src/cpu/m68000/exception.rs frame-build and confirming RTE/exception entry use a matching frame format. If a 68010 frame is needed, add it behind the existing variant gate.

Deliverable: a note plus any small gated frame fix - no behavior change expected. Cheap, do first.
close_reason: 68010 fidelity confirmed and gated. Implemented behind M68kVariant::M68010: the format $0 exception frame (vector-offset word + RTE consumption) and privileged MOVE from SR. Verified the M68000 path is byte-for-byte unchanged (full cpu-validation incl. SingleStepTests passes; new 68010 tests added). Documented the deferred 68010 deltas (VBR, MOVEC/MOVES/RTD, MOVE from CCR, format $8 fault frame) in the README for Phase 1 to watch. 3 commits on branch marble-68010-fidelity.

title: Follow-up: real YM2151 FM synthesis core
description: Replace the YM2151 stub (core/src/device/ym2151.rs) with a real FM synthesis core, restoring Marble Madness music/SFX. The single largest follow-up; the stub keeps the sound CPU alive so the rest of the machine is testable meanwhile. Drops in behind the same register/IRQ API established in P4.
close_reason: Real YM2151 (OPM) FM synthesis done. Replaced the timer/IRQ stub with a faithful integer port of the OPM synthesis path from MAME's ymfm reference core (no SSG-EG/depress/reverb/rhythm): die-extracted log-sine/exponent/EG-increment/detune/phase-step tables generated verbatim from ymfm; per-operator phase generator (key-code->phase-step, detune-1/2, MUL, LFO PM), envelope generator (KS-scaled AR/D1R/D2R/RR, D1L sustain, EG-counter divider + attack/decay curves), the 8 channel algorithms with op-1 self-feedback, LFO (saw/square/triangle/noise AM+PM) and the ch-7 noise operator, 8-channel per-sample mix at the native FM rate (clock/64) resampled on drain. Wired into the sound board: POKEY (unipolar) + YM (bipolar) summed, one-pole DC blocker (~35Hz) before i16 output, tunable FM mix gain. Verified vs MAME: identical register stream, attract FM-silent in both (game primes frequencies but keys no notes 40s+), music keys notes once a game starts. Address/data/status ports + A/B timers preserved. Synthesis + timer unit tests; cargo fmt + clippy --all-features --all-targets clean. User confirmed in-game music sounds correct. 3 commits on marble-68010-fidelity.

title: P1: Machine skeleton + main CPU boots
description:
Create machines/src/marble.rs; add mod marble; to machines/src/lib.rs.

- Region enum + build_map() (AddressSpace32): Program ROM (000000-07FFFF), Slapstic ROM window (080000-087FFF), Work RAM (400000), Playfield/MO/Alpha RAM (A00000-A03FFF), Palette RAM (B00000).
- ROM manifest (RomRegion/RomEntry) from the MAME 'marble' set: even/odd interleaved program ROMs, banked ROM, alpha/PF/MO GFX ROMs, two GFX-select PROMs. Pull exact filenames/sizes/CRCs from ROM_START(marble) in atarisy1.cpp.
- M68000::new() with variant=M68010; tick() cycle loop and reset() via bus_split! (mirror foodf). Wire watchdog (8-VBLANK) and 8A0000 VBLANK-ack.
- Bus read/write dispatch for ROM/RAM/EEPROM/control regs; stub video RAM as plain memory.
- Register via inventory::submit! { MachineEntry::new("marble", &["marble"], create_machine) }; add DisasmRegion entries (M68000 main, M6502 sound).

Verify: unit tests for map decode + reset-from-vectors (mirror foodf tests); a boot-check example runs N frames without panicking and the CPU leaves the reset vector.
close_reason: Machine skeleton boots. machines/src/marble.rs: AddressSpace32 map (program ROM, slapstic window as plain ROM, work/cart/playfield/MO/alpha/palette RAM); ROM manifest from the MAME 'marble' set (motherboard BIOS holding the reset vectors at 0x000000 + 4 even/odd cartridge banks + slapstic chips, de-interleaved); M68000 core in M68010 mode with bus_split tick/reset; VBLANK IRQ4 + 8-VBLANK watchdog; control/IO dispatch (scroll/priority/bankselect latches, F60000 switch port with live VBLANK bit, stubbed EEPROM/trackball/ADC/sound); registered as 'marble'; disasm regions for 68010 main + M6502 sound. 13 unit tests incl. map decode, reset-from-BIOS-vectors, and a synthetic 68010 program that boots + services VBLANK IRQ (RTE through the Phase-0 frame). Plus a headless marble_boot_check example. Full workspace builds; all 411 phosphor-machines tests pass. 2 commits on branch marble-68010-fidelity. NOTE: GFX/PROM ROM manifest + decode deferred to Phase 3 (3a/3b/3c) where they are consumed and CRC-verified; Slapstic/EEPROM to Phase 2; sound CPU to Phase 4; trackball/coins to Phase 5 - all stubbed with TODO markers.

title: P2: Slapstic 137412-103 + EEPROM 2804
description:
Port core/src/device/slapstic.rs from MAME atari/slapstic.cpp, configured for bank 103. Self-contained address-sequence state machine; exposes tweak(addr)->bank so the Bus drives map.remap_range on the 080000-087FFF window.

EEPROM 2804: 512-byte array, low-byte R/W at F00000, gated by the 8C0000 enable latch; expose via the Nvram trait (like foodf's nvram).

Verify: unit test that the documented Slapstic unlock sequence selects each bank; EEPROM round-trip test. Game should get past its protection/config checks (watch the 01006E game-id byte the boot code writes).
close_reason: Slapstic + EEPROM done. core/src/device/slapstic.rs: chip-103 address-sequence state machine ported from MAME atari/slapstic.cpp (103-110 state set: idle/active/alt/bitwise), expressed in in-window word-offset space; tweak(offset)->bank, Saveable, 10 unit tests (arming, direct switch per bank, alt-sequence bank encoding, sequence-break abort, bitwise phase swap, reset, save/load mid-sequence). marble.rs: 080000-087FFF decoded in the bus and banked per-access via the slapstic (window held outside the map, x4 mirror -> low 13 bits); EEPROM 2804 (512 bytes) at F00000-F003FF with reads returning the low byte and writes gated by the 8C0001 unlock latch + re-lock after one byte; exposed via Nvram. Slapstic state + EEPROM in save/load; reset re-arms slapstic and preserves the EEPROM. 3 new marble tests. Full core (799) + machines (414) suites pass; workspace builds. 2 commits on branch marble-68010-fidelity.

title: P3a: Video - palette + alpha layer
description:
Decode IRGB-4444 palette RAM (B00000+) to RGB. Render the 64x32 alpha tilemap (8x8, 2bpp, anlayout) - the text/HUD layer and easiest correctness signal. Full-frame compositor like foodf::render.

Verify: boot-check example dumps lit-pixel / distinct-color counts (model on machines/examples/galaxian_boot_check.rs); compare attract-mode HUD to MAME.
close_reason: Palette + alpha layer done. irgb4444_to_rgb ports MAME standard_irgb_decoder<4,4,4,4,12,8,4,0> (4-bit intensity scales each 4-bit RGB component, c=(expand4(i)*expand4(comp))>>8). Alpha font ROM (136032.104.f5) added to the manifest and decoded as 512 8x8 2bpp tiles via the anlayout layout. Full-frame compositor renders the 64x32 alpha tilemap 1:1 from the screen origin: per pixel code=data&0x3FF, color=(data>>10)&7, opaque=data&0x2000; composites palette[color*4+pen]; pen 0 transparent unless the cell forces layer 0 (black background until Phase 3b playfield). 4 new tests (IRGB conversion vs MAME values, opaque-cell compositing, transparent-pen-0 black). marble_boot_check example extended with lit/distinct-colour stats + ASCII thumbnail per the verify step. All 417 phosphor-machines tests pass; clippy/fmt clean. 2 commits on branch marble-68010-fidelity. NOTE: visual attract-mode comparison vs MAME not done here - the marble ROM set is not present on this machine; the boot-check is ready to run once ROMs are available.

title: P3b: Video - playfield tilemap + PROM GFX decode
description:
64x64 playfield tilemap with X/Y scroll (800000/820000). Implement the PROM-driven GFX decode (decode_gfx in atarisy1_v.cpp: PROM1/PROM2 -> bank, bpp 4/5/6, color, offset) and the runtime tile-bank select from 860000. Start with a single bank / fixed bpp, then generalize.

Least-standard part of the video; bring up incrementally against MAME, expect iteration.

Verify: playfield matches MAME attract-mode frames.
close_reason: Playfield + PROM GFX decode done. tiles (0x100000) + graphics PROMs (0x400) added to the manifest; tiles region handled as ROMREGION_INVERT|ROMREGION_ERASEFF by inverting the whole zero-filled buffer. build_playfield_gfx/get_pf_bank port MAME decode_gfx+get_bank: each of 256 remap entries -> tile bank (1-7), bpp (4/5/6), color, offset; banks decoded on demand at their bpp (planes 0x10000 apart, reversed to LSB-first). render: 64x64 playfield as opaque background with X/Y scroll (800000/820000), lookup ((data>>8)&0x7f | tile_bank<<7), code=(offset<<8)|(data&0xff), palette[0x100 + palcolor*2^bpp + pen]; alpha overlays on top; tile bank from 860001 bit 2. 3 new tests (PROM lookup decode, bpp select + unmapped remap, playfield pixel composites under alpha). All 420 phosphor-machines tests pass; clippy/fmt clean. 1 commit on branch marble-68010-fidelity. CAVEATS (issue flagged iteration expected): visual attract-mode comparison vs MAME not done - marble ROM set not on this machine. The scroll sign/offset convention (src = screen + scroll) and bank2's missing-4th-plane edge case are the most likely things to need adjustment once ROMs are available.

title: P3c: Video - motion objects (atarimo) + priority/translucency
description:
Port the atarimo linked-list motion-object walker (8 banks x 64 entries x 4 words; X/Y flip, size, link-to-next) and the priority/translucency merge from screen_update (high-pri MO vs playfield_priority_pens, 0x300 translucency bank). From atarimo.cpp.

Verify: marbles/sprites render and composite correctly vs MAME.
close_reason: Motion objects + priority/translucency done. PROM decode builds a sprite remap lookup (proms +0x100/+0x300, MO colour mask) sharing the playfield tile banks; render_motion_objects walks the active bank's linked list (split 4-word entries, timer entries skipped) and rasterises each sprite (h-flip, transparent pen 0, yscroll 256, 512x512 wrap) into a palette-index buffer merged over the playfield: high-priority pens blend through the translucent bank (0x300+pf<<4+mo), low-priority pens draw unless the playfield pixel is a colour-0 priority pen (0x840000 mask). Also fixed the tile ROM to true ROMREGION_ERASEFF (load_erased(0xFF)+invert) so bank 2's absent plane 3 reads 0 — without it sprites rendered all black (pen bit 3 forced). render() refactored to index-based compositing first. Verified vs MAME (palette/PF/sprite pens); attract sprites now render in colour. 3 commits on marble-68010-fidelity. Follow-up: SLIP/IRQ3 (iv0.7).

title: P3d: Video - SLIP / IRQ3 scanline motion-object interrupts
description:
Scanline-position motion-object interrupts (the int3_callback timer) and the 2E0000 sprite-interrupt-state read (bit 7). Add once static rendering is correct.

SLIP timing affects both visuals and game logic; verify cadence against MAME traces.
close_reason: SLIP / IRQ3 scanline motion-object interrupts done. A motion-object timer entry (0xFFFF in word[1]) asserts IRQ3 for the one scanline at the top of its band (ypos = 256 - (word0>>5) - vsize*8 - 1, per MAME update_timers), recomputed each scanline boundary from the active sprite bank; drives the IRQ3 line (priority below IRQ4/IRQ6) and the 0x2E0000 status read bit 7 (was stubbed 0). State-saved; unit test covers the firing scanline + status/level wiring. Verified vs MAME: SLIP is negligible in attract (MAME fires it 2x at boot frame 6 then never; VBLANK ~1/frame). Our attract writes no timer entries so IRQ3 stays idle there — mechanism matches MAME's algorithm for gameplay and is unit-tested. 1 commit on marble-68010-fidelity. Note: the 2 MAME boot-frame-6 firings aren't replicated (boot-state timing diverges via the EEPROM/sound path); not a SLIP bug.

title: P4: Sound CPU (M6502) + inter-CPU comms, YM2151 stubbed
description:
Add M6502 sound CPU with its own AddressSpace16 map and a Bresenham ClockDivider (1.789772 vs 7.15909 MHz ~= 1/4) like machines/src/tkg04.rs.

Latches: main FE0000 write -> sound NMI (command); sound 1810 write -> main IRQ6 (response); FC0000/1810 reads; status bits at 1820/F60000 (buffer-full flags); 860000 bit drives sound-CPU reset.

POKEY at 1870-187F (reuse Pokey), mixed to stereo in run_frame. YM2151 stub (core/src/device/ym2151.rs) at 1800-1801: accept register writes, return not-busy status, raise the IRQ line on its timers so the 6502 IRQ handler executes - but emit silence from drain_audio. Structured so the real FM core drops in behind the same API.

Verify: command/response handshake in a unit test (write command -> NMI taken -> response latched -> main IRQ6). POKEY audio path produces output without underruns.
close_reason: Sound CPU done — and it unblocks boot. core/src/device/ym2151.rs: timer/IRQ stub (timer A/B overflow -> status flag -> IRQ; register writes stored; silent audio; 6 tests). machines/src/marble_sound.rs: MarbleSound = M6502 @ 1.789772 MHz with its own Bus<u16> (RAM/ROM/YM2151/POKEY/output-latch), inter-CPU latches (main FE0000->sound NMI command; sound 1810->main IRQ6 response; FC0000/1810 reads; F60000/1820 buffer flags; 860001 bit7 = sound reset, held at power-on until released), driven at 1/4 main via ClockDivider; POKEY mixed in run_frame, YM silent; IRQ6 in the main interrupt priority; save/load; 4 tests incl. the full command->NMI->response->IRQ6 handshake. VERIFIED against the real ROM set (~/ws/mame-runtime/roms/marble.zip): marble now boots through self-test — the EEPROM self-initialises (195 byte writes), the sound CPU runs once released, and the frame renders attract content (alpha HUD text + playfield visibly working, 1379 lit px / 20 colours). All 805 core+machines tests pass; clippy/fmt clean; 2 commits on branch marble-68010-fidelity. Follow-up iv0.10 (real YM2151 FM) remains; exact attract-mode pixel match vs MAME (scroll sign, bank-2 plane, MO) is Phase 3c/polish.

title: P5: Trackball input, save-state, polish
description:
Trackballs: accumulate host InputEvent::Relative deltas (foodf already uses Relative for analog) into the four F20000-F20007 read values; coins/start/service/self-test at F60000/1820. InputConfigurable control table; DIP/EEPROM-config defaults.

Saveable: snapshot both CPUs, POKEY, YM2151 stub, all video/work RAM, palette, EEPROM, Slapstic state, latches, scroll/bank registers (mirror foodf save_state/load_state).

README/roadmap checkbox; cargo fmt + cargo clippy --all-features --all-targets clean.
close_reason: Trackball input, coins, save-state, polish done. Trackballs: 0xF20000-0xF20007 returns the 45-degree rotated counter pairs (X port = x+y, Y port = x-y, latched on the even read like MAME); host mouse Relative deltas and a keyboard/D-pad digital fallback both feed per-axis accumulators drained a capped step/frame (cap avoids >127 aliasing of the 8-bit counter; keyboard step gentle 6/frame; X reversed per cabinet PORT_REVERSE). Four AnalogAxis + four DigitalDirection controls (P1 mouse+keys, P2 rebindable). Coins: sound-board 0x1820 active-low bits 0-2 via MarbleSound::set_coin, COIN control routes to it; verified headlessly the coin credits (game shows PUSH 1 PLAYER START) and the user confirms play/start work. Save-state was already comprehensive (both CPUs, POKEY, YM stub, all video/work RAM, palette, EEPROM, slapstic, latches, scroll/bank, IRQ latches); extended with trackball counters + coin state. Marble has no DIPs (config in the 2804 EEPROM, self-initialised). README machines list updated. cargo fmt --all and cargo clippy --all-features --all-targets both clean; 635 machines tests pass. ~6 commits on marble-68010-fidelity.

title: Add Mario Bros. (Nintendo, Z80 + I8039 sound)
description: Nintendo Mario Bros. (1983) arcade machine. Hardware: Z80 main CPU + I8039 (MCS-48) sound CPU + 2x AY-3-8910 + tile/sprite video. Z80 and AY-8910 are implemented; the I8039 is in the same MCS-48 family as the existing I8035 core (may need MCS-48 variant work). See README Future > Games.
close_reason: Implemented: Mario Bros. machine present at machines/src/mario_bros.rs (Z80 + I8039 sound), registered in machines/src/lib.rs and available in the disasm machine list.

title: Epic: Mid-frame raster fidelity
description:
Correctness: several machines render the whole frame once from final video state, losing mid-frame palette/scroll/bank/flip changes. Decide which machines actually need per-scanline rendering by MEASUREMENT (via the headless trace tool), migrate the ones that do, and cheaply fix the rest. Subsumes the ifs0 debugger-stale-image bug for every machine it touches. Design: ~/mid-frame-raster-fidelity.md.

Verified against code: per-scanline vs render-once split is real and broad; galaga run_frame is the render-once pattern; atari_system1 already records per-scanline mo_bank_changes while compositing once (proof at least one machine needs this today); mcr2/atari_system1 use indexed+priority buffers. Main correctness risk (doc-flagged): must NOT re-sample vblank-latched state (galaga starfield) per scanline.

Depends on: Epic headless-debugging (Phase 0 audit uses the trace tool) and Epic graphics-consolidation (Tier A migrations use the enriched 2a / indexed 2b scanline helpers). Sequence LAST of the three.

Phases: (0) trace-based Tier A/B audit; (1) Tier B frame-boundary fix [closes ifs0, zero output change]; (2) Tier A non-priority per-scanline; (3) Tier A priority-compositing [after graphics 2b].
close_reason:
Epic complete. Goal was: decide by MEASUREMENT which machines need per-scanline rendering, migrate those that do, cheaply fix the rest.

Decided (Phase 0): all 37 registered machines classified; evidence in docs/designs/mid-frame-raster-audit.md. Of 10 render-once boards, 9 measured Tier B; the one Tier A case (atari_system1 via Road Runner's mid-frame MO-bank switch) already implements per-scanline band rendering and pjl verified it renders correctly. Per-scanline boards (williams/namco_pac/tkg04/mario_bros/congo_bongo/galaxian_video + gridlee/ccastles/missile/irobot) were already mid-frame-correct; DVG/AVG vector games (incl. esb, which runs on Star Wars hardware) are not raster.

Migrated (Phases 2/3): nothing needed — both closed as not-needed, with reasons. The audit's whole point was to avoid needless per-scanline cost, and it did.

Fixed cheaply (Phase 1): the six machines that cached a render in run_frame now render at a frame-boundary hook shared with debug_tick. Byte-identical output (frameshot 12/12), guarded by a ROM-gated acceptance test proven to fail when the bug is reintroduced. Closed phosphor-emulator-ifs0 (open since 2026-07-03), verified by pjl in the real frontend debugger.

Also built the missing instrument the audit depended on: CPU-agnostic, region-tagged bus write-event tracing for every AddressSpace16/32 board (previously only the 3 hand-wired Namco boards emitted events), plus io_write capture.

Follow-ups filed: nx2p (framebuffer ownership/format/lifecycle consolidation), j55q (unify Namco boards onto AddressSpace16), pvmf (Marble Madness MOB rendering bug). Note graphics-consolidation.md Feature 2b lost its only consumer from this epic and should now be justified on its own merits.

comments.author: pjl
comments.text: Correction to the close reason: it stated graphics-consolidation.md Feature 2b 'lost its only consumer and should now be justified on its own merits'. That is wrong. 2b is already implemented (render_tilemap_scanline_indexed / render_scrolled_tilemap_scanline_indexed in core/src/gfx/tilemap.rs; draw_sprite_row_indexed in core/src/gfx/sprite.rs) and is in production use by gottlieb/qbert. mcr2 and atari_system1 were deliberately not migrated to it for structural reasons (mcr2: 2x tile upscale vs the helper's 1:1 loop, plus dirty-tile incremental redraw vs unconditional per-scanline; atari_system1: u16 1024-entry index space vs the helper's &mut [u8], plus a priority_pens/translucency merge rather than a per-pixel prio_buf). So Phase 3 was never 2b's motivation and no 2b action is needed. graphics-consolidation.md's table listing mcr2 as a 2b target is stale.

title: raster: Phase 0 — trace-based Tier A/B classification audit
description: Phase 0, do first — first concrete consumer of the headless trace tool. For each render-once machine (digdug, galaga, xevious, btime, mrdo, foodf, gottlieb, mcr2/satans_hollow, atari_system1): enumerate its video registers (palette latch, scroll, bank latches, flip), set write-watchpoints / DebugTrace filtered to writes via 'disasm trace', run representative gameplay, and flag any write landing inside active display (cycle % cycles_per_frame < VISIBLE_LINES*cycles_per_scanline). Any active-display write => Tier A candidate (confirm visually vs a MAME per-scanline reference); none => Tier B. Record the result + evidence per machine so the decision is auditable. Initial hypotheses (must be measured): atari_system1=A confirmed; xevious/mcr2 likely A; galaga/digdug/btime/mrdo/foodf/gottlieb likely B.
close_reason: Phase 0 audit complete. Method + per-machine evidence in docs/designs/mid-frame-raster-audit.md. Result: of 9 render-once boards, only atari_system1 (Road Runner MO-bank) is Tier A and already implements per-band rendering; digdug/galaga/xevious/mrdo/burgertime/foodf/qbert/shollow/marble are all Tier B (measured: video registers written only in vblank, at init, sporadically at transitions, or as IRQ-acks with constant video bits). Also classified the full roster (per-scanline boards already correct; DVG/AVG vector N/A). Built the missing instrument: CPU-agnostic bus write-event tracing for all AddressSpace16/32 boards. Follow-ups: pvmf (marble MOB bug), j55q (Namco AddressSpace consolidation).

title: raster: Phase 1 — Tier B frame-boundary render fix (closes ifs0)
description: Phase 1 — low risk, high value, closes phosphor-emulator-ifs0. For each measured Tier B machine, move the single render out of run_frame() into a frame-boundary hook in tick() (render on the last visible-line boundary, or share a 'frame just completed' signal between run_frame and debug_tick); delete the redundant run_frame render call. Output must be byte-identical (same state, same frame boundary) — verify with disasm frameshot --compare vs pre-change. Add the ifs0 acceptance check: under debug_tick the framebuffer now changes across frames (was frozen). Zero runtime cost beyond today.
close_reason: Phase 1 complete (commit e9380a3).
