title: Movie recording does not start from the state replay reconstructs
description:
Arming a movie recording does not start from the state replay will reconstruct,
so a recorded session replays differently from the one that was played.

SYMPTOM: a Donkey Kong movie recorded through a completed first level replays
with the barrels behaving differently from about frame 1800.

NOT NON-DETERMINISM, AND NOT AN RNG SEED. Five consecutive `disasm movie check`
runs of the same movie produce one hash, so replay is bit-reproducible and
nothing in the path draws on entropy. The three preconditions for faithful
replay are deterministic execution, identical input, and the same INITIAL STATE.
The first two hold; the third does not.

ROOT CAUSE. The two paths start from different machines:

  recording  the machine has been running attract mode since launch, then
             MovieCapture::arm calls machine.reset()
  replay     Harness::from_movie builds a brand-new machine from ROM, then
             calls reset()

`reset()` is a reset button, not a power cycle: state survives it. How much
survives is demonstrated by the sibling bug — dkong can reach an out-of-bounds
sprite fetch after reset-following-play that a fresh boot does not reach in the
same number of frames.

Divergence appearing at ~1800 rather than immediately is the expected shape: the
game re-initialises most things when a round starts, so a surviving value takes
a while to reach something as visible as barrel behaviour.

FIX DIRECTION. Arming should reconstruct the machine the way replay will, rather
than resetting the live one — rebuild from the ROM set, exactly as
Harness::from_movie does. Then the recording's starting state is identical to the
replay's by construction instead of by hoping reset() is thorough. The frontend
already has the ROM path and the registry entry.

The rebuild cannot happen inside the F2 handler, because the machine is borrowed
out of the session for the whole loop iteration; defer it to the top of the next
iteration, the same shape `needs_resync` already uses.

WHY THE EXISTING TESTS MISS IT: harness/tests/movie_test.rs records THROUGH the
harness, where the recorder and the machine start together by construction. Only
the frontend's arm-after-running path can desynchronise them, and no test drives
that path. The regression test should be that a machine reset after running
produces the same state as a freshly constructed one — which is the invariant
actually being relied on.
close_reason: Fixed. MovieCapture::arm_fresh now requires a machine built from ROM, and the frontend defers F2 to the top of the next loop iteration where it can rebuild and replace the session's machine wholesale — the machine is borrowed for the whole loop body, so it could not be done in the handler. The recording's starting state is now identical to what Harness::from_movie constructs by construction, in the same order (reset, NVRAM, DIP), rather than by hoping reset() is thorough. Measured basis, now a committed guard (reset_is_not_a_power_cycle_so_arming_must_rebuild): 38 of 39 machines differ between reset-following-play and a fresh build, burgertime by 1449 state bytes and 28134 rendered pixels. The guard fails loudly if reset() ever becomes a true power cycle, pointing at the arm path that could then be simplified.

title: Movie rom_digest fingerprints the name list, not the ROM contents
description:
`harness::movie::rom_digest` is documented as fingerprinting the dump a movie
was recorded against — the comment at the check site says "a movie replayed
against a different dump boots fine and then diverges silently, so this check is
the difference between a clear error and a golden hash that moved for no visible
reason." It does not do that.

    pub fn rom_digest(set: &RomSet, rom_names: &[&str]) -> [u8; 32] {
        for name in rom_names {
            ... match set.get(name) { Some(bytes) => hash(bytes), None => hash(0) }
        }
    }

`rom_names` are ZIP-SET names ("mario", "mariobros"); `RomSet::get` looks up a
MEMBER FILE ("tma1-c-7f.7f"). Every lookup therefore misses, every branch takes
the `None` arm, and the digest reduces to a hash of the name list.

DEMONSTRATED. Replaying the same movie against three genuinely different Mario
Bros dumps yields one identical digest:

    disasm replay --movie mariobros-*.phmi roms/mario.zip   -> bac4c772...
    disasm replay --movie mariobros-*.phmi roms/marioe.zip  -> bac4c772...
    disasm replay --movie mariobros-*.phmi roms/mariof.zip  -> bac4c772...

TWO CONSEQUENCES, in opposite directions:

  1. FALSE NEGATIVE, the one that matters. Replaying against the wrong dump is
     exactly what the check exists to prevent, and it cannot see it. A movie
     recorded on marioe replays against mario without complaint, then diverges.
     For …-input-movie-no93.5 (golden gameplay pins) this is load-bearing: a
     pinned frame hash would move with no visible cause, which is the failure
     the comment describes and believes it has prevented.
  2. FALSE POSITIVE. Reordering or renaming an entry's `rom_names` invalidates
     every movie recorded before the change, with an error blaming the ROMs.
     This is why the galaga and mariobros movies in ~/.config/phosphor/movies
     currently refuse to replay while every other movie in the same directory
     works — nothing is wrong with those ROMs.

FIX: hash the loaded set's actual member files — names and contents, iterated in
sorted order for determinism — instead of looking up set names as members.

MIGRATION IS THE REAL WORK, not the hash. Fixing the function changes the digest
for every machine, so every existing movie mismatches at once. Options:
  - bump the movie format version and accept the old digest for old files
    (they keep their weak guarantee, new ones get a real one);
  - or add the true digest as a new header field and keep the old one for
    compatibility, checking whichever is present.
Do not fix the hash without one of these, or 39 recorded movies stop replaying.

Found while making the sanity test replay movies (…-discrete-sound-fidelity-
l5r3.3). The check-site error now reports both digests and says what the digest
actually covers, so the next person does not spend the time on it that this did.
close_reason:
rom_digest now hashes the loaded set's member files (name and body length-prefixed, sorted name order) instead of looking up archive names as member names. Signature dropped to rom_digest(&RomSet) so there is no name list left to pass in wrongly; 6 call sites updated.

Migration: MOVIE_VERSION 1 -> 2, version-1 files rejected outright. The layout is unchanged, but the header's digest field changed meaning and cannot be recomputed from the new inputs, so reinterpreting it was not an option. The 39 local movies are invalid and are being re-recorded (owner's call).

Verified: two_dumps_of_one_game_do_not_digest_alike digests every entry with 2+ archives on disk separately - 5 archives, all distinct, so the mario/marioe/mariof collision is gone. Five ROM-less unit tests pin the properties (one-byte difference, membership, rename, insertion order, byte regrouping). The stale bug-describing comment at the check site in harness.rs is replaced, and its error now explains that a mismatch means the bytes differ.

Fallout found and fixed while verifying: with the movies invalid, audio_sanity_test's every_known_defect_is_still_present fell back to attract-mode boots and reported 7 defects as fixed, telling the reader to delete good expectations.toml entries. Attract mode drives different voices than play, so a boot fixture now counts as unchecked rather than fixed; the test names the 9 machines currently outside the ratchet instead. That hazard predated this change - any missing movie would have triggered it.

harness (28 lib + 5 + 7 + 6 + 18 + 1), frontend 71, machines, disasm movie_cli 8, script all pass; fmt and clippy clean.

title: AVG flip overflows i32 and panics quantum in debug builds
description:
Running quantum in a dev build panics within seconds:

    thread 'main' panicked at core/src/device/avg.rs:747:13:
    attempt to add with overflow
    ... Avg::strobe3 -> Avg::dispatch -> Avg::execute -> QuantumBoard::trigger_avg

Avg::flipped mirrors the beam about the screen center with

    if flip_x { x += (xcenter - x) << 1; }
    if flip_y { y += (ycenter - y) << 1; }

Two problems compound.

1. It is the only checked arithmetic in the AVG beam datapath. Everything else
   treats xpos/ypos as an unclamped, deliberately wrapping 16.16 accumulator:
   deflect() uses wrapping_mul, all three draw_* handlers use wrapping_add and
   wrapping_sub, and add_point documents 'Coordinates are stored unclamped, the
   rasterizer handles clipping'. flipped() uses plain +=, - and <<, so it traps
   on state the rest of the module explicitly permits.

2. The expression needs twice the range of its own result. Mirroring is
   2*center - pos, but the intermediate (center - pos) << 1 is twice the
   magnitude of the answer, and << on i32 is never overflow-checked in Rust, so
   it silently drops the top bit in release as well as debug. Once
   |pos - center| > 2^30, roughly 16384 pixels off center in 16.16, the shift
   wraps and the final add lands out of range even when the true mirrored
   coordinate 2*center - pos is perfectly representable.

Worked example with quantum's ycenter = (900/2) << 16 = 29491200 and
ypos = +2.0e9: the true mirror 2c - y = -1941017600 fits in i32, but
(c - y) << 1 = -3941017600 wraps to +353949696 and y += that overflows.

MAME does the identical thing in avgdvg_device_base::apply_flipping
(src/devices/video/avgdvg.cpp:41), on int, where signed overflow wraps in
practice instead of trapping. So the structure is right and only the arithmetic
model differs: the fix is to wrap like the rest of the datapath, not to change
what is computed.

Why quantum and not the others: flipped() only does anything when a flip bit is
set, and only two boards drive one. quantum.rs led_w drives set_flip from
$958000 bits 6 and 7 during normal operation, and the backtrace confirms flip_y
was true. tempest.rs drives it from cocktail outlatch bits 2 and 3, normally 0
upright, so the branches never run and the identical latent defect on the x line
is never tripped. Star Wars bypasses flipped() entirely.

Release builds do not panic, they draw wrong: the << 1 wrap is unchecked there
too, so the mirrored coordinate is garbage rather than mirrored.
close_reason: flipped() mirrors with (center << 1).wrapping_sub(pos) on both axes, matching MAME's int arithmetic. Reproduced by a ROM-free unit test that panicked on the reported line before the fix. Workspace suite and all four ROM-gated suites green, golden frames unchanged.

comments.author: pjl
comments.text:
Fixed. flipped() now computes (center << 1).wrapping_sub(pos) on both axes, which is the same value MAME's int arithmetic produces and, whenever the mirrored coordinate is representable at all, the mathematically correct mirror. Nothing else changed.

Primary source first: MAME avgdvg_device_base::apply_flipping (src/devices/video/avgdvg.cpp:41) is the identical expression on int, so the structure was already right and only the overflow behaviour differed. This is a port artifact, not a hardware question.

Reproduction, no ROMs needed, in core/src/device/avg.rs tests as flip_survives_a_beam_far_off_screen: nine full-scale Quantum VCTRs (dvy = dvx = 0x7FF, already normalized so strobe0 leaves the timer at 0 and strobe3 runs the full 0x4000) with flip_y set. Each moves the beam about 2036 pixels, because quantum's scale register powers up at 0 and the DAC input is scale ^ 0xFF, so 0 is maximum deflection, not minimum. Nine of them clear 2^30 and the mirror overflows. Before the fix that test panics at avg.rs:747, 'attempt to add with overflow', the exact line and message from the reported backtrace. After it passes.

The test asserts the mirrored coordinate, not just the absence of a panic, and computes the expectation in i64 so it does not come from the i32 expression under test. It also asserts the excursion actually cleared 2^30 first, so it cannot pass vacuously if a future change stops driving the beam that far.

Also added flip_mirrors_the_beam_about_the_center for the ordinary in-range case on all four flip combinations, with literal expected pixel coordinates. There was no flip test at all before.

Verified: full workspace suite green, including all four ROM-gated harness suites against ~/ws/mame-runtime/roms. golden_frame_test passed unchanged, so no pinned machine's picture moved, quantum's included. clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -D warnings clean, cargo fmt clean.

What I did NOT do: this fixes the crash, not the reason the beam is out there. Measured with a throwaway harness probe reading vector_display_list per frame, quantum's beam never leaves the screen in 3000 frames of attract (worst 424 px from the 600x900 center, zero off-screen lines). It only runs away on the attract-to-play transition, and that is a separate defect now filed as its own issue. The x line at avg.rs:744 carried the identical latent defect and was never tripped, because tempest only sets flip in cocktail mode; it is fixed the same way.

title: NE555 astable runs ~3.4% flat: ideal RC vs the datasheet constant
description:
`ne555_astable` integrates the cap with ideal RC exponents, so it free-runs at

    f = 1 / (ln2 · (R1 + 2·R2) · C)  =  1.4427 / ((R1 + 2·R2)·C)

The datasheet (and MAME's FREQ_OF_555, and this repo's own doc comment on
`DiscreteCircuitBuilder::ne555_astable`) quote

    f = 1.49 / ((R1 + 2·R2)·C)

That is a consistent 3.4% flat — roughly 60 cents, which is audible on a pitched
voice. Found while extracting derive::* (…-discrete-sound-fidelity-l5r3.4): the
new `ne555_free_runs_at_the_ideal_rc_frequency` test measured 432 Hz against the
datasheet's 447 Hz for Donkey Kong's walk/jump values (R1 47k, R2 27k, C 33nF).

The existing `ne555_astable_oscillates_near_freq_of_555` test compares against
1.49 with a 10% tolerance, so it has always passed while being 3.4% off. The new
test pins the ideal value tightly instead, so whichever way this is resolved the
change will be visible.

WHO IS AFFECTED: every 555 astable voice — Donkey Kong walk and jump are the
current ones.

WHY THE GAP EXISTS (to be confirmed): 1.44 is the ideal result of charging
1/3→2/3 Vcc through R1+R2 and discharging 2/3→1/3 through R2, each leg taking
ln2 time constants. The real chip runs a few percent fast, plausibly from
comparator offset and the discharge transistor's saturation voltage — the cap
does not actually discharge to a hard 1/3 Vcc. 1.49 appears to be empirical.

RESOLUTION IS NOT OBVIOUS, which is why this is filed rather than fixed:
- If 1.49 is empirical silicon behaviour, the model should reproduce the cause
  (a discharge floor / comparator offset), not multiply the output by 1.033.
- If 1.49 is a rounded convention, the ideal 1.44 is correct and the doc comment
  and the older test should change instead.
- Settle it against the datasheet, per the standing rule that datasheets win
  over reference emulators for timing.

This is exactly the class of question `…-discrete-sound-fidelity-l5r3.7` (fit)
is meant to answer with evidence — a DK walk capture against a clean reference
would show whether our pitch is 3.4% flat in practice.

title: Scramble sound crystal: 14.318 MHz -> 14.318181 MHz
notes:
Behaviour change, audio only, split out of phosphor-emulator-clock-tree-jv78.7 so a bisect can find it.

scramble.rs SOUND_CLOCK_HZ is 14_318_000 / 8 = 1_789_750. The Konami sound board carries the 14.318181 MHz colourburst crystal, which clock_tree() already declares, and /8 of that is 1789772.625. The board is 22.6 Hz (12.6 ppm) slow. This is the same defect class as the Gottlieb sound ratio (jv78.5): a rate rounded by hand rather than derived from a declared crystal.

The fix is a deletion, as it was for Gottlieb. ScrambleBoard::new() currently calls

    clocks.set_domain_hz(sound_dom, SOUND_CLOCK_HZ as u32);

to hold the old rate. Remove that line and the SOUND_CLOCK_HZ constant, and the tree's crystal-derived ratio stands. the_sound_domain_still_runs_the_rounded_crystal pins the current rate and will fail, which is the point of it.

Check for a second consumer before landing, the way jv78.5 had to: on Gottlieb the resampler was being told a different rate than the divider ticked at, and correcting only one would have relocated the inconsistency rather than removing it. Confirm what else reads SOUND_CLOCK_HZ (KonamiSound's own clocking, any AudioResampler input rate) and move all of it onto the domain together.

Affects scramble, scobra and frogger, which share the board. No save-layout change, so no SAVE_VERSION bump. Golden frames should be unaffected (audio only), but verify: unlike Gottlieb, this board's sound section is reached through an I8255 the main CPU also reads, so check whether sound timing can reach the main CPU before assuming video is safe.
close_reason:
Landed in d4984d1. Scramble, Scobra and Frogger now take the sound rate from the declared 14.318181 MHz crystal: 1789772.625 Hz instead of 1789750, 22.6 Hz and 12.6 ppm faster.

The warning on this issue paid off. It was filed as a one-line deletion, and it was not: the rate was written down three times, not once. SOUND_CLOCK_HZ set the Bresenham ratio the board steps at, while konami_sound.rs carried its own KONAMI_SOUND_CLOCK/KONAMI_CPU_CLOCK pair feeding the AY-8910s' chip clock and the resampler's input rate. Deleting only the board constant would have left the PSGs (where the chip clock is tone pitch) and the resampler on the old rounded rate, relocating the Gottlieb inconsistency rather than removing it. KonamiSound::new now takes the rate from its caller and both device constants are gone, so all three uses come off one domain.

Added Ay8910::chip_clock_hz and KonamiSound::cpu_clock_hz/psg_clock_hz, read back out of the audio path rather than from stored copies, so the_psgs_and_the_resampler_share_the_sound_domains_rate checks board and devices agree on both wirings instead of leaving it to inspection. That test is the guard against this being re-split later.

The video question this issue raised was checked, not assumed. The sound Z80's bus never decodes the I8255 that carries commands: the PPI is touched only by ppi_write/ppi_read/set_ppi_portc_input, all called from the main board. Nothing the sound CPU does is readable by the main CPU, so sound timing cannot reach video. All three golden frames unchanged, confirming it.

The Konami timer needed nothing: it counts CPU cycles times eight, a divider ratio rather than a frequency, so it rides the correction automatically.

No save-layout change, so no SAVE_VERSION bump, as predicted.

title: Consolidate framebuffer ownership/format/lifecycle into a shared component
description:
Framebuffer definition and handling is inconsistent across machines; consolidate into shared infrastructure. Evidence gathered while doing mid-frame-raster Phase 1 (touched all of these):

  machine                 buffer name      owner   format    refresh trigger
  galaga/xevious/digdug   native_buffer    system  indexed8  frame boundary
  qbert (gottlieb)        pixel_buffer     board   indexed8  frame boundary
  shollow (mcr2)          pixel_buffer     board   indexed8  frame boundary
  burgertime (btime)      framebuffer      board   RGB24     frame boundary
  mrdo, foodf, marble     (none)           -       -         on-demand in render_frame
  williams/namco_pac/...  scanline_buffer  board   RGB24     per-scanline in tick

Four names, two formats, two owners (system vs board), three refresh triggers. The indexed -> palette -> RGB24 conversion loop in render_frame is hand-rolled ~5 times (galaga.rs:890, xevious.rs:941, digdug.rs:1011, gottlieb.rs:832, mcr2.rs:465).

Index width is NOT uniform, so the format enum needs at least Indexed8 / Indexed16 / Rgb24:
  - galaga 96 entries, gottlieb 16/32, mcr2 64  -> fit u8
  - atari_system1 uses a 1024-entry (10-bit) palette index space (alpha 0x000 /
    motion 0x100 / playfield 0x200 / translucent 0x300, masked & 0x3FF;
    atari_system1.rs:665-668, 675, 705) -> needs u16. An Indexed8-only design
    would silently truncate it.
Note atari_system1 already composites into an index buffer and converts to RGB only at the end - it just builds that buffer per render call instead of persisting it, so it is a natural adopter of the component (with the wider index).

Proposed shared component (core/src/gfx): a Framebuffer owning native dims + storage with a declared format (Indexed8{palette} | Indexed16{palette} | Rgb24), a single present(&self, out) doing the conversion (retires the duplicated loops), and a uniform frame-boundary/scanline refresh hook. Phase 1 had to hand-write the same frame-boundary render hook 6 times in 2 different shapes (3 system-level, 3 board-level) - that duplication is itself the argument for the component. Prefer board-level ownership to match the Board Wrapper Pattern.

Complementary to graphics-consolidation.md, which covers the scanline RENDER helpers (tilemap/sprite/bitmap, indexed+priority) but not framebuffer ownership/format/lifecycle. Must preserve byte-identical output per machine (frameshot compare).

Shared root cause worth exploiting: the u8-index assumption is baked into the EXISTING Feature 2b helpers too — render_tilemap_scanline_indexed / render_scrolled_tilemap_scanline_indexed (core/src/gfx/tilemap.rs:107,216) and draw_sprite_row_indexed (core/src/gfx/sprite.rs:108) all take index_buf: &mut [u8]. That is precisely why atari_system1 cannot use them: it composites into vec![0u16; w*h] for its 1024-entry palette (atari_system1.rs:682) and a u8 buffer would truncate the 10-bit index. So introducing Indexed16 here should come with u16 variants of those helpers; that removes one of atari_system1's two blockers (the other is its priority model - a priority_pens mask + translucency applied during the motion-object merge, not a per-pixel u8 prio_buf - which is not addressed by widening the index).

For reference, Feature 2b IS implemented and in production use by gottlieb/qbert (3 call sites). mcr2 does not adopt it for unrelated structural reasons: 2x tile upscale (helper is 1:1) and dirty-tile incremental redraw (helper renders every scanline unconditionally). graphics-consolidation.md's table still lists mcr2 as a 2b target; that table is stale.

title: Galaxian's background (wolf-whistle) voice has never been compared
description:
Galaxian's melody, hit and fire each have an isolated scenario, a reference
driver arm, and a measured comparison. The background voice has none of them.

There is no tools/sound-compare/scenarios/galaxian/background.toml and no
GAL_EFFECT=background arm in drive_galaxian_single.lua. The multi-voice driver
drive_galaxian_sound.lua does exercise FS1-3, but that driver overlaps voices and
has never been through verify-reference.sh for this one, so nothing has checked
the background against anything.

This is the same shape of gap that hid Donkey Kong's jump: a board declared done
with one of its voices unmeasured.

WHAT IT IS. The wolf-whistle: a 4-bit R-1 ladder DAC (R15-R20) driving a 555
constant-current VCO on C15, through an op-amp mult/add (R31-R33) and a clamp,
whose output is the control voltage for three CV-modulated 555 astables
(R22/R23/C17, R25/R26/C18, R28/R29/C19), summed through R24/R27/R30 into C20.
Four 555s and a DAC, so considerably more machinery than the hit or the fire, and
correspondingly more to get wrong.

WHAT IS ALREADY IN PLACE:
  - a `background` probe on the sndcmp target, pointing at the `bg` node
  - node dumps for the whole chain in the mame-nodelog build: discrete_3 carries
    NODE_10, NODE_100, NODE_105, NODE_110 and NODE_111 (the DAC through the
    control voltage) and discrete_4 carries NODE_115, NODE_116, NODE_117 and
    NODE_120 (the three astables and their mix). Both dumps read correctly.

TO DO:
  1. Add a background.toml scenario. Note the DAC value is the stimulus and it
     SWEEPS, so unlike the other three this voice cannot be measured at one
     parked setting; either hold a few fixed DAC codes and measure each, or
     measure the sweep and compare the pitch trajectory.
  2. Add the driver arm and confirm it passes verify-reference.sh.
  3. Capture at 192 kHz and resample, per the reference-rate rule.
  4. Compare, starting from the node dumps rather than the output.
close_reason:
Measured, and it was already right.

FIRST COMPARISON of this voice, ours against a 192 kHz reference resampled to
44.1 kHz, over 1.5 s of steady warble:

                     ours      board
  gain ratio        0.97x               (-0.23 dB)
  fundamental      202.9 Hz   203.8 Hz
  centroid         269.0 Hz   272.4 Hz
  rolloff 85%      344.5 Hz   366.1 Hz
  crest              2.74       2.60
  band 0-150         5.46 %     5.80 %
  band 150-400      85.09 %    82.58 %
  band 400-1000      8.18 %    10.42 %
  band 1000-3000     1.21 %     1.15 %
  STFT              0.857
  -> within tolerance on every band, fundamental 0.4 % apart.

WHAT WAS ADDED:
  - tools/sound-compare/scenarios/galaxian/background.toml, which passes
    sndcmp verify
  - a GAL_EFFECT=background arm in drive_galaxian_single.lua, which passes
    verify-reference.sh (null silent, capture changes on a 30 ms nudge)
  - a set_lfo helper in that driver, and DAC parking in both sides' setup, since
    a fresh device starts at code 0 while the board starts at whatever the game
    last wrote, which is 15 in practice

WHY A PARKED DAC IS THE RIGHT SCENARIO, since the issue asked. The DAC does not
set the whistle's pitch. It sets the charging current of a 555 whose capacitor
sawtooth is what sweeps the three oscillators, and that sawtooth always runs
between a third and two thirds of the supply. So the DAC changes the warble's
RATE and not its depth: from the parts, about 63 ms per cycle at code 0 and
48 ms at code 15. Parking the DAC therefore still leaves a moving voice, and the
1.5 s window covers roughly 25 warble cycles, which averages to something
stationary. Sweeping the DAC as the game does would smear the spectrum for no
extra information.

A consequence worth recording: because the DAC only moves the rate, the
long-window average spectrum is nearly the same at every code, so this scenario
does NOT test the DAC ladder's weights. If those are ever in question the test
is the warble period, in the time domain, not the spectrum.

NODE DUMPS WERE NOT NEEDED and are not usable anyway: discrete_3 and discrete_4
in the current mame-nodelog build read as zeros, the same task-placement problem
that made the noise dump unusable. Localising was never required here because
nothing was wrong. Comparing first and localising only on a residual is the
right order regardless.

Also fixed while here: the fitted decay tau reported 143 seconds with an r2 of
0.000 on this sustained voice. The r2 was doing its job, but a number that
meaningless should not be printed, so decay_tau now returns nothing below an r2
of 0.5.

title: Epic: Monitor orientation framework — declarative rotation + cocktail flip
description:
Unify the four incompatible ways screen orientation is handled today into one declarative model. Machines report native (unrotated) dimensions and declare an Orientation (MAME-style FLIP_X/FLIP_Y/SWAP_XY bitfield, queried per-frame for dynamic cocktail DIPs); the frontend applies the transform centrally. Rotation, cocktail flip, and aspect fold into one path.

Today: (1) ScreenRotation enum (None/Rot270) used only by Tempest and only affects window geometry for raster; (2) ~12 raster machines bake rotation into render_frame via 4 gfx::rotate_* helpers + TimingConfig width/height swaps; (3) cocktail flip implemented 4 incompatible ways (mario_bros post-pass reverse, galaxian_video pre-rotate mirror, foodf source-coord mirror, gridlee scanline XOR); (4) display_aspect a separate hint. Board-delegation macro cannot forward rotation.

Approach: build the central path, migrate a 4-machine proof set (Tempest/vector, Q*Bert/ROT270, Galaga/ROT90+board-macro, Mario Bros/dynamic-cocktail), leave remaining ~12 machines baking-and-working. Full plan: ~/.claude/plans/should-we-develop-a-dapper-raccoon.md

title: Star Wars AVG busy window too short; VG_HALT clears early
description:
IN1 bit 6 is VG_HALT, the AVG done flag. We report done essentially always,
because trigger_avg() rasterises the entire vector list synchronously on the
$4600 GO write and the AVG is halted again by the time the CPU can look.
MAME models the AVG as taking real time (avg_starwars_device, done_r).

Caught under instruction-level lockstep against MAME 0.287: the two runs are
identical for 498,252 instructions and then

  idx 498252  EABA  LDA $4320     <- IN1
  idx 498253  ours A=$74   mame A=$34      (bit 6 differs)

Consequence: a game that spins waiting for VG_HALT exits the wait
immediately here, so it completes more work per frame than the hardware
would. That matches the measured symptom in phosphor-emulator-j63p — our
attract-mode slapstic bank switches run at 38/106/270 over 82/123/205 frames
against MAME's 39/87/187 — and it is the leading candidate for the state
divergence that eventually walks ESB into the frame-1129 failure path.

To reproduce the comparison:
  disasm trace --machine esb --frames 90 --cpu 0:regs \
    --entropy-file <mame LCG stream> -o ours.txt <roms>
  (MAME side: -debug -debugscript with `trace f,maincpu,noloop,{tracelog "%d %04X ",totalcycles,d}`
   under SDL_VIDEODRIVER=dummy)

Fix direction: give the AVG a duration. MAME derives it from the vector list
it walks; the cheapest faithful approach here is probably to count the AVG's
own cycles while rasterising and hold `halted` false for that many machine
cycles, rather than completing on the GO write.
notes:
2026-08-15 — the restructure this issue called for has landed (f184a12,
ea9c9c2), and the lockstep now verifies it (tooling in 75b5a92).

WHAT CHANGED

Avg::execute is now the sequencer loop itself rather than a per-instruction
decoder: it addresses the PROM with (halt ^ 1) | op | state, latches the next
state, dispatches handlers 0-7 when ST3 is set, and charges 8 master cycles
per state plus the beam time strobe3 consumes. states_for_op and its
"walk until a state repeats" construction are gone. The old decode_* bodies
now live in latch0-latch3 / strobe0-strobe3.

Two further sources of missing time came out of the restructure: CNTR now runs
the vector timer down before re-centering, and a run picks up the idle state
the sequencer parks in after a halt. run_cycles is sampled on the state that
raises the halt rather than summed to the end of the list.

Tempest and Quantum now load 136002-125, their own copy of the PROM. Quantum's
factory was calling load_program directly and bypassing load_rom_set, so
anything added there was dead code.

VERIFICATION (esb, 90 frames, MAME 0.287, instruction-level)

  before:  first divergence at instruction 507357
             ours cyc=2280017 pc=EABA D=74DF
             mame cyc=2280017 pc=EABA D=34DF     <- bit 6, VG_HALT
  after:   no divergence in 755843 instructions
             pc, D and cycle delta agree for the whole run

The "before" number is a control run of f184a12~1 against the same captured
reference, so the divergence this issue records reproduces on demand and it is
this change that closes it, not the harness.

Confirmed the entropy replay is not masking anything: re-running with 400 junk
values appended produces a byte-identical trace, so the recording never ran
out and the LFSR never silently took over.

Also measured, esb attract over 300 frames: the VG_HALT busy window grows from
a mean of 48,404 to 55,243 CPU cycles per GO, and the game issues 149 GO writes
instead of 165.

Frameshots at frames 400/900/1800: tempest and quantum pixel-identical across
the change; starwars and esb differ only in attract-sequence phase.

REPRO, corrected

The recipe in the description above does not work as written. `-debugscript`
is inert under `-debugger none` — that front-end resumes without ever pumping
the debugger's command loop — and the entropy stream had no recorded capture
method. Both are now checked in; see the header of
tools/mame_esb_lockstep.lua for the full command line, then
tools/lockstep_diff.py ours.txt mame_raw.txt.

Two traps worth repeating: clear MAME's -nvram_directory before each capture
(it writes NVRAM at exit, so run 2 is not a cold boot and splits from us at the
first $4500 read), and only the common prefix is comparable, since MAME
overruns the frame limit by a scheduler boundary.
close_reason: Fixed in f184a12: Avg::execute is now the PROM state sequencer rather than a per-instruction decoder, so the VG_HALT window comes from the real state sequence plus beam time. Verified by instruction-level lockstep against MAME 0.287 — esb now matches for all 755,843 instructions of a 90-frame run (pc, D, cycle delta), where a control run of the previous commit still diverges at instruction 507,357 on the LDA $4320 that reads VG_HALT.

title: M6809 indexed [n] extended indirect: reference core charges +8 cycles, datasheet says +5
description:
Documenting a KNOWN, EXPECTED cross-validation divergence so it is not re-investigated as a regression. No phosphor-side change is believed necessary.

SYMPTOM
  ./cross-validation/bin/validate_m6809 cpu-validation/test_data/m6809/*.json
  -> 264,090/266,000 pass. 53 opcodes fail a few cases each, always
     'cycles expected=N got=N+3' (expected = phosphor, got = reference).

CAUSE
Every failing case uses indexed postbyte 0x9F -- [n], extended indirect.
Verified by counting: a4.json has 8 failures and exactly 8 cases whose name
starts 'a4 9f'. All 53 affected opcodes are indexed; the deficit is uniformly 3.

WHICH SIDE IS RIGHT
MC6809E datasheet Table 2 (Indexed Addressing Mode) lists Extended Indirect,
16-Bit Address, [n], postbyte 10011111, as +5 cycles / +2 bytes. phosphor
charges 5 (core/src/cpu/m6809/alu.rs indexed_mode_internal: 0x0F => 0, plus
4 bus cycles). The reference core (cross-validation/mame0148/.../m6809.c)
charges 8. Per CLAUDE.md ('if cross-validation differs from datasheet for
timings, use the datasheet values') phosphor is correct.

NOTES
- Pre-existing, unrelated to phosphor-emulator-m6809-tst-vma-cycle-2kaj; the
  '6d 998/1000' figure quoted in that issue is this, not a TST problem.
- Per-opcode counts shift on every regeneration since they depend on how often
  a random postbyte lands on 0x9F (~4/1000 per indexed opcode).
- Recorded in cpu-validation/README_m6809.md under 'Known divergence'.

ACTION
Confirm the reading of Table 2 independently, then either close as
working-as-intended or, if the reference turns out to match real silicon,
reopen the timing question.
notes:
2026-08-09 — RETRACTION. I raised this to P1 and made it block j63p on the
theory that this cycle discrepancy was the source of j63p's timing drift.
That theory is DISPROVEN; priority is back to P3 and the dependency is
removed. j63p's cause is the CPU reset sequence costing 0 emulated cycles,
not instruction timing.

What the j63p side-by-side against MAME 0.287 does and does not say here:

DOES: over the first 454,189 instructions of ESB boot, our M6809 matches
modern MAME's cycle-stepped core EXACTLY — a constant offset and zero
per-instruction discrepancies. Many indexed modes are exercised (postbyte
modes 0x0-0x9, 0xC-0xE non-indirect, and 0x1/0x2/0x3/0x4/0x6/0x8/0x9
indirect). Our indexed timing is right for all of them.

DOES NOT: that workload never executes postbyte 0x9F ([n] extended
indirect), so it does not settle THIS issue either way. I briefly thought
it did — that was a decoding bug in my analysis script, which treated the
second byte of every instruction as a postbyte and so counted `LDA #$FF`
(86 FF) as postbyte 0xFF. Corrected: zero occurrences.

NEW EVIDENCE, static, still needs an empirical check:
Modern MAME (src/devices/cpu/m6809/m6809.lst, cycle-stepped, generated) is
a different core from the cross-validation reference (mame0148, 2013,
table-driven). Counting its cycle markers for the INDEXED routine, noting
that `dummy_vma(n)` is n cycles (m6809.h:217, it reads $FFFF n times):
  postbyte 0x84 (,R):   postbyte + dummy_read_opcode_arg + set_ea      = 3
  postbyte 0x9F ([n]):  postbyte + 2 offset reads + dummy_vma(1)
                        + 2 indirect reads + dummy_vma(1) + set_ea     = 8
  delta = +5
So MODERN MAME agrees with the datasheet and with phosphor; only the 2013
reference core charges +8. That is consistent with closing this as
working-as-intended, but it is a static reading of generated source, not a
measurement.

TO CLOSE: measure it. `mame esb ... -debug -debugscript` with
SDL_VIDEODRIVER=dummy works headlessly; inject `A6 9F nn nn` (LDA [n]) and
`A6 84` (LDA ,X) into RAM, trace with {tracelog "%d ",totalcycles}, and
diff the deltas. My first attempt at this failed — only the trailing NOPs
were traced and the injected LDAs produced no usable line — so the
injection/step sequencing needs work.

title: Conditional DIP options: bonus-life tables depend on Lives (Galaga/Dig Dug/Xevious)
description:
The DIP framework (DipOption/DipChoice in core machine.rs) has no support for options whose valid choices depend on another option's value. On real Namco Galaga-family hardware the Bonus Life bits are interpreted differently based on the Lives/fighters setting (MAME models this with PORT_CONDITION):
- Galaga: Bonus Life (DSWB 0x38) conditioned on fighters (DSWB 0xc0).
- Xevious: Bonus Life (DSWA 0x1c) conditioned on Lives (DSWA 0x60).
- Dig Dug: similar.

Today all three flatten it to one non-conditional table, so the labels shown are only correct for one Lives setting (and Galaga's current labels don't even match MAME's conditional tables). The DIP bits still reach the game; only the UI labels are wrong.

Fix: add an optional condition to DipOption (e.g. {other_mask, equals/not-equals, value} + per-condition choice lists), teach assert_dip_banks_valid + the frontend rebinding UI to honor it, then make the Galaga/Dig Dug/Xevious bonus-life tables conditional and correct against MAME.

title: golden_frame_test runs 39 machines single-threaded in one test
description:
golden_frame_test runs 39 machines on one thread because it is one test.

MEASURED: 173.53s for `every_pinned_machine_still_draws_its_frame` over 39
machines, all of it in a single #[test] that loops over the registry. The Rust
test harness parallelises across tests, not within one, so the other 38 cores sit
idle. Emulating a machine for 1800 to 2400 frames is pure CPU with no shared
mutable state between machines, which is close to the ideal case for fanning out.

Two ways, with a real tradeoff between them:

1. rayon (or a thread pool) inside the existing test. Smallest change, keeps the
   collected-failures reporting exactly as it is: "9 of 39 pinned machines no
   longer draw their pinned frame" in one message, which is the diagnosis when a
   shared renderer moves. Needs the per-machine work to be Send, and the failure
   list to be collected through a Mutex or a map-reduce.
2. One #[test] per machine, generated by a macro over the registry. The harness
   then parallelises for free and reports each machine by name, and a single
   machine can be re-run with a filter instead of an env var. The cost is the
   aggregate message: the runner lists failures individually, so "these nine
   moved and these thirty-one did not" has to be read off the summary rather
   than being stated in one place. The file's own doc comment argues for the
   aggregate, so this is a deliberate reversal, not an oversight.

Option 2 also removes the need for PHOSPHOR_GOLDEN_ONLY, which exists only
because the test cannot be filtered by name today.

CHECK THE PREMISE BEFORE BUILDING EITHER. Confirm the run is actually CPU-bound
across machines and not serialised on ROM archive reads or on a shared lazily
initialised registry. If it is I/O, threads buy nothing and the measurement will
say so.

RELATED: phosphor-emulator-lpu3 says audio_sanity_test takes 7 minutes and is
the cost of every local test run. It has the same shape, a single test looping
over machines, and probably the same fix. Worth doing both with one decision
rather than twice.

Neither is a correctness change, so the acceptance check is that the same set of
machines passes and fails before and after, on the same pins.
close_reason: golden 173.53s -> 26.94s with an identical verdict; audio ~7min -> 93.6s, half of which was a doubled sweep rather than threading. Audio now has a ~94s floor set by galaga alone, which no thread count beats; reducing it means replaying less of the longest movies, filed separately.

comments.author: pjl
comments.text:
Done for the parallelism part, in 880429f and 0fc0f35. The premise the issue
said to check first turned out to be half right, and the audio half has a floor
that threads cannot move.

MEASURED.

  golden_frame_test   173.53s -> 26.94s   39 machines, identical verdict
  audio_sanity_test    ~7 min -> 93.6s    5 tests pass

Golden spends 4:42 of CPU in 28s of wall, a ratio of 9.9 on 16 cores, so the
suspicion that it might be I/O bound on ROM archives is settled: it is not.

THE BIGGEST SINGLE WIN WAS NOT THREADS. audio_sanity_test was emulating the
whole roster TWICE. sweep() is a plain function, both ratchet tests call it, and
libtest runs those two on separate threads, so the split its own doc comment
describes ("Measure every machine once, then judge") bought the shared judgement
but not the shared work. A OnceLock fixes it: first test through does the sweep,
the second waits. That is half the audio saving before any thread exists.

HOW IT WAS DONE. harness/tests/common/map_parallel, std::thread::scope over a
shared index cursor, no rayon: the crate has no dependencies and the process-wide
pool rayon would bring is worth less now that neither suite sweeps twice.
Results go back in INPUT order, which matters because these suites report "these
nine machines moved and these thirty-one did not" and a failure list that
reorders itself cannot be diffed. Judging stays sequential and costs nothing.
PHOSPHOR_TEST_THREADS=1 forces either suite back to sequential.

WHAT WRITING THE TESTS FOUND. std::thread::scope propagates a worker's panic but
REPLACES the payload with "a scoped thread panicked". Every carefully worded
assertion inside capture() and measure() would have become that string. Each
item is now caught and the lowest-index panic re-raised with its own message, so
a parallel failure reads like the sequential one it replaces and is reproducible
rather than depending on which worker lost the race. The test written to check
this failed on its first run, which is how it was noticed.

Six tests on the helper, no ROMs needed, so it is covered in CI where the suites
themselves skip. The load-bearing one makes item 0 sleep longest: an
implementation that pushes results as they complete passes every uniform-work
test and fails that one.

EQUIVALENCE, on real data rather than by argument: the parallel golden run fails
on exactly the sequential run's set minus robotron and sinistar, the two
recaptured in 0e796ed. The audio suite's sequential-vs-parallel table comparison
was attempted and the run was killed twice; it is NOT verified that way, and the
honest statement is that only the helper's ordering guarantees and the golden
equivalence back it.

THE AUDIO SUITE NOW HAS A FLOOR OF ABOUT 94s AND MORE THREADS CANNOT BEAT IT.
PHOSPHOR_AUDIO_REPORT=1 prints the cost breakdown that shows why:

  galaga 93.59s, digdug 88.08s, dkong 48.29s, dowild 40.90s, marble 40.85s
  40 machines, 654.2s of CPU in 93.6s of wall (7.0x parallel on 16 cores)

Galaga alone IS the wall time. Emulating one machine is sequential, so the
makespan cannot go below the longest board, and the other 38 total roughly 470s
and fit underneath with cores idle. The 44% utilisation is fifteen cores
finishing early and waiting on two, not serialisation left to find.

ALSO FIXED, small and honest about its size: measure() decompressed each ROM zip
twice, once to answer an existence question and once inside Harness::build. Now
answered by checking for the file. It removes real work and does not move the
wall time, because galaga sets that either way.

WHAT IS LEFT, and it is a change to what the suite measures rather than to how
it is scheduled. The only remaining lever is replaying less of the longest
movies. Galaga and digdug are movie fixtures and their recordings are long; the
integrity statistics (DC offset, clipped fraction, silent fraction) plausibly
converge long before the recording ends. Capping the span would need the
statistics shown stable first, by moving the window two ways and changing its
length, or it is just measuring less and hoping. That is a separate issue and a
decision about the suite's contract, not a performance tweak.

title: Slow test binaries are single tests doing long loops
description:
Several slow test binaries are one #[test] doing a long loop, which is the one
shape libtest cannot help with: it parallelises across tests, not within one.

MEASURED, from a full `cargo test --workspace --all-features --locked` on 16
cores with ROMs at the default path (so the ROM-gated suites ran):

    secs  tests  binary
   70.89     18  harness/tests/movie_test.rs
   70.44      1  cpu-validation/tests/i8088_single_step_test.rs
   27.59     13  harness/tests/audio_sanity_test.rs      (already fanned out)
   26.34      1  harness/tests/save_state_rom_test.rs
   11.33      7  harness/tests/boot_check_test.rs
    9.45      1  cpu-validation/tests/z80_single_step_test.rs
    9.42      1  frontend/tests/watchpoints.rs
    7.97      1  harness/tests/frameshot_parity.rs
    7.90      1  frontend/tests/state_and_dip.rs
    4.76      1  cpu-validation/tests/m68000_single_step_test.rs
    4.51      1  cpu-validation/tests/m6502_single_step_test.rs
    1.29      1  cpu-validation/tests/m6809_single_step_test.rs
    0.68      1  cpu-validation/tests/m6800_single_step_test.rs

267s of test time across 127 binaries. Cargo runs binaries concurrently, so the
test phase cannot finish faster than its slowest binary: two of them are ~71s, so
that is the floor today no matter how many cores are free.

THE CANDIDATES, and what the independent unit is.

A. One #[test] over independent per-file work. The CPU validators each walk a
   directory of vector files, decompress, parse and run every case:

     i8088       70.44s   323 files   (test_all_i8088_opcodes)
     z80          9.45s  1604 files
     m6502        4.51s   256 files
     m68000       4.76s   124 files
     m6809/m6800  2.0s combined

B. One #[test] over `registry::all()`, one machine per iteration, which is
   exactly the shape already fixed in golden_frame_test and audio_sanity_test:

     save_state_rom_test  26.34s  a_snapshot_of_a_running_game_determines_everything_that_follows_it
     movie_test           42.38s  a_recorded_session_replays_identically_on_a_booted_machine

   movie_test's binary is 70.89s over 18 tests, so libtest is already
   parallelising them; that one 42.4s test is its floor. Timed individually the
   next three are 22.4s, 15.0s and 14.7s, and those loop over the registry too.

C. Single tests that are NOT a file or registry loop, so their cost is
   unexplained: frontend/tests/watchpoints.rs 9.42s,
   harness/tests/frameshot_parity.rs 7.97s, frontend/tests/state_and_dip.rs
   7.90s. Look before assuming they fan out.

EXPECTED WIN. Fixing i8088 and movie_test's slowest test moves the floor from
~71s to whichever binary is next, which is audio_sanity at 27.6s; fixing
save_state_rom_test as well leaves audio_sanity as the floor. So the test phase
plausibly goes from ~71s to ~28s, and the CPU validators from ~91s of CPU to
single digits of wall. Confirm rather than assume: the numbers above are one run
on one machine.

THE HELPER EXISTS BUT IS NOT REACHABLE. harness/tests/common/map_parallel does
exactly this: a bounded pool over a shared index cursor, results returned in
INPUT order so failure lists stay diffable, PHOSPHOR_TEST_THREADS=1 to force
sequential, and six tests of its own. It lives in harness/tests/common, so the
cpu-validation crate cannot see it. THAT IS THE DESIGN QUESTION THIS ISSUE FORKS
ON and it should be answered before any of the work:

  - move it into phosphor-cpu-validation's lib, which already exposes helpers
    (vector_dir, require_test_data) to its own tests, and have harness depend on
    that; or
  - add a small test-support crate to the workspace; or
  - duplicate ~40 lines per crate and accept the copies.

TWO TRAPS ALREADY PAID FOR, do not rediscover them:
  - std::thread::scope propagates a worker's panic but REPLACES the payload with
    "a scoped thread panicked", which throws away the assertion message. Catch
    per item and re-raise the lowest-index panic. map_parallel already does.
  - Results must come back in input order, or a failure list reorders itself
    between runs and cannot be diffed.

MEMORY IS A REAL CONSTRAINT FOR THE 8088 CASE, unlike the machine sweeps. The
8088 vectors are 727 MB compressed over 323 files, the largest single file 7 MB
gzipped, and each is decompressed and parsed into serde structures before being
run. Sixteen of those at once is a different proposition from sixteen emulated
machines. Measure peak RSS, and bound the worker count for this one if needed
rather than discovering it as an OOM kill in a full workspace run.

ACCEPTANCE. Not "it got faster": the same set of tests passes and fails as
before, on the same inputs, with the before and after numbers in the commit.
PHOSPHOR_TEST_THREADS=1 must reproduce the sequential result exactly.
close_reason: Test-phase floor ~71s -> 30.0s, workspace run 4:54 -> 2:51. movie_test 70.9->25.2, i8088 70.4->11.4, save_state_rom 26.3->4.0, verdicts identical. Two hand-rolled schedulers measured and both wrong (oversubscription 80.0s, starvation 74.6s); rayon as a dev-dependency fixed both. Remaining validators left alone, measured as below the new floor.

comments.author: pjl
comments.text:
Done in 25b9c0d.

  movie_test              70.89s -> 25.24s
  i8088_single_step_test  70.44s -> 11.38s
  save_state_rom_test     26.34s ->  3.99s
  test-phase floor        ~71s   -> 30.0s   (audio_sanity, already fanned out)
  full workspace run      4:54   -> 2:51
  127 test groups green either way

THE ISSUE'S OWN DIAGNOSIS WAS RIGHT AND ITS TARGET LIST WAS WRONG. It named
movie_test's 42.4s test as that binary's floor. That was measured with the test
running alone; timing all eighteen individually found
reset_is_not_a_power_cycle_so_arming_must_rebuild at 70.41s, which had never
been timed and which simply IS the binary. The 42.4s and 22.4s tests fanned out
to 5.7s and 3.1s and made no difference to the binary at all until the 70.4s one
was fixed. Time every candidate before picking one.

THE FORK THIS ISSUE NAMED RESOLVED ITSELF. It asked where map_parallel should
live so cpu-validation could reach it. The answer turned out to be nowhere: the
validators accumulate counts rather than asserting per item, so they need a
reduction, not the panic-ordering helper. They use rayon directly and reduce
per-file outcomes in file order. If a third consumer ever wants the helper
itself, that question comes back.

TWO HAND-ROLLED SCHEDULERS WERE MEASURED AND BOTH WERE WRONG. Recorded in the
commit and in the source, because neither failure is obvious:

- A pool per call oversubscribed: libtest already runs a binary's tests
  concurrently, so each one spawning sixteen workers put ~80 threads on 16
  cores. movie_test went to 80.0s, SLOWER than the sequential loops it replaced.
- A process-wide budget handed out first-come starved the caller that mattered:
  the quick tests start first and took every worker, so the 70.4s test got none.
  74.6s, no better than doing nothing.

Only a shared work-stealing pool fixes both, which is what rayon is. It is a
dev-dependency of the two test crates and nothing shipped depends on it. The
"~40 lines duplicated" option the issue listed would have carried the bug too.

EQUIVALENCE, checked rather than assumed. i8088: 2,577,000 passed, 0 failed, 279
files, 44 skipped, identical parallel and with RAYON_NUM_THREADS=1 (69.94s).
save_state_rom_test: 39 machines both ways, PHOSPHOR_TEST_THREADS=1 reproducing
26.77s. map_parallel keeps results in input order and re-raises the lowest-index
panic with its own message, so a failing run names the same item however the work
was scheduled.

THE MEMORY WORRY DID NOT MATERIALISE. The issue flagged 727 MB of compressed
8088 vectors as a reason to bound the workers. Peak did not become a problem at
16 workers, because rayon processes files as it steals them rather than holding
all 323 decompressed at once. No cap was needed and none was added.

LEFT ALONE, MEASURED. z80 9.45s, m68000 4.76s, m6502 4.51s, m6809 1.29s, m6800
0.68s: all below the 30s floor audio_sanity now sets, so fanning them out moves
no wall time anyone waits on. Same shape, same fix, if that floor ever drops.
Not touched at all: watchpoints 9.42s, frameshot_parity 7.97s, state_and_dip
7.90s, whose cost is not a loop over independent work and wants its own look.

title: Xevious 54XX discrete explosion sound
description:
Wire the shared Namco 54XX (MB8844) explosion-sound generator into Xevious so bomb/explosion effects are audible. The Xevious M3 pass (xevious-8u2a.3.2) deliberately left this stubbed silent: WSG melodic/effect sound works, but 54XX commands via 06XX chip-select 3 are discarded at machines/src/namco_galaga.rs:771. A seam is documented in the xevious.rs module header.

Depends on the Galaga 54XX issue (phosphor-emulator-uxi9), which builds the reusable LLE 54XX device + discrete DAC/filter primitives. This issue then:
- Fits the 54XX on the Xevious board (54xx.bin ships in xevious.zip) and routes its output into the Xevious audio mix.
- Supplies Xevious's DAC/filter network values (per MAME xevious/galaga audio) if they differ from Galaga's bosco_54xx_dac ladder.
- Updates the xevious.rs header note + README bullet to drop 'explosion channel stubbed'.
- Tests: machine-level check that an in-game explosion command produces non-silent output.

Timings/datasheet take precedence over MAME per project convention; keep MAME refs in commit/PR, not source comments.

title: Per-game settings: per-machine config overrides + unify DIP/binding persistence
description:
Make all config.toml settings overridable per game and restructure persistence so a machine's config overrides, DIP switch state, and input bindings live together under one per-machine section.

Today: config.toml (config.rs Config: rom_path, nvram_path, save_path, scale) is entirely global. state.toml (state.rs State) already persists input_bindings and dip_switches as separate top-level maps keyed by machine_id. So bindings + DIPs are per-game but config is not, and the three per-machine concerns are scattered.

Goal:
- Per-game config overrides for every Config field (rom_path, nvram_path, save_path, scale), keyed by machine_id. Resolution order: CLI arg > per-game override > global config.toml > built-in default. Global config.toml stays the user-edited default source.
- Restructure DIP + binding storage into a single per-machine settings section instead of separate top-level input_bindings / dip_switches maps. Sketch: State { window_position, machines: HashMap<String, MachineSettings> } where MachineSettings { scale, rom_path, nvram_path, save_path, dip_switches: Vec<u8>, input_bindings: Vec<SerializedBinding> } (all optional / diff-only — omit fields equal to the resolved default, drop the whole entry when empty, preserving the current no-redundant-defaults behavior).

Touch points: frontend/src/config.rs (Config), frontend/src/state.rs (State + save/load), frontend/src/main.rs (load/resolve/persist: lines ~98-150 build bindings, dips, scale; lines ~134-150 persist diffs).

Considerations:
- Backward-compat / migration for existing state.toml (top-level input_bindings + dip_switches). Decide: one-time migration on load vs. accept a clean break (state.toml is auto-generated, low stakes) — document the choice.
- Keep the diff-only persistence (bindings_eq pattern, DIP-vs-default compare) so unchanged games leave no entry.
- Likely warrants splitting into subtasks (config.rs/state.rs schema + resolution; main.rs wiring + migration; tests) when picked up.
close_reason: Unified per-machine settings into a single [machines.<name>] section in state.toml (MachineSettings with diff-only config overrides + DIP/binding state), with one-time migration from legacy top-level maps; wired CLI > per-game > config > default resolution for scale/rom_path/nvram_path/save_path in main.rs. Keyed by registry/CLI name (rather than machine_id) so per-game rom_path can resolve before machine creation.

title: Marble Madness: motion-object (MOB) rendering incorrect
description: Observed during the mid-frame-raster Phase 0 audit: Marble Madness (atari_system1) renders motion objects (MOBs) incorrectly. Marble's scroll is vblank-latched (Tier B) but MOB rendering is visibly wrong in gameplay (~frame 1200+). Separate from the raster classification; likely in atari_system1 render_motion_objects / sprite decode for the marble ROM set.
close_reason: Fixed by 327a182 (draw motion objects from a vblank snapshot, not live state). Confirmed against marble.zip: attract frames 1200/1400/1500 render the marbles with no stale red wedge, and gameplay (coin + start + trackball) renders the player marble tracking input across frames 120-900 with the score updating — the gameplay case this issue was filed for, which the fix commit did not cover. Caveat found and closed: the original regression test latched the snapshot by hand, so deleting the snapshot_motion_objects() call from tick() left the suite green; 03a5404 adds vblank_tick_latches_the_motion_object_snapshot, verified to fail without that call.

title: Asteroids Deluxe: emulate + expose the L8 coinage DIP bank
description: Asteroids Deluxe has two DIP banks: R5 (game options — Language/Lives/Min Plays/Difficulty/Bonus Life, already exposed via DipSwitches as bank 0) and L8 (coinage — Coinage/Right Coin/Center Coin/Bonus Coins). The emulator only models the single R5 byte (dip_switches). Add the L8 dip byte field, wire its read, and expose it as a second DipSwitchBank per MAME's astdelux L8 layout. Defaults must preserve current behavior.

title: Add Quantum (Atari color vector, 68000 + AVG)
description: Atari Quantum (1982) arcade machine. Hardware: MC68000 + Atari color AVG vector generator + 2x POKEY + trackball. Both the 68000 core and the AVG are already implemented; this is primarily board wiring (memory map, I/O, AVG color-decode variant) plus ROM definitions. See README Future > Games.
close_reason: Implemented Quantum: AvgVariant::Quantum color-AVG decode in core, plus a standalone 68000 board (machines/src/quantum.rs) with memory map, 2x POKEY, X2212 NVRAM, trackball, DSW0, periodic IRQ auto-ack, and three rev registrations. Tests pass; visual tuning against MAME left to bring-up.

title: Pac-Man / Ms. Pac-Man (namco_pac): migrate to declarative ROT90
close_reason: namco_pac board emits native 288x224 RGB and declares Orientation::ROT90 (forwarded to Pac-Man + Ms. Pac-Man via board macro); frontend rotates centrally. TIMING reports native dims.

title: Concrete bus dispatch: Do Castle family
description: Convert docastle.rs (two Z80s, five registered variants, eight bus_split! sites, board and machines in one file) per docs/designs/concrete-bus-dispatch.md. Follow the Galaga shape: group the CPUs into one field beside the bus, one generic per-cycle tick. Measure docastle before/after; run golden frames for all five variants.
close_reason:
Done in f38e13a.

Numbers (phosphor-bench, release, 400f x 5 reps, best of 6 alternating runs, idle host):
  docastle 2.506 -> 2.403 ms/f  -4.1%
  dorunrun 3.202 -> 3.095       -3.3%

Modest, and diagnosed rather than shrugged at: these are the slowest boards in the bench set and most of a frame is not bus dispatch. Four SN76489A PSGs are serviced every cycle, and every main-CPU T-state clones the whole Z80 for the WAIT rewind. Filed the clone as its own issue.

Shape: simplest possible -- the board already decodes through variant.map(), so DocastleBoard implements Bus and IS the bus for all five registered variants. No view, no trait, no per-game wrapper. Both Z80s moved to DocastleSystem; tick/step_main/run_scanlines/run_frame became free functions over (main, sub, board).

Why the split has to be real here: step_main rewinds the main Z80 when a latch read asserts WAIT -- the board sets main_retry from *inside* a bus read and the caller restores a snapshot afterwards. That handshake only works if the CPU is reachable independently of the bus it is reading, which is exactly what this refactor provides (previously it worked through the aliased raw pointer).

Also inverted the frame loop to scanline-outer / cycle-inner (VBLANK IRQ + the sub CPU's periodic raster IRQ were the only per-scanline work), renamed DocastleBoard::check_interrupts to interrupt_state to avoid Bus-method recursion, and preserved the save-state layout (machine writes both CPUs before the board, the order the board used).

Six of the eight bus_split! sites were in tests; they became sys.step_cycle() loops with bus_read/bus_write for direct bus pokes.

Golden frames unchanged for all three pinned variants (docastle, dorunrun, dowild); machine, harness and ROM-gated suites pass; clippy and fmt clean.

title: Epic: Raster sampling fidelity
description:
Design: docs/designs/raster-sampling-fidelity.md

Successor to the CLOSED mid-frame-raster-fidelity epic
(phosphor-emulator-mid-frame-raster-7zzi). That epic asked "which machines
exhibit a mid-frame raster effect?", measured the answer, and correctly did
almost nothing. This epic asks a different question — "at what rate does the
hardware sample each piece of video state, and do we match it?" — and reaches a
different answer. Nothing in the prior audit was wrong; the acceptance standard
changed.

WHY REVISIT. The Phase 0 audit's conclusion rests on a scope condition stated in
its own Method section: writes were captured across representative attract-DEMO
gameplay. That parenthetical is an assumption, not a measurement. Nothing covered
real gameplay past the demo loop, later levels, cocktail mode, service mode, or
non-default DIPs. "Tier B" does not mean "this machine has no mid-frame effects";
it means "none appeared in the attract loop". Nine machines carry that assumption
and nothing tracks it.

Two of the nine were additionally classified B on VISIBILITY grounds despite
genuine active-display writes: burgertime (scroll written 4x at scanlines 88-91)
and shollow (palette rewritten across active display in 4 of 2400 frames). On
hardware those frames show the rows above the write with the old value and the
rows below with the new one; we render them uniformly. They were classified B
because the effect does not repeat. That is an argument from "nobody will
notice", and CLAUDE.md ranks Correctness first and Performance last.

THE PRINCIPLE: sample each piece of video state at the rate the hardware samples
it. This SUBSUMES per-scanline rendering and also RULES IT OUT where the hardware
latches at vblank. atari_system1 is the in-tree existence proof of both halves at
once — per-scanline MO bands driven by a mid-frame bank switch, AND an mo_shadow
snapshot of sprite RAM taken at vblank because the MO circuit reads a list
captured then, not live RAM. Rendering that board's sprites per-scanline from
live RAM would introduce tearing a real cabinet never shows.

Per-scanline rendering does not make the Tier A/B classification more accurate.
It makes it UNNECESSARY — which is the actual reason to do this work, and the
reason it is worth doing on machines whose frames would not change at all today.

A reasonable stopping point is after W3. W4 is the part to defer if effort is
constrained.

title: W1: per-scanline palette on gottlieb and mcr2
description:
W1 — the cheapest real accuracy win in the design, and it fixes the shollow case.

gottlieb.rs:873 and mcr2.rs:539 have a byte-for-byte identical final pass: a flat
iteration over a palette-INDEX buffer against a single palette. Because these
boards composite into an index buffer and resolve colour only at the very end,
the palette can be made per-scanline WITHOUT TOUCHING TILE OR SPRITE RENDERING AT
ALL.

1. Add `palette_scanline: Vec<[(u8,u8,u8); N]>` (N = 16 gottlieb / 64 mcr2).
2. In the existing per-scanline hook, copy palette_rgb into
   palette_scanline[scanline].
3. render_frame iterates row-outer and indexes the row's snapshot.
4. Mark it #[save_skip] (derived, rebuilt every frame) but SEED IT FROM
   palette_rgb IN load_state, or the first frame after a load resolves against a
   stale snapshot.

COST: gottlieb 240 x 16 x 3 = 11.5 KB; mcr2 480 x 64 x 3 = 92 KB. Per frame, one
48-byte or 192-byte copy_from_slice per scanline. Negligible. Zero change to the
render loops.

This also sidesteps a real conflict: mcr2 is simultaneously the machine that most
needs a mid-frame fix and the one whose renderer least fits per-scanline
rendering (dirty-gated per-tile cache at 2x upscale — graphics-consolidation.md
recommends against migrating it on structural grounds that still hold). W1 fixes
mcr2's actual defect without touching the structure that makes it a bad migration
target.

WORTH DOING HERE: gottlieb and mcr2's index->RGB passes are identical and W1
changes both the same way. Extract a shared gfx::resolve_indexed_scanline rather
than editing the same loop twice.

ACCEPTANCE: golden frames byte-identical and MUST NOT BE RECAPTURED (the audit
says these boards write palette during vblank in all but 4 of 2400 frames), PLUS
a targeted test that writes the palette at a known active-display scanline and
asserts only rows below it change. Without that second test a migration can be
byte-identical and still not honour mid-frame changes.

atari_system1 uses a u16 index buffer and the same technique applies, but its
palette is larger and its resolve pass differs — follow-on, not part of W1.

title: W2: burgertime BnJ background scroll during active display
description:
W2 — burgertime background scroll during active display.

The audit measured 4 writes to 0x4004 at scanlines 88-91 across 4 frames. That
register is bnj_scroll0 (btime.rs:274), which drives three things in
draw_background (btime.rs:701): bits 0-1 horizontal scroll, bit 2 background
tile-bank offset, bit 4 background layer ENABLE (btime.rs:576).

CONFIRM BEFORE BUILDING ANYTHING. bnj_ is the Bump 'n' Jump register set and this
board is shared. First establish whether Burger Time enables the background layer
at all — if bnj_scroll0 & 0x10 is never set on this ROM set, draw_background
returns early and the four writes are invisible regardless of when they land. If
so, CLOSE THIS AS A NON-ISSUE and record the finding; that is a perfectly good
outcome and cheaper than the alternative.

If the layer IS enabled: sample bnj_scroll0 into a per-scanline array in the
frame hook and have draw_background consume the row's value. Same shape as W1, no
restructuring of btime's tile blitter.

ACCEPTANCE: golden frame unchanged for the 2396 frames with no mid-frame write,
plus a targeted test asserting a mid-frame scroll write splits the background.

title: W3: latched-vs-live determination for the sprite layer
description:
W3 — determine, per board, whether the sprite/motion-object circuit reads a list
captured at vblank or reads sprite RAM live during hblank. RESEARCH, NOT CODE.

WHY THIS IS A HARD PREREQUISITE FOR W4. The prior audit traced when the CPU
WRITES. That does not answer when the video circuit READS, and it is the read
side that decides whether per-scanline sampling is correct. Rendering a
vblank-latched sprite layer per-scanline from live RAM would introduce tearing a
real cabinet never shows — a NEW bug, introduced in the name of accuracy.

Nearly all the uncertainty in the whole design sits in this one layer. Tilemap
VRAM, scroll registers, palette, bank and flip latches are all read as the beam
scans, so per-scanline is strictly better for them. Sprites are board-specific.
That asymmetry is what makes this tractable: take the safe win now and quarantine
the part that needs research.

BOARDS TO COVER: namco_galaga (galaga/digdug/xevious), btime, mrdo, foodf,
gottlieb, mcr2, atari_system1 (KNOWN latched — use as the reference,
atari_system1.rs:451 mo_shadow), plus the already-per-scanline boards for
completeness. Determine from schematics and a reference driver; per project
convention cite them in the commit, not in source comments.

Record the result as a table in raster-sampling-fidelity.md. Two outcomes per
board:
- LIVE -> sprites may be rendered per-scanline from live RAM (unblocks W4).
- LATCHED -> model the latch explicitly, mo_shadow-style, and keep whole-frame
  sprite compositing.

W3 IS WORTH DOING EVEN IF W4 NEVER HAPPENS. A board that reads a vblank-captured
list but renders from live RAM at end-of-frame is wrong TODAY in the opposite
direction, and nobody has checked. Any such board found is an accuracy fix in its
own right.

title: W4: scanline-outer restructure of the tilemap layer
description:
W4 — invert the render nesting from layer-outer to scanline-outer for the
LIVE-READ layers only (tilemap, scroll, palette, bank, flip). Sprites follow W3's
per-board answer. The bulk of the labour, and the part to defer if effort is
constrained.

THE SAFETY PROPERTY THAT MAKES THIS ATTRACTIVE. The prior audit establishes that
these machines do not write video registers during active display in the measured
window. Therefore per-scanline rendering must produce BYTE-IDENTICAL output on
every golden pin. golden_frame_test becomes an exact regression gate: any hash
change is a bug, not an expected improvement, and MUST NOT BE RECAPTURED. That is
an unusually strong position for a correctness refactor — the accuracy guarantee
is obtained at zero output risk, verified by tests that already exist.

Note the structural pattern these renderers share: they are layer-outer,
scanline-inner. Even the ones already calling the shared scanline helpers
(galaga, digdug, xevious, gottlieb call render_tilemap_scanline_indexed) call
them from a `for scanline` loop INSIDE a whole-frame layer pass. Inverting that
nesting is the work, and it is not mechanical. Roughly 50-100 lines per machine.
mrdo and foodf are per-pixel whole-frame loops rather than layer passes and need
more care.

Layer ORDER can itself be a mid-frame-variable register — gottlieb picks
tiles-over-sprites vs sprites-over-tiles from video_control & 0x01
(gottlieb.rs:732), read once per frame today. Under scanline-outer that becomes
per-row for free.

EXPLICITLY OUT OF SCOPE: mcr2 (dirty-gated per-tile cache at 2x upscale; W1
addresses its actual defect and a restructure would fight its dirty-tracking
design for no measured benefit), vector machines, and the 19 boards already
rendering per-scanline.

ACCEPTANCE: golden frames byte-identical, not recaptured; a targeted mid-frame
test per machine; an explicit assertion that vblank-latched state (galaga's
update_starfield_at_vblank, atari_system1's mo_shadow) is NOT re-sampled per line
— that is the main way this could introduce a new bug. Perf: tile-info lookups go
from per-tile to per-tile-per-scanline (1008 -> 8064 per frame on a 36x28
tilemap); expected negligible, confirm with phosphor-bench in release.

title: Standing convention: new raster machines render per-scanline
description:
Add to machines/CLAUDE.md: NEW RASTER MACHINES RENDER PER-SCANLINE FROM LIVE
STATE BY DEFAULT. A whole-frame render needs a comment justifying it, and any
state the hardware latches at vblank is modelled as an explicit snapshot rather
than read live.

This is what stops the ratio drifting back. The prior epic measured 9 render-once
machines against 19 per-scanline ones; without a stated default, the next machine
added is a coin flip and the audit has to be redone.

Cheap, independent of every other item in this epic, and adopt it regardless of
whether W4 ever happens.

title: Remove compatibility aliases (MemoryMap, Machine)
description: Final cleanup: remove the migration-only MemoryMap and Machine aliases once all code has migrated. One alias at a time - never two half-migrations open at once. Blocked by all four prior epics.
close_reason: All 3 subtasks complete: MemoryMap alias removed + module split (9vp.1), Machine alias trait removed (9vp.2), docs updated to final names (9vp.3). No compatibility aliases remain.

description: Remove the MemoryMap alias; update the #[debug_map] macro and MachineDebug::memory_map return type to the final AddressSpace16/AddressSpace32 names; rename module; fix re-exports.
close_reason: MemoryMap alias removed; all 14 boards, the debug_map/BusDebug macro, and MachineDebug::memory_map name AddressSpace16 directly. memory_map.rs split into address_space.rs (shared RegionId/AccessKind/DebugRead/DebugWrite/MemoryBacking) + address_space16.rs (Phase 7 module split); re-exports fixed. Landed as 2 commits.

description: Remove the Machine compatibility alias trait; migrate any remaining references to MachineCore/FrontendMachine.
close_reason: Machine alias trait + blanket impl + core/prelude re-exports removed (all call sites were already on FrontendMachine/MachineCore); stale 'Machine trait' comment banners renamed to the real traits. Landed as 2 commits.
