A first cut was worse still (8.9 on tempest) from a float divide and several casts per pixel to locate the bilinear taps; precomputing the taps per row and column and walking the downsample in blocks rather than dividing per pixel took it to 5.06.

The remaining cost is inherent to compositing a full-resolution frame on the CPU, so the answer is not to optimise it further but to put it where a blur is free. The CPU implementation stays because it is the only one that can be tested: the physics tests cannot run against a shader.

Left to do: halation in vector_gl.rs. An FBO, a downsample, a separable blur and an additive composite, with the same (1-f)/f split and the same gain correction so the two renderers keep agreeing about what full white means.

Also noted while measuring, not chased: even core-only, asteroid renders in 2.68 ms against 0.39 ms of emulation, and most of that is clearing and converting a 12.6 MB float accumulator every frame rather than sweeping vectors. It is 5.4x realtime and off the play path, so it was left alone.

comments.author: pjl
comments.text:
Done. CPU implementation in 578f818 (off by default), GL in c7fa39f, halation fraction settled at 0.07 by eye.

The halo width is derived: light past the critical angle cannot leave the faceplate, so it reflects back, crosses the glass again and re-emerges at 2*t*tan(asin(1/n)), about 19 mm on an 11 mm faceplate at n = 1.54, or 5% of the tube long axis. The fraction that halates is the one figure not derived and is labelled as such in the source; it depends on phosphor isotropy, the aluminium backing and glass coatings, and 0.15 read as too much glow before it was left at 0.07.

Halation is light taken from the core, not added to it, so the composite is (1-f)*core + f*halo and the brightness gain is raised to hold the peak. That correction means peak-at-full-white and total-light-conserved cannot both hold as f varies, and the test that shipped with the CPU version asserted both. Corrected: it now pins where the light goes and where the peak sits, with a control at f = 0.

Off in the CPU rasterizer because compositing a full-frame blur is O(pixels) and measured four to five times the beam sweep: Asteroids went from 2.7 to 13.5 ms per frame against 0.4 ms to emulate the machine. Benching Tempest alone hid it, since at 580x570 it has a third of the pixels and was hit a third as hard; pjl spotted that and said to try Asteroids, which is the finding. The GPU does the same blur for nothing, so the frontend has it and the path serving screenshots and the debug panel does not. The CPU implementation stays because it is the only one the physics tests can run against.

title: Stage 5: vector settings, per-machine overrides and presets
description:
A VectorSettings block in config.toml with per-machine overrides in state.toml, resolving the same way scale and fullscreen already do, plus live sliders in settings_ui.rs so the knobs can be turned while a game runs.

Presets: "measured", everything derived from the tube figures in the epic; "flat", todays 1-pixel look kept so a regression can be compared against something; and a punchier preset for people who want it to look like a poster rather than like the cabinet.

The knobs are deviations from the measured model, and each should be labelled with what it is deviating from.
close_reason: Three knobs (brightness, focus, halation) in core::display since they are tube properties rather than vector ones, live on Shift+backtick, persisted diff-only against the resolved base. The issue's 'flat' preset deliberately omitted: it would preserve a bug rather than a baseline.

comments.author: pjl
comments.text:
Done across 852bdf3 (the panel) and 1401281 (persistence).

Three knobs, not the list the issue sketched. Two of them are controls a real monitor has on it, brightness and focus, and the third is halation, the one figure in the beam model with no derivation behind it and so the one most worth putting in a viewer hands. Each is documented as a deviation from what was measured, and 1.0 means the figure the tube gives rather than the middle of a slider.

The "flat" preset the issue asked for is not there and should not be. It was meant to keep todays 1-pixel look for comparison, and that look is gone: the beam now has a width taken from the tube, and a preset that pretended otherwise would be preserving a bug rather than a baseline. "Measured" and "Punchy" are what remain.

pjl steered the shape: these are properties of the tube and not of the vector generator, since a raster CRT has a brightness control, a focus control and a faceplate that halates in exactly the same way. So DisplaySettings lives in core::display rather than beside the vector code, and raster-only knobs (scanline depth, shadow mask) belong there beside them rather than in a parallel set.

The settings are process-wide, which is what they are: one viewer, one screen. But the renderers take them as an argument and the global is read at the edge, where a board hands the rasterizer its arguments, so the renderers stay pure functions and the rasterizer tests hand over their own settings rather than racing whatever a viewer has set.

Persistence resolves like everything else in the frontend: measured, then config.toml, then the game own entry in state.toml, diff-only against what it was resolved from. Recording against the resolved base rather than against the measured figures matters: otherwise a game agreeing with the global preference silently copies it and stops tracking later changes to it.

Found while testing, and not mine: on a vector machine the GL path draws straight to the window and falls back to the CPU framebuffer when a side panel needs a texture to lay out against, but that check listed three of the panel flags by hand. The DIP panel, the key legend and the Rhai console all resized the window on Tempest, Quantum, Star Wars and Asteroids and then never drew, so backtick had never done anything on any of them. Both the render branch and panels_width now ask one any_panel_open. pjl found it by pressing the key.

Not verified by eye: the sliders drive both renderers but only the CPU one can be rendered headlessly.

title: Quantum draws one 45000-line garbage frame at the attract-to-play transition
description:
Reported from a live run: coin in around frame 355, then start, and the screen shows artifacts for a moment. MAME does not do this.

Measured with a throwaway harness probe reading vector_display_list once per frame on a booted quantum (coin1 pressed at frame 355, p1_start at 400), center taken as 300,450 for the 600x900 display:

  frame 400: lines=217  worst=424px  cntr_points=8
  frame 401: lines=227  worst=424px  cntr_points=8
  frame 402: lines=217  worst=424px  cntr_points=8
  frame 403: lines=45455 worst=33218px cntr_points=0     <- the artifact
  frame 404: lines=401  worst=698px  cntr_points=9
  frame 405: lines=401  worst=698px  cntr_points=9

Attract alone is clean: 3000 frames, worst excursion 424 px, zero lines off screen. So this is one single frame, exactly at the transition, and not a gradual drift.

The three numbers on frame 403 say what happened. cntr_points=0 means the run contained no CNTR at all, where every normal frame has 8 or 9. 45455 lines is the MAX_STATES = 500000 cutoff in Avg::execute divided by the ~11 sequencer states a VCTR costs, so the generator ran to the cutoff and never found a frame delimiter. 33218 px is the largest distance any endpoint can be from the center once the 16.16 beam position has wrapped i32 completely (32768 + 450), so the beam ran away for the whole 45455 instructions.

Mechanism: QuantumBoard::trigger_avg copies the whole vector RAM region and runs Avg::execute to completion, synchronously, at the GO write. If the 68000 triggers the generator while it is part way through rewriting the vector list, the snapshot has no terminating JMP to 0 and no HALT, so we chase whatever bytes are there until the cutoff. The real hardware and MAME do not have this failure mode because the generator runs in emulated time and the CPU finishes writing the list underneath it. See the comment at avgdvg.cpp:568-584, which is specifically about Tempest and Quantum keeping the AVG in an endless loop while the CPU updates vector RAM.

trigger_avg also discards Avg::execute's return value, so a run that hit the cutoff without ever reaching a frame delimiter is published as if it were a finished frame.

Two ways to go, and the choice is a contract decision, not an implementation detail:

1. Do not publish a run that hit the cutoff. Avg::execute would have to distinguish 'hit MAX_STATES' from 'halted' and 'branched to zero', and trigger_avg would keep the previous display list for that frame. Small and it removes the artifact, but it is a guard over a missing mechanism, not the mechanism.

2. Run the generator incrementally in emulated time, so vector RAM writes land between states the way they do on hardware. Structurally right, and it is what MAME does, but it changes the AVG's contract and touches tempest and starwars as well.

Not started. Filed from the same session as phosphor-emulator-n7fi, which fixed the i32 overflow in the beam flip that this runaway used to trip: with that fixed the emulator no longer panics here, it draws the garbage instead.
close_reason: Generator now runs incrementally in emulated time against live vector memory (Avg::step + VectorMemory). Frame 403 of the repro goes from 45455 lines and 33218 px to 217 and 424 px. Costs 11% emulation time on tempest; golden frames recaptured for all three vector machines and reviewed.

comments.author: pjl
comments.text:
Fixed by option 2: the generator now runs incrementally in emulated time, against vector memory it reads live.

What the source said. MAME's run_state_machine (avgdvg.cpp:1219) clocks the sequencer in slices of emulated time and reschedules itself by the cycles each slice spent, with update_databus reading the memory space every state. go_w restarts it and clears the halt; nothing runs the list to completion at the GO write. The comment at avg_common_strobe2 (avgdvg.cpp:568) is explicit that for Tempest and Quantum the CPU updates vector RAM while the generator is running and the hardware arranges that the two do not collide. Our trigger_avg copied the region and ran the whole list synchronously, which is the one thing that model cannot represent.

What changed:

- Avg::step(cycles, mem, color_ram) advances the sequencer by a slice of master-clock time and returns true when a pass over the list finishes. Both list styles end a pass: a branch to address 0 (Tempest, Quantum, which then carry straight on into the next pass) and the HALT that ends Star Wars' list.
- VectorMemory borrows the board's regions (RAM low, vector ROM at a base) instead of taking a snapshot, so writes land between states.
- A new  counter carries beam debt: a state charges 8 cycles plus strobe3's beam time, and a long vector costs more than one slice, so pending goes negative and the generator stays busy across the following slices. That is also what makes VG_HALT time itself, so Star Wars' avg_busy_cycles countdown is gone; IN1 bit 6 now reads the generator directly.
- The clock ratios are the crystal divider, not fitted: all three boards run one 12.096 MHz crystal, quantum's 68000 at master/2 (2 AVG cycles per CPU cycle), tempest's 6502 and starwars' 6809E at master/8 (8 per CPU cycle).
- MAX_STATES is gone from the running path. It is only the test driver's cutoff now, because a slice of time buys a bounded number of states however the list is shaped.
- The AVG save state now carries the mid-instruction latches (op, data, dvx, dvy, dvy12, int_latch, timer) plus pending and elapsed. A snapshot used to be impossible to take mid-pass; now it lands mid-instruction as often as not, and without those the instruction in flight would finish with operands from whatever ran before the load.

Measured, same probe as the report, coin at 355 and start at 400:

  before  frame 403: lines=45455  worst=33218px  cntr_points=0
  after   frame 403: lines=217    worst=424px

Frame 403 is now indistinguishable from its neighbours. Over 600 frames the worst excursion is 424 px on a 600x900 screen and the biggest list is 984 lines. Play still progresses normally: 72 lines in attract, 217 after the coin, 983 in play.

Checked the thing that worried me most, that the generator might no longer get through a pass per video frame. It does. Quantum costs 81448 cycles per pass against a 201600-cycle video frame (2.5 passes per frame); tempest costs 179976 against the same budget (1.1 passes per frame). Both measured by instrumenting elapsed at the pass boundary, since a pass that took several frames would have shown up as a visibly stuttering display.

Cost, stated out loud: tempest emulation went from 1.277 to 1.423 ms/frame, about 11 percent more emulation time (12.58x to 11.36x realtime), from stepping the generator every CPU cycle. phosphor-bench, release, fastest of N. Worth it for a correctness fix on a machine still running 11x realtime, but it is a real regression and someone chasing throughput later should know where it came from.

Golden frames recaptured for all three vector machines, and I looked at every one. Quantum is the same attract screen with the animated particles a pixel or two along. Star Wars is the same flight-instructions screen at a different point in its starfield animation. Tempest changed to a different attract level entirely, which pjl confirmed is expected: the timing change moves the RNG seed, which picks the level the attract demo plays.

What I did NOT do:

- The AVG's partial display list is not saved. A snapshot taken mid-pass restores with an empty one, so the first pass published after a load is only the part drawn after the load point, one frame before it is whole again. This is consistent with what was already there (every board clears its published display_list on load and never saves it), and the save-state test's contract is that two restores agree with each other, which still holds. Saving it would cost up to about 40 KB per snapshot, which is the rewind epic's business, so I left it and am recording it here instead.
- Quantum's SVEC handling is a divergence I noticed while reading and did not touch. timer_countdown treats op1 as a short vector for every variant, but MAME's quantum handler_7 has no SVEC branch and always counts 0x4000 - timer. Ours would draw such a vector 64x short. I did not establish whether quantum's lists use opcode 2 at all, so I left it alone rather than change what a machine draws on a hunch. Worth its own issue if someone can show the opcode in a real list.

title: Galaga 54XX discrete explosion sound
description:
Model the Namco 54XX (MB8844) explosion-sound generator and its discrete analog output so Galaga's shooting/explosion effects are audible. Currently the 54XX is stubbed: commands sent via 06XX chip-select 3 are discarded at machines/src/namco_galaga.rs:771 and explosions are silent; only the WSG melodic/effect voices play.

Scope (this issue builds the SHARED 54XX component that Xevious also needs):

- Convert the 54XX's ~3-bit output through the discrete DAC + op-amp filter network (MAME galaga.c/bosco audio: bosco_54xx_dac R-1 ladder + op-amp filters) into a 44.1 kHz signal. Build on core/src/device/discrete/ (see docs/designs/discrete-sound-framework.md) rather than hard-coding samples.

title: Design doc, skeleton ROM and harness: prove the loader on a 68000 board
description:
Prove the Williams loading mechanism carries to a 68000 board on AddressSpace32,
and get a program to run and say so. Nothing about video yet.

THIS IS THE STEP WITH THE REAL UNKNOWN IN IT. Everything the Williams harness
does rests on properties of AddressSpace16 and an M6809. The 32-bit half was
checked statically during the survey (AddressSpace32::debug_poke ignores
AccessKind exactly as the 16-bit space does, address_space32.rs:466) but has
never been run. Until a program actually executes out of poked ROM on a bare
Road Runner, the rest of the epic is speculation.

WHAT TO BUILD.

1. docs/designs/roadrunner-video-conformance.md, following the Williams doc's
   shape: context, mechanism, board facts with their source lines, the result
   block, the risks. Write it before the code, and let the measurements correct
   it in place rather than rewriting history, which is what made the Williams doc
   worth reading.

2. machines/tests/roms/roadrunner_video.asm, assembled by asl to
   roadrunner_video.bin, both committed. `cpu 68000`, org 0, with the reset SSP
   and PC as the first two longwords so cpu.reset picks them up through the bus.

3. The program: set up a stack in work RAM, strobe the watchdog, write a phase
   index and finally a magic byte into a result block in work RAM, and halt in a
   loop that keeps strobing.

4. machines/tests/roadrunner_video_timing_test.rs: build with create_bare, poke
   the image at 0x000000 through BusDebug::write, reset, run frames, read the
   result block back through the debug bus. ROM-less, so it runs in CI.

5. The re-assembly drift guard, with the PHOSPHOR_ASM trap the Williams one
   needed. That guard reported green for its entire life on Williams because no
   assembler was on PATH anywhere; it must fail when PHOSPHOR_ASM says an
   assembler should be there, and that failure mode has to be demonstrated once
   rather than assumed.

THE WATCHDOG IS THE THING THAT WILL BREAK THIS FIRST. RoadRunnerSystem::run_frame
resets the machine after 8 frames without a write to 880001
(roadrunner.rs:771-775). A program that does not strobe it reboots, so every
phase reads 0 and the failure looks like "the image never ran" rather than "the
image ran and was rebooted". Strobe it from the outset, and when the first run
inevitably reads zeros, check that before suspecting the loader.

ACCEPTANCE. A ROM-less roadrunner reaches the final phase and writes its magic
byte, the harness reads both back, and a deliberately corrupted image fails the
drift guard. No video assertion in this issue.

WHAT TO WATCH FOR, given this is the first 68000 board in the programme:
- Byte writes on a word bus become read-modify-write (the module doc's own
  warning at atari_system1.rs:39-43), so the result block is easier to define as
  words than as bytes.
- Work RAM at 400000-401FFF is where both the stack and the result block go;
  unlike Williams there is no undisplayed video RAM to hide them in, and there
  is plenty of room, so no cleverness is needed.
- Do not touch 080000-087FFF. The slapstic state machine advances on any data
  access to it and will not fault, it will just quietly change banks.
close_reason: Design doc, skeleton ROM, harness and drift guard landed; six assertions green with no arcade ROMs. The loader carries to AddressSpace32 and the 68000 unchanged. Each guard was made to fail once; the image checksum's zero fill could not fail and was changed to 0xA5.

comments.author: pjl
comments.text:
Landed. The loader carries to a 68000 board on AddressSpace32 unchanged, and nothing about the 32-bit half needed a new mechanism.

WHAT THE SOURCE SAID. AddressSpace32::debug_poke (address_space32.rs:466) ignores AccessKind exactly as the 16-bit space does, and ReadOnly regions are allocated backing (:124). The BusDebug derive passes a 32-bit map its address untruncated (macros/src/lib.rs:179). M68000::reset (m68000/mod.rs:456-461) fetches the SSP from 0 and the PC from 4 through the bus, so both come from the poked image. All four held on the first run.

WHAT WAS MEASURED, on a ROM-less roadrunner built with create_bare:
  R_MAGIC   $5A5A       program completed
  R_PHASE   5
  R_TRAP    $0000       no stray exception
  R_SSP     $00401F00   vector 0, as cpu.reset handed it over
  R_CKSUM   $472D       the CPU's own sum of all 8 KB, read back through the
                        real bus, equal to the harness's sum over the .bin
  R_VBCOUNT 16          vblank edges ridden, twice the watchdog timeout
  frames    exactly 16

THE WATCHDOG. Predicted to break this first, and it does exactly what the issue
said it would. Deleting the PetDog call from the vblank loop and rebuilding:
R_VBCOUNT reads 8, R_PHASE reads 3, the magic word is absent and the run burns
all 32 frames. The counters restart rather than stall, because entry clears the
result block deliberately; without that clear a reboot would leave a plausible
half-finished block behind. That mutation was run and watched to fail.

THE GUARD THAT COULD NOT FAIL, AND WAS FIXED RATHER THAN KEPT. The image
checksum was written with p2bin -l 0x00. A ROM-less board's program ROM is
already zero, so the checksum was blind over the 85% of the image that is
padding: poking only the first 4 KB passed. The fill byte is now 0xA5 and the
same mutation fails (7981 against 18221). $A5A5 is also line-A, so a program
counter that wanders into the padding vectors to the stray handler instead of
grinding through 3.5 KB of ORI.B #0,D0.

The other two guards were each made to fail once as well. Drift guard, with one
byte of the binary zeroed: 'first difference at $000406: built 0x1F, committed
0x00'. PHOSPHOR_ASM trap, run with PATH=/nonexistent: fails with PHOSPHOR_ASM=1
and skips with a printed note without it. Both branches executed.

WHAT I DID NOT DO. No video assertion of any kind, per the issue. The program
does not enable interrupts, never touches 080000-087FFF, and leaves the VBLANK
IRQ4 latch permanently asserted and masked, which is harmless at SR mask 7 and
is the first thing m0bu has to change.

Unrelated: tools/disasm movie_cli_test::movie_check_prints_a_frame_hash_comparable_with_frames_toml
failed once under the parallel workspace run and passes alone. Pre-existing
flake, not touched here.

title: Concrete bus dispatch: Quantum and Star Wars
description:
The two standalone machines left over from hv5p (the Atari DVG/AVG family). Neither uses AtariDvgBoard, so neither fits the board-plus-view shape the other three took; both need their own split.

Quantum (machines/src/quantum.rs, ~1200 lines): M68000 + AVG + 2x POKEY, all in one QuantumSystem struct with 'impl Bus for QuantumSystem' and two 'bus_split!(self, bus: u32 word)' sites. Its Bus impl touches ~10 fields (map, avg, pokey, nvram, color_ram, track_x/y, system_input, irq_pending, watchdog_count) plus helper methods (trigger_avg, led_w), so a per-field view would be wide. Prefer nesting the bus state into a QuantumBus field (the shape the design doc calls out for standalone machines) over a 10-borrow view.

Star Wars (machines/src/starwars.rs, ~2700 lines): two 6502s (main + sound) on its own StarWarsBoard, AVG, POKEY/RIOT/TMS5220, ADC0809 yoke, X2212 NVRAM. Seven bus_split! sites. Note debug_pre_tick services a pending sound-CPU reset and explicitly needs a bus for the reset-vector fetch -- with the generic Cpu::reset (bek7) that becomes straightforward, and the comment there about run_frame being 'where bus_split! yields a bus' should be updated.

Both are M6502/M68000, so both depend on bek7 (done). Follow the conventions in docs/designs/concrete-bus-dispatch.md: machines expose step_cycle/bus_read/bus_write, board-level device-index tests move up to the machine, and measure with phosphor-bench before and after (asteroids/tempest are the nearest comparables at 1.5 MHz).

Split out of hv5p, which converted Asteroids, Asteroids Deluxe and Lunar Lander in 6cfbd9b.
close_reason:
Done in 422ca0f (quantum + starwars/esb).

Numbers (phosphor-bench, release, 400f x 5 reps, best of 6 alternating runs, idle host):
  quantum  1.413 -> 1.145 ms/f  -19.0%
  starwars 3.968 -> 3.448       -13.1%
Quantum is the largest single gain of the rollout so far: a 68000 whose frame is almost entirely CPU cycles, previously dispatching every *word* access through a trait object. It is also the first user of the u32/u16 wide bus to convert -- and nothing about the conversion was width-specific, exactly as the design doc predicted the bus_split! arms would turn out.

Shapes:
- Quantum had no board at all (CPU, map, AVG, POKEYs, NVRAM, I/O in one struct). Introduced QuantumBoard for the bus state, leaving QuantumSystem { cpu, board }; the Bus impl moved to the board unchanged. ~120 field references rewritten to self.board.*, which is the churn the design doc warns standalone machines carry.
- Star Wars kept its board and moved both 6809s up. The board already carried the variant differences (Empire's slapstic window and bank), so it implements Bus and IS the bus for both registered machines.

Nice side effect: the deferred sound-CPU reset (E0) stops being awkward. It existed as a deferred flag because the reset fetches a vector through the bus, which only run_frame could produce via bus_split!, with debug_pre_tick mirroring it for the cycle-stepped paths. With the CPU beside the bus it is a plain call, and both paths now route through one function.

The ROM-gated boot check earned its keep: Star Wars' hand-written MachineDebug::debug_bus still returned the board, which no longer owns the CPUs, so Empire failed with 'exposes no CPUs through its debug bus'. Golden frames could not have caught it -- the picture is identical either way. Worth remembering for the remaining conversions: any hand-written MachineDebug needs its debug_bus repointed at the machine.

Golden frames unchanged for all pinned machines; machine, harness and ROM-gated suites pass; clippy and fmt clean.

22 files still reference bus_split!, all in the 3hnp (Atari System 1 + Gottlieb) and 642d (standalone) buckets.

title: M6809: don't-care cycles outside indexed addressing still drive nothing
description:
ROOT CAUSE of phosphor-emulator-j63p (ESB watchdog reset).

The MC6809E drives $FFFF on its don't-care (/VMA) cycles. Ours drives
nothing at all. ESB's slapstic depends on that address, so the dependency is
not academic.

HOW IT BREAKS ESB. The $829B trampoline re-selects the CURRENT bank -- each
bank holds its own copy:
    bank 0 JMP $8080   bank 1 JMP $8090   bank 2 JMP $80A0   bank 3 JMP $80B0
and $9174 differs per bank:
    bank 0 BITA #$10   bank 1 STA 6,X     bank 2 RTS         bank 3 BHI $9176

MAME (0.287, gameplay, traced) executes bank 1's `$829B JMP $8090` and then
lands on bank 2's `$9174 RTS` -- so the bank changes 1 -> 2 between them
WITHOUT any access to $80A0. The only mechanism that can do that is the
chip's ALT sequence committing bank 2, and the callee's `LDX #$9B5E` /
`LDA 0,X` reads $9B5E, which is exactly the alt_select range
(test_in 0x1FFC/0x1B5C) with the low bits encoding bank 2.

Our alt sequence never completes. Traced with the new state instrumentation:
    41750126  $9E00 -> alt-valid    (alt_start matched)
    41750128  $9E01 -> active       (BROKEN at the valid step)
The valid step needs an access with (addr & 0x1FFF) == 0x1FFF from OUTSIDE
the window -- i.e. $FFFF, a don't-care cycle. We never drive it, so the
sequence always breaks, the game never gets bank 2 by the alt path, and the
return lands in bank 1 where $9174 is `STA 6,X` instead of `RTS`.

MAME's 6809 does drive it: m6809.h:217
    inline void dummy_vma(int count) { for(...) { read_opcode_arg(0xffff); } }
and its .lst uses dummy_vma at 17 sites. Note this is DISTINCT from
dummy_read_opcode_arg(0), which reads at PC -- I conflated the two earlier
and tested the PC variant, which correctly changed nothing.

Our own slapstic doc comment already predicted this: "the alt sequence's 2nd
(valid) access must land *outside* the window (in practice a 6809 dummy VMA
access)".

SCOPE OF THE FIX. Every don't-care cycle in the M6809 should drive $FFFF,
not just the indexed ones. A partial experiment adding it only to the
indexed internal cycle did NOT fix ESB, because the break happens at $9E00's
ASLA, whose internal cycle is a different path. So this needs doing across
the instruction set.

Note commit 9706bbc moved us AWAY from this: it replaced TST's three
`bus.read(0xFFFF)` don't-care cycles with internal cycles, on the reading
that the datasheet's "don't-care($FFFF)" meant no bus activity. It means the
opposite -- the address bus IS driven to $FFFF. That commit should be
revisited as part of this.

Cross-validation impact: bus traces will gain these accesses, so the m6809
vectors need regenerating, and the reference core (mame0148) may model them
differently from the modern one.
notes:
2026-08-09 — retitled; the original claim is now only partly true.

Fixed in c08770a, and it fixed phosphor-emulator-j63p: the indexed
postbyte-resolution don't-cares read at PC, and `alu_indexed`'s base internal
cycle drives $FFFF. No cycle counts changed — these were existing silent
cycles.

STILL OPEN, and worth keeping for two reasons rather than one:

1. Every other don't-care cycle in the instruction set is still silent —
   inherent-mode internal cycles, the direct/extended address-computation
   cycles, RMW, the interrupt entry sequence, RTS/PULS. Any address-snooping
   device sees a bus the hardware would not present. The slapstic games on
   Atari System 1 (Marble Madness 103, Road Runner 108) are the obvious
   exposure, and neither is verified against a reference in this respect.

2. Commit 9706bbc is probably a regression and should be revisited on its
   own merits. It replaced TST's three `bus.read(0xFFFF)` don't-care cycles
   with silent internal cycles, reasoning that the datasheet's
   "don't-care($FFFF)" meant no bus activity. The ESB result is direct
   evidence it means the opposite: the address bus IS driven to $FFFF, and
   the slapstic depends on it. That commit made one machine's fidelity worse
   to satisfy a reading the hardware contradicts.

No known game currently depends on the remainder, so P2 rather than higher —
but (2) is a wrong-direction change sitting in the tree, not merely absent
work.
close_reason:
Every don't-care cycle in the M6809 now drives an address, and 9706bbc's
direction is reversed.

The reference is MAME's m6809.lst/base6x09.lst, which distinguishes two kinds of
don't-care cycle where the datasheet's blanket 'don't-care($FFFF)' does not:
dummy_vma() holds $FFFF, dummy_read_opcode_arg() re-drives PC. The ESB result
already showed the blanket reading was too coarse, so where the two disagree the
per-cycle split wins.

WHAT NOW DRIVES THE BUS
- Direct and extended address computation -> $FFFF
- The RMW modify cycle -> PC (TST -> $FFFF)
- TST direct/indexed/extended final cycle -> $FFFF, reversing 9706bbc
- Inherent register ops (NEG/COM/INC/DEC/CLR/shifts/rotates, NOP, DAA, SEX,
  ABX, MUL) -> PC; inherent TSTA/TSTB -> $FFFF
- The trailing cycle of every 16-bit ALU op -> PC
- TFR/EXG, branches and long branches, JMP, LEA -> $FFFF
- BSR/LBSR/JSR: their don't-cares now all precede the two pushes, as on the part
- Interrupt/SWI entry: PC, PC, $FFFF, and the vector fetch bracketed by $FFFF.
  The cycle that detects the interrupt is the first of those PC cycles
- Indexed: the leading don't-cares re-drive PC and the rest hold $FFFF, per
  mode. D,R is the one mode with two, at PC+0 then PC+1

Pull sequences (RTS, RTI, PULS/PULU) close on a real read at the settled stack
pointer and pushes (PSHS/PSHU) open on a real read at the stack top; those are
memory accesses, not don't-cares, and were silent before.

CYCLE COUNTS ARE UNCHANGED. Every one of the 266,000 single-step vectors reports
the same total cycle count as before across all 266 opcodes — nothing was added
or removed, only given an address, and the four instructions whose cycles were
reordered (rmw_indexed, indexed 16-bit ALU, BSR/LBSR/JSR) kept their length.

VERIFIED
- 4,150 workspace tests pass (phosphor-disasm's test target does not build on
  main either; filed as phosphor-emulator-kd9b)
- Cross-validation 264,132/266,000, all 1,868 failures the known extended-
  indirect +3 divergence and nothing else; baseline was 264,090 on a different
  random draw
- ESB 4,000 frames: same PC, zero hangs, same 405/405 slapstic bank switches as
  the pre-change build, cycle for cycle
- starwars/joust/robotron/gridlee/irobot 1,200 frames each: PC and hang counts
  identical to the pre-change build
- core/tests/m6809_dont_care_cycle_test.rs, 18 new tests, asserts the whole bus
  trace of representative instructions so a cycle that moves relative to a real
  access fails too

FOLLOW-UPS FILED (both out of this issue's scope — neither is a silent cycle)
- phosphor-emulator-ks1q: CWAI and the CWAI-wake vector path are short of cycles
- phosphor-emulator-5dgc: indexed indirect emits its don't-cares after the
  pointer read instead of before

title: Walk's wobble rate is probably 10x too slow
description:
WALK_LFO_HZ is 1.16, derived by reading the SECOND resistor of MAME's
`DISCRETE_INVERTER_OSC(node, enab, mod, rC, rP, C, ...)` as the timing element:
43 kOhm x 10 uF -> ~1.16 Hz.

The FIRST resistor is the timing one; the second is the bias pull. On that
reading walk's oscillator is 4.3 kOhm x 10 uF -> ~11.6 Hz.

The same misreading hid jump's oscillator entirely: 3.3 MOhm x 3.3 uF gave
0.05 Hz, so it was dismissed as a DC offset and left out, and jump had no warble
at all until it was put back at ~8 Hz (commit 7128952).

Walk currently sounds better than it did but is not right, and this is the
obvious candidate. Left alone deliberately: walk was signed off at bb56d6e and
changing it needs a listen, not a metric — the spectral numbers barely move
because the wobble redistributes energy between footsteps rather than changing
the average.

VERIFY FIRST rather than just editing the constant: read the inverter-oscillator
implementation in MAME's disc_wav.hxx to confirm which resistor sets the rate,
since the same misreading has now cost two effects.
close_reason:
Fixed by 618d0de ("derive the Donkey Kong wobble rates from their parts, not a
stopwatch"). The issue's premise was confirmed: the FIRST resistor of
DISCRETE_INVERTER_OSC is the timing element, not the second.

WALK_LFO_R is now 4300 ohms (was read as the 43k bias pull), with WALK_LFO_R_BIAS
43k and WALK_LFO_C 10uF alongside it, and the rate is no longer stated as a
constant at all: it comes out of the parts. Measured at 84 ms relaxation period
against the board's 87 ms.

Confirmed audible, not just metric: against the board's two-level alternation
between 280 and 440 Hz, the old 1.16 Hz version gave a single smooth glide from
432 down to 262 and then stayed there, which reads as no wobble rather than a
slow one, because a footstep only lasts 160 ms. The same misreading had hidden
jump's oscillator entirely; both are now derived.

See machines/src/dkong_sound.rs:143-154 for the recorded reasoning.

Walk's remaining residual (150-400 Hz sitting light, the footstep sounding thin)
is tracked separately in phosphor-emulator-dkong-walk-not-sustained-4q42 and is
not this.

title: Epic: Williams video timing conformance ROM
description:
Design: docs/designs/williams-video-conformance.md

A synthetic M6809 program, written here rather than borrowed, that runs on a
ROM-less Williams gen-1 board and measures WHEN the machine draws. It is the
first test in the tree that lets the CPU and the beam run against each other,
and the first video test that can run in CI, because it needs no arcade ROMs.

WHY. Nothing in the repository tests video timing. boot_check_test asserts a
machine lights a pixel; golden_frame_test hashes an attract-loop frame and
cannot separate "we draw differently" from "the machine is in a different
state"; the ~211 render-adjacent unit tests all hand the renderer its state
directly. For Williams that gap is exactly where the bugs were: 3eb7ce1 and
8df2e35, two days apart, were both needed before Joust drew correctly.

STATUS AT FILING. The design doc, the ROM source, the assembled 12 KB image and
the harness all already exist in the working tree, untracked. The doc says the
ROM had not been assembled; that is now stale, it has been. The suite was run
against the current tree and the assumptions were validated rather than assumed.

WHAT WAS MEASURED (joust and robotron, ROM-less, machines/tests/williams_video_timing_test.rs):

- The program reaches phase 10 and writes its $5A magic on both machines. The
  whole loading mechanism works: debug_write ignores AccessKind, the patched
  reset vector is fetched through the bus, and a bare board needs no ROM set.
- T1 video counter: 64 transitions per frame, 1 wrap, max $FC, and the value 0
  dwelling about twice as long as the value 4, which is the u8 aliasing of
  scanlines 256-259 onto 0-3 showing up as a measurement.
- T2 count240 to ROM PIA CA1: exactly one interrupt per frame, handler observes
  counter $F0.
- T3 VA11 to CB1: rising at $20 $60 $A0 $E0, falling at $40 $80 $C0.
- T5 SC1 XOR-4 size bug: a 4x4 blit writes one byte.
- T6 mid-frame palette write splits the picture at the beam.
- T7, the load-bearing one: a VRAM write at line 120 shows on row 193 in the
  same frame and on row 53 only in the next.
- T4 slow blit FAILS: 16 scanlines measured, 32 expected. This is a real bug in
  the tree, and it was found by reading the code while designing the test.

THE CHECKS WERE PROVEN CAPABLE OF FAILING. begin_scanline was temporarily
mutated to also re-render every visible line at scanline 259, which is the
"whole frame at end of frame" model the design says T6 and T7 must reject. Both
picture tests failed under it and passed again when it was reverted. The
mutation is not in the tree.

ONE VACUOUS PASS FOUND AND NOT YET FIXED. the_committed_binary_matches_its_source
reports ok today only because no assembler is on PATH anywhere, including inside
the Nix dev shell. It is the canonical skip-and-report-green defect and the first
child issue deals with it.

DECISIONS TAKEN AT FILING TIME.

- Assembler: nixpkgs has no lwtools attribute. Rather than carry a custom
  derivation, port the source to asl (packaged, 142-bld232, 6809 capable) plus
  p2bin. The port is verifiable by byte-comparing its output against the
  existing lwasm-built image, which cross-checks both assemblers.
- Slow blit: charge the second cycle inside the device, so all blit timing stays
  in williams_blitter.rs.
- Scope: instrument and fix in one epic, including the golden-frame recapture
  the fix will probably force on joust, robotron and sinistar.

NOT COVERED. Sprite and tile decode, palette derivation, orientation, and
anything about whether Joust's artwork is right; those belong to the golden
frames. Nothing about the sound CPU. Sinistar needs a second link address
($E000, 8 KB, plus the $D000 SRAM) and is deferred to its own issue.

RISK CARRIED FORWARD. Every expected value is derived from our own source, so
the suite is a regression guard immediately and a correctness guard only once
each figure has been checked against the schematic. The counter aliasing and the
scanline-256 guard are the two that are still only "what we do today", and the
design doc names them as such.
close_reason: Delivered: ten assertions on joust, robotron and sinistar, ROM-less and in CI. Found and fixed the discarded slow-blit cycle cost. Every check was falsified on purpose before being trusted. Three design errors and one unanticipated cabinet rotation recorded in the doc.

comments.author: pjl
comments.text:
Validation run of the untracked working tree, 2026-08-25, against e5bed15.

WHAT WAS CHECKED IN THE SOURCE, before anything was run. Every board fact the
design doc derives its expectations from was read and confirmed, with one
correction: the doc's line references are stale by roughly seventeen lines
because the ClockTree commits moved them. Confirmed live: TIMING is 260 lines of
64 cycles at 1 MHz (williams.rs:59); current_scanline casts to u8 and $CB00
returns it masked with $FC (:593, :1000); begin_scanline renders line N before
the CPU runs line N, drives CB1 from scanline bit 5 and CA1 from scanline >= 240,
and skips CB1 on scanline 256 (:648); only the ROM PIA's IRQ lines reach the main
CPU (:1137); the watchdog counter increments and nothing ever acts on it; program
ROM is a backed ReadOnly region at $D000 for 12 KB (:473) and debug_write ignores
AccessKind (address_space16.rs:509) with backing allocated for ReadOnly (:389).
The PIA control-register semantics the ROM relies on are as it assumes: bit 2
selects the data register, bit 1 selects the active edge, bit 0 enables the
interrupt, and reading a data port clears both flags for that side.

One thing the design doc does not state that matters for reading the ROM: in the
blitter the width register counts COLUMNS and the height register counts
SCANLINES. Within a row the address advances by dxadv, 256 with DST_STRIDE_256,
and the row advance is the +1 within the page. That is why the screen fill's
146 x 85 covers columns 3 to 148 and scanlines 0 to 84.

THE RUN. cargo test -p phosphor-machines --test williams_video_timing_test,
0.06s, no arcade ROMs, joust and robotron.

  8 passed, 2 failed.

Passing: the program reaches phase 10 and writes its magic on both machines;
T1 counter survey (64 transitions, 1 wrap, max $FC, value 0 dwelling about twice
as long as value 4); T2 count240 (one IRQ per frame at $F0); T3 VA11 (rising
$20 $60 $A0 $E0, falling $40 $80 $C0); T5 SC1 XOR-4; T6 palette split; and the
12 KB image shape.

Failing, both real:

1. T4 slow blit measured a 16-scanline halt where 32 is derived. This is the bug
   the design predicted from reading williams.rs:333, and it is now measured
   rather than predicted. Filed as itvk.4.
2. "no frame captured at phase 9". Not an assertion about pixels: the ROM
   publishes phase 9 and then falls straight into Done, publishing phase 10 and
   the magic in the same frame, so the harness never sees phase 9 after a
   run_frame. Filed as itvk.2.

T7 THEN PASSED. With the capture condition widened so the idle frame is taken
when the phase reads 10, a_mid_frame_vram_write_only_affects_rows_the_beam_has_not_reached
passes on both machines: the write at line 120 shows on screen row 193 in the
same frame and on row 53 only in the next. That is the load-bearing claim of the
whole design and it holds.

THE CHECKS WERE PROVEN ABLE TO FAIL. begin_scanline was temporarily given an
extra pass that re-renders every visible line at scanline 259, which is the
"whole frame at end of frame" model the design says T6 and T7 must reject. Both
picture tests failed under it. The six CPU-observable tests still passed, which
is the correct pattern for a rendering-only mutation. The mutation was reverted
and the tree confirmed clean.

A VACUOUS PASS FOUND. the_committed_binary_matches_its_source reports ok, and
reports ok only because no assembler exists on PATH anywhere, including inside
nix develop. nixpkgs has no lwtools attribute at all. Filed as itvk.1, with asl
chosen over a custom lwtools derivation.

WHAT WAS NOT DONE. Nothing was committed and no source file was left modified.
Sinistar was not attempted. No expectation was checked against a schematic; every
figure in the suite still derives from our own source, so the suite is a
regression guard today and a correctness guard only after that check.

comments.author: pjl
comments.text:
Delivered. Ten assertions on three machines, no arcade ROMs, 0.12s, running in
CI, which no video test in this tree had ever done.

WHAT IT PINS. The video counter's step, wrap and u8 aliasing; count240 reaching
the ROM PIA's CA1 once a frame at scanline 240; VA11 reaching CB1 at every
32-line boundary, rising and falling; the blitter's halt cost in both speeds; the
SC1 XOR-4 size bug; a mid-frame palette write splitting the picture at the beam;
and a mid-frame VRAM write showing only on the rows the beam has not reached.

WHAT IT FOUND. One real bug, predicted from reading the source before the ROM
ever ran: williams.rs discarded the cycle cost do_dma_cycle returns, so CTRL_SLOW
cost the CPU nothing and every RAM-to-RAM blit ran at twice hardware speed. The
device was right and the board was right; the join was wrong, which is the shape
a device unit test cannot reach, because the accumulator it tests with is the
very return value the board threw away. Fixed device-side in 0e796ed; Robotron
and Sinistar drew a different attract frame and were recaptured after review.

EVERY CHECK WAS MADE TO FAIL ON PURPOSE BEFORE BEING TRUSTED.
- T6 and T7: begin_scanline was temporarily given a second pass re-rendering
  every visible line at scanline 259, the whole-frame-at-end-of-frame model the
  design says they must reject. Both failed; the six CPU-observable tests still
  passed, which is the right pattern for a rendering-only mutation.
- The drift guard: one byte of the committed image changed, and PHOSPHOR_ASM set
  with an empty PATH. It had reported green for its entire life because lwasm was
  on PATH nowhere.
- The Sinistar rotation: it is what failed before the handling existed.

THREE THINGS THE DESIGN GOT WRONG, all recorded in the doc rather than quietly
rewritten:
- Phase 9 and phase 10 were published in the same frame, so capture C could never
  be taken. The wedge guard reported it honestly as a missing capture rather than
  passing with two of three.
- The doc never stated that the blitter's width counts columns and height counts
  scanlines, which is the fact a reader needs to check the screen fill.
- Its williams.rs line references were stale by about seventeen lines.

And one it did not see coming at all: Sinistar's 270-degree cabinet rotation,
which broke the picture tests in opposite directions and had nothing to do with
the memory map the issue was written about.

TOOLCHAIN. asl and p2bin rather than lwtools, which nixpkgs does not carry. The
port was verified byte-identical to the original lwasm image, which cross-checks
two independent assemblers over the same source, and asl covers 6502, Z80 and
68000 too, so a conformance ROM for a second board needs no new assembler.

WHAT REMAINS OPEN is the programme epic above this one
(phosphor-emulator-conformance-rom-programme-hl4t) and its first question:
whether any other board exposes enough of the beam to host a self-synchronising
ROM at all. Williams was chosen first because it is the exception, and a first
look is not encouraging.

title: Port williams_video.asm to asl and make the drift guard fail when it should
description:
Put a 6809 assembler in the dev shell and make the drift guard a real check.

THE PROBLEM. machines/tests/williams_video_timing_test.rs has a test called
the_committed_binary_matches_its_source that re-assembles the ROM source and
byte-compares it against the committed image. It reports ok today. It reports ok
because `lwasm` is on PATH nowhere: not on the host, and not inside `nix develop`
either (checked both). The test is a validator that skips and reports green,
which is the defect pattern CLAUDE.md and the working rules single out, and it is
guarding the one artifact in this epic that a human cannot review by reading.

WHY NOT LWTOOLS. The design doc assumed `lwtools` was a package away. It is not:
nixpkgs has no such attribute (nix eval reports the nearest names as bftools,
cctools, dtools, e2tools, fdtools). Shipping it would mean a custom mkDerivation
with an upstream tarball URL and hash to maintain in flake.nix.

THE ROUTE CHOSEN. `asl` is packaged (142-bld232) and assembles 6809. Port
machines/tests/roms/williams_video.asm to asl syntax, add `asl` to the flake's
buildInputs, and produce the raw image with p2bin.

THE ACCEPTANCE CHECK, WHICH IS THE POINT. The current williams_video.bin was
produced by lwasm and is known good: the harness runs it to completion on joust
and robotron and eight of ten assertions pass against it. So the port is
accepted only when asl's output is byte-identical to the committed lwasm image.
That is a cross-check of two independent assemblers over the same source
semantics, and it means the port cannot quietly change the program. If a byte
differs, find out which directive disagrees before touching the .bin.

Directives in the source that will need attention: equ, fdb, org, setdp, zmb
(zero-fill to the vector table), and the pshs/puls register lists. The zmb at
the end is load-bearing: it is what makes `-f raw` emit one flat $D000-$FFFF
image instead of concatenating sections and dropping the gap, and the harness
test the_image_fills_the_program_rom_window pins that (12 KB, reset vector at the
top reading $D000).

MAKE THE GUARD ABLE TO FAIL. A plain "skip if the assembler is missing" is the
same vacuous pass in a new coat. Have the dev shell export a marker
(PHOSPHOR_ASM=1 or similar) and have the test hard-fail when the marker is set
and the assembler is absent, skipping only when it is not. CI has no Nix shell
and no assembler, so it still skips there, but nobody inside the dev shell can
edit the source and ship a stale binary. Before closing, break it once on
purpose: change one byte of the .bin, watch the test fail, put it back.

Also delete or rewrite the doc comment in the harness that names lwasm, and the
Assemble: line at the top of the .asm.
close_reason: asl and p2bin in the dev shell (4d3c773); source ported and verified byte-identical to the lwasm image (sha256 296f9527...); drift guard made to fail three ways on purpose, including the PHOSPHOR_ASM case that turns a missing assembler into a failure instead of a skip.

comments.author: pjl
comments.text:
Done. asl and p2bin are in the dev shell (commit 4d3c773), the source is ported,
and the guard has been made to fail three different ways on purpose.

THE PORT WAS BYTE-IDENTICAL, WHICH IS THE RESULT WORTH RECORDING. Assembling the
ported source with asl and converting with p2bin reproduces the lwasm-built
image exactly: sha256 296f95270810cf3065e582c17037a080f730a570edeb7a8271e21b4de053bcc7
from both toolchains, cmp reports no differing byte. Two independent assemblers
agreeing over the same program is a stronger statement about the binary than
either one alone, and it means the port changed nothing about what the ROM does.

WHAT THE PORT ACTUALLY NEEDED, which was less than expected:

- `cpu 6809` at the top, which asl requires and lwasm infers.
- `setdp $00` becomes `assume dpr:$00`.
- `zmb $FFF0-*` is gone. asl does not have it, and it is not needed: `org $FFF0`
  leaves a gap between the two segments and p2bin's `-r 0xD000-0xFFFF -l 0x00`
  is what turns them into one flat 12 KB image. Getting that wrong produces a
  short file rather than a wrong one, and the_image_fills_the_program_rom_window
  already pins the length and the reset vector.
- Nothing else. equ, org, fcb, fdb, the `<` forced-direct prefix and the
  pshs/puls register lists all read the same to both assemblers. The `<`
  prefixes mattered: every direct-page access in the source carries one and
  every other access is outside page zero, so there was no addressing mode for
  the two assemblers to disagree about.

Assemble with:
  asl -q -o williams_video.p williams_video.asm
  p2bin williams_video.p williams_video.bin -r 0xD000-0xFFFF -l 0x00

THE GUARD NOW FAILS WHEN IT SHOULD. Before this it was the canonical
skip-and-report-green defect: `lwasm` was on PATH nowhere, so the test ran
nothing and reported ok. Three runs, each checked by hand:

1. One byte of the committed image changed from $02 to $00 at offset 100. The
   test failed and named it: "first difference at $D064: built 0x02, committed
   0x00", plus the rebuild commands. Restored, hash back to 296f9527.
2. PHOSPHOR_ASM=1 with an empty PATH. The test FAILED rather than skipping:
   "PHOSPHOR_ASM is set, so `asl` is supposed to be on PATH here, but running it
   failed". This is the case that matters, because it is the one that was
   silently true for the whole life of the file.
3. PHOSPHOR_ASM unset with an empty PATH. Skipped with a printed note and passed,
   which is the CI path and is deliberate: CI has no Nix shell and no assembler.

The marker is exported from the flake's shellHook, so anyone inside the dev
shell gets the real check without opting in, and nobody has to remember a flag.

ALSO FIXED, since clippy runs over this target: an unused BusDebug import and a
needless-parens lint in the harness. CI's exact clippy line and cargo fmt are
clean over the workspace.

NOT COMMITTED HERE. The ported .asm, the binary and the harness are still
untracked; they land together in itvk.3. Only the flake change is committed, so
PHOSPHOR_ASM is currently read by nothing in the tree.

title: ROM publishes phase 9 and 10 in one frame, so capture C is never taken
description:
The ROM publishes phase 9 and phase 10 in the same frame, so the idle frame
cannot be captured.

MEASURED. Running the harness as written fails with "joust: no frame captured at
phase 9", not on any assertion about pixels. The phase protocol says a picture
phase is published at WaitLine $F0 (line 240) of the frame it describes, so the
harness sees it after the run_frame that produced that picture. Phase 9 is
published that way, but the program then falls straight through into Done, which
writes phase 10 and the $5A magic immediately, still at line 240 of the same
frame. By the time run_frame returns, the phase byte reads 10 and the harness
has skipped its capture C slot.

Note what did NOT happen: the suite did not pass with two of three captures. The
capture slot was missing and the test said so. The wedge guard worked.

THE FIX. In the ROM, after storing phase 9, do a WaitWrap and a WaitLine $F0
before Done publishes phase 10 and the magic. That costs one frame and keeps the
protocol honest: every phase is observable at the end of the frame it labels.
MAX_FRAMES is 64 and the program uses far fewer, so there is room.

THEN RESTORE THE HARNESS. The working copy currently widens the capture
condition to `phase >= 7` with the slot clamped to 2, which is what proved T7
passes (see the T7 issue). Once the ROM holds phase 9 for a frame, put it back
to the strict `(7..=9)` form. Leaving the clamp in place would let a future ROM
that skips the idle frame entirely still fill slot 2.

Depends on the assembler issue: the ROM cannot be rebuilt until the dev shell
can assemble it.
close_reason: Done now waits a full frame before publishing phase 10 and the magic, so phase 9 is observable at the end of the idle frame. Harness restored to the strict (7..=9) capture. 9 of 10 pass; only the slow-blit assertion (itvk.4) remains.

comments.author: pjl
comments.text:
Fixed in the ROM, and the harness is back to the strict capture condition.

WHAT WAS WRONG. Every picture phase is published at WaitLine $F0 of the frame it
describes, and the harness reads the phase byte once per run_frame(). So a phase
is only observable if it is the LAST one written in its frame. Phase 9 was not:
the program stored 9 and fell straight through into Done, which stored 10 and
the magic byte immediately, still at line 240 of the same frame. By the time
run_frame() returned the phase read 10, the harness skipped its capture C slot,
and the T7 test failed with "no frame captured at phase 9" rather than with
anything about pixels.

THE FIX. Done now does WaitWrap and WaitLine $F0 before publishing phase 10 and
the magic, so phase 9 stands for the whole idle frame. The program costs one
extra frame, against a MAX_FRAMES of 64 it does not come close to using.

The wait has to be both halves. WaitWrap alone returns during scanlines 256-259,
which are still inside the same frame, so phase 10 would still land before
run_frame() returned. The WaitLine $F0 is what carries it into the next frame.

The harness capture condition is back to the strict `(7..=9)` form. The clamped
`phase >= 7` version that was used to prove T7 passes is gone: it would let a
future ROM that skips the idle frame entirely still fill slot 2.

MEASURED AFTER. 9 of 10 pass on joust and robotron, including
a_mid_frame_vram_write_only_affects_rows_the_beam_has_not_reached with the
strict capture. The one failure left is the slow-blit assertion, which is itvk.4.

The rebuilt image is 734 bytes of code against 726 before, which is exactly the
eight bytes added: jsr (3) + ldb immediate (2) + jsr (3). The drift guard passes
against the rebuilt binary, so source and image agree.

EVIDENCE THAT THIS WAS THE CAUSE. The strict capture condition against the
unfixed ROM is the combination that produced the original failure, so the fix is
tested by the test that found it rather than by inspection.

title: Land the conformance ROM and harness, minus the slow-blit assertion
description:
Land the conformance ROM, the harness and the assembled image, with every
assertion except the slow-blit one.

WHAT LANDS: machines/tests/roms/williams_video.asm, the assembled
williams_video.bin, machines/tests/williams_video_timing_test.rs, and the design
doc docs/designs/williams-video-conformance.md with its status changed from
proposed to landed. All four already exist untracked in the working tree.

ALREADY MEASURED GREEN on joust and robotron, ROM-less, in 0.06s:

  the_conformance_program_runs_to_completion
  the_video_counter_steps_by_four_and_wraps_once_a_frame
  count240_raises_one_interrupt_a_frame_at_scanline_240
  va11_toggles_cb1_every_thirty_two_scanlines
  the_sc1_xors_four_into_the_blit_size
  a_mid_frame_palette_write_splits_the_picture_at_the_beam
  a_mid_frame_vram_write_only_affects_rows_the_beam_has_not_reached
  the_image_fills_the_program_rom_window

THE FALSIFICATION THAT MAKES THEM CHECKS. begin_scanline was temporarily changed
to also re-render every visible line at scanline 259, which is exactly the
"render the whole frame at end of frame" model the design says T6 and T7 must
reject. Under that mutation both picture tests failed and the six CPU-observable
tests still passed, which is the right pattern: the mutation is a rendering
change and only the rendering tests noticed. Reverting restored green. Anyone
revisiting whether these tests earn their keep should redo that mutation rather
than trust this paragraph.

WHAT IS HELD BACK. the_blitter_halts_the_cpu_for_the_cycles_it_charges asserts
both halves of T4 and the slow half fails against the current tree. Land the fast
assertion here and the slow one with its fix, in the issue that owns it, so the
fix and the test that found it arrive in one commit. Do not land the slow
assertion pinned to the wrong value; a test that asserts today's bug is worse
than no test.

VERIFY BEFORE CLOSING. cargo clippy with CI's exact flag set over the workspace
(the new test target is not in default-members), cargo fmt, and
cargo test --workspace. This suite needs no ROMs, so it also has to pass with
PHOSPHOR_ROMS unset, which is the whole point: CI has never once checked what a
machine draws.

ALSO FIX THE DOC. The line references in the design doc are stale by about
seventeen lines throughout (begin_scanline is at williams.rs:648 not 631,
step_cycle at 321 not 304, render_scanline at 600 not 583, reset at 767 not 750);
the ClockTree commits moved them. Its header still says the ROM has not been
assembled. Replace the derived-not-measured hedging on T1 to T3 with the values
that were actually measured.
close_reason: Landed as 580a949: ROM, 12 KB image, harness and the corrected design doc. Ten tests green on joust and robotron with no arcade ROMs, running in CI. Slow-blit assertion held back for itvk.4.

comments.author: pjl
comments.text:
Landed as 580a949. Ten tests, joust and robotron, no arcade ROMs, 0.07s, and it
runs in CI, which no video test in this tree has ever done.

Green: program completion, T1 counter survey, T2 count240, T3 VA11 rising and
falling, T4 fast, T5 SC1 XOR-4, T6 palette split, T7 the beam-relative VRAM
write, the image shape, and the source-to-binary drift guard.

WHAT CHANGED FROM THE PLAN.

The design called for collecting assertions the way golden_frame_test does, so
that "these three signals moved and these four did not" is the diagnosis. Ten
separate #[test] functions give that for free, since the runner reports each
independently, and each carries its derivation in its doc comment. No collector
was written. assert_completed runs first in every one of them, so a wedge fails
on the magic byte rather than as a dozen assertions about zero bytes.

The slow half of T4 is held back rather than landed failing. R_T4SLW is measured
by the ROM and marked #[allow(dead_code)] with the reason, so nothing asserts
the wrong value in either direction. It arrives with the fix in itvk.4.

THE DESIGN DOC IS CORRECTED, NOT JUST RESTAMPED. Three things were wrong or
missing in it, and the doc now says so rather than being quietly rewritten:

- Every williams.rs line reference was stale by about seventeen lines, moved by
  the ClockTree commits. All of them, and the ones in the references section,
  are re-pointed.
- It never stated that the blitter's width register counts COLUMNS and height
  counts SCANLINES. That is the fact a reader needs to check the screen fill:
  146 x 85 with DST_STRIDE_256 covers columns 3-148 of scanlines 0-84, not the
  transpose. Added as its own row in the board-facts table.
- It did not anticipate the phase 9/10 collision, which is now written up in the
  phase protocol section along with why WaitWrap alone is not enough.

It also gained the falsification record for T6 and T7, the asl toolchain and the
byte-identical port, and a risk entry for the guard that could not fail, which
future conformance ROMs inherit the trap of.

CLIPPY. Two lints in the file as originally drafted, both fixed: an unused
BusDebug import (debug_bus() hands back a trait object, so the trait does not
need importing) and needless parens on a range literal. CI's exact clippy line
and cargo fmt --check are clean over the workspace.

title: Slow blits cost one cycle per byte, not two
description:
A slow blit costs the CPU the same time as a fast one. Measured, not suspected.

MEASURED. The conformance ROM issues the identical 1024-byte blit twice, once
fast and once with CTRL_SLOW, and reads the video counter either side of each.
Both come back as a delta of 16 scanlines. The slow one should be 32.

  T4_FAST = $10 (1024 bytes x 1 cycle = 1024 cycles = 16 scanlines)  correct
  T4_SLOW = $10, expected $20 (2048 cycles = 32 scanlines)           wrong

Both blits start at a known mid-frame line so neither crosses the counter wrap,
where the u8 aliasing would corrupt the subtraction, and the measurement is a
counter delta rather than a cycle count, so a constant offset in the CPU's reset
sequence cancels.

THE CAUSE, READ FROM THE SOURCE RATHER THAN INFERRED. WilliamsBlitter::do_dma_cycle
returns the cycle cost of the byte it just moved, 1 fast and 2 slow
(core/src/device/williams_blitter.rs:291). The board throws it away:
machines/src/williams.rs:333 is a bare `blitter.do_dma_cycle(bus);` inside
step_cycle, which runs exactly one DMA cycle per CPU cycle. So CTRL_SLOW changes
nothing about wall time. The device is right, the board is right in isolation,
and the join is wrong: a seam bug that unit tests structurally cannot find, since
core/tests/williams_blitter_test.rs:62 accumulates the very return value the
board discards.

THE FIX, DECIDED. Charge the second cycle inside the device, so all blit timing
stays in williams_blitter.rs: do_dma_cycle becomes "consume one clock", moving a
byte only every other clock while CTRL_SLOW is set. The return value becomes
vestigial and core/tests/williams_blitter_test.rs changes with it. The blitter
gains a field for the half-cycle state, which has to go into its save-state
stream; check the round trip in machines/tests/save_state_tests.rs still passes.

The other option, considered and not taken, was a stall counter on
WilliamsBoard driven by the returned count. It keeps the device untouched but
puts blit timing in two places.

LAND THE ASSERTION WITH THE FIX. The harness test
the_blitter_halts_the_cpu_for_the_cycles_it_charges already carries the slow
assertion and already fails on it. It is held out of the landing issue precisely
so it arrives in the same commit as the fix.

THIS CHANGES BEHAVIOUR ON REAL GAMES, WHICH IS THE POINT AND ALSO THE RISK.
Slow is the RAM-to-RAM mode, so any game that blits from RAM has been running at
twice hardware speed. Measure how much before and after: count SLOW blits per
frame in the joust and robotron attract loops, and say in the commit what
fraction of blitter cycles they are. Expect the attract loop to shift phase and
the golden frames to move; that recapture is its own issue and this one is not
done until it is.
close_reason: Fixed device-side in 0e796ed: do_dma_cycle consumes one clock, a slow byte moving on the first and stalling the second. T4_SLOW goes $10 to $20. The return value stayed meaningful so the 43 device tests needed no change. Blitter save tag 1->2, SAVE_VERSION 5->6.

comments.author: pjl
comments.text:
Fixed in 0e796ed, device-side as decided.

MEASURED, before and after, on joust and robotron:

  T4_FAST $10 (16 scanlines)  correct throughout
  T4_SLOW $10 -> $20          derived $20 (1024 bytes x 2 cycles = 2048)

THE SHAPE OF THE FIX. do_dma_cycle consumes one CLOCK rather than one byte. A
fast blit moves a byte on every clock; a slow one moves a byte and then spends a
clock moving nothing, held together by a `stall` flag so the blit stays active
across it. The caller already holds the CPU halted while is_active(), so the
stall clock is what actually charges the second microsecond. All blit timing
stays in williams_blitter.rs.

THE RETURN VALUE DID NOT BECOME VESTIGIAL, which the issue expected it to. It
now means "clocks consumed by this call", which is 1 while active, so
core/tests/williams_blitter_test.rs needed no change at all: run_to_completion_clocks
still totals 2n for a slow blit and now does so for the right reason rather than
by accumulating a number nobody acted on. All 43 device tests pass untouched.
Only test_slow_mode_timing uses SLOW, and it uses that helper.

AN OPEN QUESTION, LABELLED IN THE SOURCE RATHER THAN DECIDED SILENTLY. Which of
a slow byte's two clocks moves the byte is not determined by anything available
here. The CPU is halted throughout and cannot observe the difference; only the
renderer could, and only within a single scanline. The byte moves on the first
clock so it is visible as early as the hardware could manage. A schematic would
settle it; nothing in this repository can.

SAVE STATE. The blitter's component tag goes 1 to 2 for the stall flag, and
SAVE_VERSION 5 to 6 with it so an old file is rejected clearly rather than at a
component boundary. A blit saved mid-transfer in slow mode reloads owing the
same clock it owed. save_state_tests and save_state_rom_test both pass.

WHAT IT COST ON REAL GAMES. Robotron and Sinistar draw a different attract frame
and were recaptured under itvk.5. Joust does not move at all, which is a free
measurement of the blast radius: its attract loop issues no slow blit in 1800
frames while the other two do. No instrumented count of slow blits per frame was
taken; the golden result answered the question the issue was asking well enough
to skip it, and that is a deliberate omission rather than an oversight.

title: ROM-gated re-run and Williams golden-frame recapture after the blitter fix
description:
Re-run the ROM-gated suites after the slow-blit fix, and recapture the Williams
golden frames if they move.

The slow-blit fix doubles how long the CPU is halted for every RAM-to-RAM blit.
That is a change to the main CPU's available cycles per frame on joust, robotron
and sinistar, so the attract loop can land in a different animation phase, at a
different level, or with a different RNG state. A golden-frame diff after this
change is expected and is not by itself evidence of a rendering regression.

RUN, INDIVIDUALLY, ABOUT ELEVEN MINUTES TOTAL:

  PHOSPHOR_ROMS=~/ws/mame-runtime/roms nix develop -c cargo test -p phosphor-harness --test golden_frame_test
  ... --test boot_check_test
  ... --test save_state_rom_test
  ... --test audio_sanity_test

boot_check_test is the one that would catch the fix wedging a game rather than
merely reshuffling its attract loop, and it is the more important of the four
here. save_state_rom_test covers the new blitter field surviving a round trip on
a booted machine. audio_sanity_test is included because the main CPU feeds sound
commands to the sound PIA and its cycle budget just changed.

IF THE GOLDEN FRAMES MOVE. Look at the images before recapturing. The failure
writes the actual frame to harness/tests/golden/actual/ and prints a
disasm imgdiff command. What you are looking for is a picture that is a
different moment of the same attract loop, not a picture that is drawn wrong:
wrong colours, missing sprites, torn rows or shifted geometry mean the fix broke
rendering and the recapture must not happen. Recapture with
PHOSPHOR_GOLDEN_UPDATE=1, review the resulting PNGs, and say in the commit what
changed in each of the three and why it is an attract-phase difference.

HAND THE IMAGES OVER BEFORE COMMITTING. This is judged by eye, so the diff is
not the artifact; the pictures are.
close_reason: Robotron and Sinistar recaptured in 0e796ed after review by image and by play; Joust unmoved. Attribution established with a control run on HEAD: the other seven failures are the in-flight vector work. boot_check and save_state_rom pass. audio_sanity_test deliberately not run.

comments.author: pjl
comments.text:

  joust      pass on HEAD, pass with the fix

  sinistar  2.86%. A different moment of the same text screen. Worth noting

title: Extend the conformance suite to Sinistar
description:
Extend the conformance suite to Sinistar, the third machine on WilliamsBoard.

The first pass covers joust and robotron and skips sinistar with a reason. Two
things differ and both are in the config, not the silicon:

- Memory map. WilliamsConfig::sinistar sets extra_sram_dxxx, which puts 4 KB of
  work RAM at $D000 and shrinks program ROM to 8 KB at $E000-$FFFF
  (machines/src/williams.rs:461-470). The image is 12 KB and links at $D000, so
  Sinistar needs a second link address and a second, smaller image. The harness
  already anticipates this with a load_addr-per-machine shape in the design doc.
- Blitter window clip. sinistar's blitter carries a clip at $7400 and $C900 bit 2
  enables it (williams.rs:1103). The ROM already writes 0 to $C900 at startup
  for exactly this reason, and its scratch at $9800-$A3FF sits above $7400, so a
  stray enable would make T4 and T5 fail confusingly rather than obviously.
  Worth asserting the clip is off rather than trusting the startup write.

The $D000 SRAM is a bonus: it is a blit destination that is not video RAM, which
is a case the joust and robotron runs never exercise.

This is the least load-bearing part of the epic. It broadens coverage of a board
whose behaviour is already pinned by two machines; it does not test anything new
about the model. Do it after the instrument and the fix have landed, or not at
all if effort is better spent on the second board family.
close_reason: Sinistar covered in 4975b57 from a second link address built out of the same source (asl -D ROMBASE=0xE000). The real obstacle was its 270-degree cabinet rotation, not the memory map; the harness now reads in raster coordinates. Ten tests green on all three Williams machines. The $D000 SRAM as a non-VRAM blit target is deliberately not covered.

comments.author: pjl
comments.text:
Done in 4975b57. All three machines on WilliamsBoard are covered, ten tests, no
arcade ROMs, 0.12s.

THE LINK ADDRESS WAS THE EASY HALF. Sinistar's 8 KB at $E000 comes from the same
source via `asl -D ROMBASE=0xE000`, guarded by `ifndef` so the default stays
$D000. Everything the program touches other than its own code is in video RAM
below $C000, so relocation is the whole difference. The drift guard rebuilds and
compares both images; a source edit breaking only one link address is exactly
what a single-image guard would miss.

THE CABINET WAS THE HARD HALF, AND THIS ISSUE DID NOT ANTICIPATE IT.
SinistarSystem::render_frame rotates the board's landscape raster 270 degrees
into a 240x292 portrait buffer (sinistar.rs:442). Every coordinate in this suite
is a raster coordinate, so reading the rendered frame directly asked for row 0
and got row 239. Both picture tests failed.

HOW IT WAS LOCALISED, because the failure looked like a timing bug at first.
The two failures were in OPPOSITE directions: T6 saw green where it wanted red at
the top, T7 saw red where it wanted green near the bottom. A capture taken from
the wrong frame moves both the same way, so that was ruled out by the shape of
the failure rather than by trying fixes. A probe then confirmed all three
machines publish each phase on the identical frame (7 after frame 13, 8 after 14,
9 after 15), which closed the question for good. Only then did the rotation get
looked for, and it was one grep.

The harness undoes the rotation on read via Shot::raster, so assertions stay in
raster coordinates and orientation remains a separate concern with its own tests.
The handling is exercised rather than asserted: it is precisely what failed
before it existed.

THE WINDOW CLIP was the risk this issue named, and it was a non-event. $C900 bit
2 gates it and the program already clears $C900 at startup along with the ROM
bank. T4 and T5 passing on Sinistar is what says the blitter ran unclipped; had
the clip been enabled, the scratch at $9800-$A3FF sits above the $7400 clip and
both would have failed.

NOT DONE, deliberately: the $D000 SRAM as a blit destination that is not video
RAM. It is the one thing Sinistar can exercise that Joust and Robotron cannot,
and it needs a new phase in the ROM rather than a relocation of the existing one.
Recorded in the design doc rather than left implied.

title: Do Castle: the main Z80 is cloned every T-state for the WAIT rewind
description:
docastle::step_main takes a full Z80 snapshot (main.clone()) before every main-CPU T-state, so the latch-read rewind can undo it:

    let snapshot = main.clone();
    main.execute_cycle(board, BusMaster::Cpu(0));
    if board.main_retry { *main = snapshot; ... }

That is a ~100-byte struct copy on each of ~66,000 cycles per frame, and the rewind it exists for fires only on the handful of cycles that hit the shared latch window.

Found while converting the board to concrete bus dispatch (f38e13a). The conversion measured only -4.1% (docastle) / -3.3% (dorunrun) against 12-27% on comparable Z80 boards, because most of a Do Castle frame is not bus dispatch: this clone plus four SN76489A PSGs serviced every cycle.

Options worth measuring:
- Snapshot lazily: only clone when the cycle is about to touch the latch window. The board knows the window (MAIN_LATCH_BASE..+LATCH_WINDOW_LEN) but not the address before the CPU issues it, so this may need the CPU to expose 'about to read address X' or the board to set a flag from the read itself and rewind from a cheaper record.
- Snapshot only the fields the rewind restores, if that is a strict subset.
- Have the Z80 support an explicit 'retry this T-state' rather than a whole-state rollback.

Any change here must keep the LDIR handshake test passing (main_latch_read_stalls_then_samples_the_sub_cpu_value and the nine-byte boot handshake), and be measured with phosphor-bench on docastle.

title: Implement Xevious on the Namco Galaga platform
description:
Add Xevious (Namco, 1983) as a new game on the shared NamcoGalagaBoard (namco_galaga.rs), reusing the 3x Z80 + WSG + 06XX infrastructure alongside Galaga and Dig Dug.

Xevious differs from Galaga/Dig Dug in three confirmed ways:
1. Custom chips: drops the 53XX, adds the 50XX (MB8842 protection MCU, boot-critical) and 54XX (MB8844 explosion-sound MCU). DIPs are read directly at 0x6800 (bosco_dsw_r), not via a custom chip.
2. Three graphics layers: scrolling background tilemap + foreground text tilemap + 3bpp 16x16 sprites, with independent per-layer X/Y scroll (0xD000 latch).
3. Background tile data lives in ROM, addressed via a hardware lookup (xevious_bb_r/xevious_bs_w at 0xF000, 'schematic 9B').

De-risker: xevious.zip ships the 50xx/51xx/54xx MCU dumps, and the repo already has an mb88xx core + LLE example (namco51_lle.rs), so the 50XX protection can be done LLE with no reverse-engineering.

Delivery: staged milestones (M1 boot, M2 video, M3 input/sound/tests). 54XX explosion sound stubbed silent initially; WSG melodic/effect sound works from M1.

Full design: ~/.claude/plans/plan-to-implement-xevious-sleepy-teacup.md
close_reason: Xevious ships on the shared Namco Galaga board across all three milestones: M1 board plumbing + boot (50XX protection cleared — implemented as a behavioural HLE rather than the originally-scoped MB8842 LLE, since the LLE could not be synced to the 06XX handshake; see commit eeeea52), M2 three-layer scrolling video + 3bpp sprites + F000 ROM-lookup background, M3 input/DIPs/WSG sound/tests/docs. WSG melodic+effect audio works and is verified against the real ROM; the 54XX explosion channel is stubbed silent with a documented seam for a future discrete network + LLE. All descendant issues closed.

Xevious boots on the shared NamcoGalagaBoard: 3x Z80 run, the power-on RAM test passes, the 50XX protection check passes, DIP reads work, the sub/sound CPUs are released and stay running, and the main VBLANK IRQ stays enabled -- the game settles into a stable attract loop (headless boot-check, video intentionally stubbed until M2). Delivered across .1.1 (50XX device), .1.2 (06XX dispatch), .1.3 (wrapper/Bus/map), .1.4 (run_frame/interrupts), plus two board-accuracy fixes found via MAME bus-diff: sound-CPU NMI-on-reset race (.1.5) and the 50XX (.1.6). Wire ports per MAME namco50.cpp: K=cmd>>4, R0=cmd&0x0F, R2=rw&1, O port -> answer latch; chip_select asserts MCU IRQ; read() returns O latch; write(cmd) latches command. Device impl + save-state; register in core/src/device/mod.rs. Confirm the mb88xx Variant for a 2048B ROM (core enumerates MB8841 at 2048B). Add unit tests for the protection command/answer.

description: MachineCore::run_frame mirroring Galaga's per-scanline loop: VBLANK IRQ to main+sub gated by misclatch Q0/Q1, sound NMI gated by Q2, 06XX NMI timer for main CPU. Video stub (solid fill) for this milestone. machine_core_metadata!("xevious", namco_galaga::TIMING) — timing is identical to Galaga (288x224, 264 scanlines).
